John Smedley bolsters leadership team with three new hires
sub_title: Heritage British knitwear brand John Smedley has shaken up its leadership team with three new hires and two expanded executive roles. Posting on LinkedIn
article_content: Heritage British knitwear brand John Smedley has shaken up its leadership team with three new hires and two expanded executive roles. Posting on LinkedIn on Friday, John Smedley Chief Executive Officer Jess McGuire-Dudley welcomed “a new chapter” for the brand. Stuart Pannell has joined as Chief Financial Officer from IDESO Group (in the manufacturing industry), Brian Lancaster has come in as Chief Operating Officer from Eviosys (also in the manufacturing industry and now Sonoco Ltd), and Nick Watt, who was previously in a consultancy role, has been appointed People Director. McGuire-Dudley said: “Today marks an important milestone in the evolution of John Smedley. "As we continue to build on more than 240 years of British manufacturing excellence, I am delighted to announce the appointment of a strengthened executive leadership team that combines deep industry expertise, operational excellence, and a shared commitment to securing the long-term future of our business. "I am also pleased to welcome back Bryan Jackson CBE as Senior Independent Director, bringing a wealth of board-level experience and strategic insight." McGuire-Dudley continued: "Together, this C-suite brings together expertise across finance, operations, product, people, sustainability and governance, creating a leadership team with the capability to guide John Smedley through its next phase of growth and transformation. “I would also like to recognise the continued stewardship of Ian Maclean MBE, our Executive Chairman, and Robert Marsden Smedley, Non-Executive Director, both representatives of the eighth generation of the John Smedley family. Their commitment to preserving the values, craftsmanship and heritage of our business while embracing the future remains central to everything we do. "This is an exciting moment for our company. We have ambitious plans to strengthen our position as one of Britain’s most respected luxury manufacturing brands, investing in our people, our products, our sustainability agenda and our global partnerships. "I’m incredibly proud to lead this exceptional team as we write the next chapter of the John Smedley story." In April, John Smedley unveiled a redesigned website “reflecting the growth of the brand’s direct-to-consumer business and its journey of digital transformation”. It came at the same time that John Smedley was granted a second Royal Warrant for exceptional knitwear and commitment to craftsmanship, quality and sustainability, the first awarded by Queen Camilla.

article_title: SKIMS opens first UK flagship on London’s Regent Street
sub_title: SKIMS has officially opened its first standalone UK store on London's Regent Street, marking a significant step in the brand's international retail expansion.
article_content: SKIMS has opened its first standalone UK flagship store on London's Regent Street, marking a significant step in the brand's international expansion. The 12,000 sq ft flagship occupies the former Ted Baker site at 245-247 Regent Street, following the announcement last year that the shapewear and lifestyle brand had signed a 10-year lease with The Crown Estate. The store offers SKIMS' full product range, including shapewear, underwear, loungewear, menswear and accessories, alongside seasonal collections and pieces from the NikeSKIMS collaboration. Designed by architect Rafael de Cárdenas, the space features open-plan interiors, sculptural displays and a large sculpture by artist Vanessa Beecroft. The opening marks SKIMS' first permanent retail store in the UK, where the brand has previously been available through wholesale partners including Selfridges, Harrods and END. Jens Grede, co-founder and CEO of SKIMS, said: “Our flagship stores play an important role in how customers experience SKIMS beyond the product.” “Opening on Regent Street is a significant milestone for the brand and reflects our continued investment in creating immersive retail destinations in the world’s leading shopping cities.” Kim Kardashian, co-founder and Chief Creative Officer, added: "London has always been one of the most inspiring fashion cities in the world to me, so opening our first UK flagship on Regent Street feels especially exciting.” The London launch follows a period of rapid growth for the business. In late 2025, SKIMS secured a $225 million funding round that valued the company at $5 billion , fuelling further investment in physical retail as well as apparel and the NikeSKIMS partnership. The Regent Street flagship is one of a series of international openings, with a new flagship at Dubai Mall and stores also planned for Delhi and Mumbai. Founded by Kim Kardashian, Jens Grede and Emma Grede in 2019, SKIMS began as a direct-to-consumer shapewear brand before expanding into underwear, swimwear, loungewear and menswear. The Regent Street opening reflects the brand's continued investment in physical retail, as SKIMS builds a global network of flagship stores to complement its online business and wholesale partnerships.

article_title: Harvey Nichols bidders asked to commit up to £60 million for turnaround
sub_title: Bidders for Harvey Nichols have been asked to commit between £50 million and £60 million over the medium term to fund the luxury department store group’s transformation plan.
article_content: Bidders for Harvey Nichols have been asked to commit between £50 million and £60 million over the medium term to fund the luxury department store's transformation plan, Sky News reported. The proposed investment, which would be separate from the acquisition price, would support a refurbishment of the Edinburgh store, international expansion, digital development and the management team’s business plan. Potential bidders currently include Frasers Group and Modella Capital, the owner of Hobbycraft and TGJones, as well as Dubai-based Chalhoub Group and India’s Reliance Retail. Indicative offers have reportedly been received from UK bidders, while international bidders are working to a different timetable. Sir Dickson Poon’s family, which owns Harvey Nichols, has appointed FTI Consulting to advise on the sale and regional advisers to attract interest from potential Gulf-based buyers. NEXT emerged as a potential bidder earlier in July , with sources saying the retailer intended to examine the business closely. It remains unclear whether NEXT would retain Harvey Nichols’ regional store network or focus on the brand and its intellectual property. Frasers Group then entered the process two weeks ago, despite concerns among some Harvey Nichols suppliers about its potential ownership. Frasers owns Sports Direct, Flannels and House of Fraser. A Harvey Nichols executive told suppliers at the time that the company was “obliged to allow Frasers Group to participate in the process alongside the other interested parties”. The memo said its admission was intended to ensure a competitive process and find the right partner for the retailer’s next phase. Harvey Nichols stocks hundreds of luxury labels. Supplier concerns have focused on whether a new owner would maintain its market positioning and existing brand relationships. The requested funding would extend a three-year transformation programme led by Chief Executive Julia Goddard, who joined Harvey Nichols in June 2024. The strategy has refocused the business on fashion, beauty and hospitality while reducing non-core operations. The department store has also continued to reshape its commercial leadership, including the promotion of Shaun Donnelly to Buying Director for Non-Apparel and Menswear. The retailer has already invested in its Knightsbridge flagship, including a fourth-floor wellness destination and a redesigned ground floor focused on jewellery , lifestyle products and flexible brand spaces. Its wider retail revival plan has also included digital investment and the addition of new fashion brands. For the year to 31 March 2024, Harvey Nichols posted revenue of £204.8 million, a 5% decline, while pre-tax losses increased to £34 million. That marked the group’s fifth consecutive annual loss. The business has about 1,200 employees in the UK and runs seven stores in the UK and Ireland, with large-format sites in London, Edinburgh, Birmingham, Leeds and Manchester, plus smaller-format branches in Bristol and Dublin. Internationally, it operates six large-format stores in Riyadh, Doha, Dubai, Hong Kong and Kuwait. The softer luxury goods market, together with the ending of VAT-free shopping for tourists after Brexit, has been pointed to as a major reason for the prolonged losses. Sir Dickson’s Dickson Concepts International acquired Harvey Nichols from Burton Group for £53 million in 1991. The retailer now operates seven stores across the UK and Ireland alongside an international network in the Middle East and Asia.

article_title: Luxury consumers see fur and exotic skins as 'less luxurious', report finds
sub_title: Luxury consumers increasingly view fashion brands using fur and wild animal skins as less luxurious, according to new research from Collective Fashion Justice (CFJ), highlighting changing attitudes towards traditional luxury materials.
article_content: Luxury consumers increasingly view fashion brands using fur and wild animal skins as less luxurious, according to new research from Collective Fashion Justice (CFJ), highlighting changing attitudes towards traditional luxury materials. The report, based on interviews with 61 high net worth and ultra-high net worth consumers across London, Paris and New York, found that 95% of respondents believe the use of fur and wild animal skins makes luxury brands appear less prestigious. Instead, many associated modern luxury with innovation, ethics and sustainability. Among those surveyed, 80% said they would be more likely to purchase wildlife-derived products if they believed they benefited conservation, while 85% said they would only consider buying them if animal welfare standards could be assured. However, almost half (48%) admitted they were unaware of the welfare issues associated with the wildlife skin trade. Emma Håkansson, founder and Director of Collective Fashion Justice, said: “It’s clear that valuable luxury consumers view the use of wild animal materials in a way that is damaging to overall brand perception. “Forward-thinking brands have already moved away from fur and wildlife derived materials. We need to see the whole of the fashion industry catching up and investing in next-generation bio-materials.” The findings come as more luxury organisations move away from animal-derived materials. Earlier this year, the Camera Nazionale della Moda Italiana announced that Milan Fashion Week would no longer promote fur across its official events or social media channels, joining fashion weeks in London, New York, Copenhagen and Berlin adopting fur-free policies. The report also found respondents were receptive to next-generation materials, provided they retained the craftsmanship, quality and exclusivity associated with luxury fashion. According to the research, consumers were more interested in rarity, innovation and design than whether a product was made from wild animal materials. Collective Fashion Justice argues that this presents an opportunity for luxury brands to invest further in alternative materials while maintaining premium positioning. The report also notes that increased regulation of the wildlife trade and changing consumer expectations could add legal and commercial risks for brands continuing to use exotic skins and fur.

article_title: Editors' Top Reads: News from Reformation, Frasers, Scoop and more...
sub_title: Here are some of this week’s news and features highlights handpicked by TheIndustry.fashion team.
article_content: Here are some of this week’s news and features highlights handpicked by TheIndustry.fashion team. Frasers Group is continuing to push forward with its takeover plans for both German luxury brand Hugo Boss and Australia-based Accent Group. On Tuesday, Frasers Group increased its stake in Hugo Boss to 30.28% , crossing Germany’s mandatory bid threshold, meaning that it is now obligated to make a takeover offer. Frasers Group had previously doubled down on its €38-per-share offer and said that it would not increase the price. Hugo Boss' board responded with a recommendation for shareholders to reject Frasers takeover offer, which they called "inadequate". Just because the formal process for a takeover offer has now been triggered, it does not mean that the board will change its mind and accept the offer. Interestingly, Frasers has been in a similar position before. In 2024, the group launched a takeover bid for British luxury brand Mulberry, in which it held around a 37% stake. Yet Mulberry's biggest shareholder, Challice, which owned a 56.4% stake, opposed Frasers' bid and the offer did not go through. So, while Frasers remains a major stakeholder within Mulberry, it does not control the business. Just two days later, Frasers announced an extension for its £166 million takeover offer for Australian footwear and lifestyle retailer Accent Group, without, however, changing any other of its terms, including its initial A$0.65-a-share bid. So, Frasers again doubled down on its initial offer price, even though Accent’s Independent Board Committee had previously recommended that shareholders reject the bid, which it described as “opportunistic and materially inadequate”. The offer had initially been due to close on 30 July, but Accent shareholders now have until the close of ASX (Australian Securities Exchange) trading on 30 September to sell into the offer. I, for one, am very interested to see how both of these offers will play out. Camilla Rydzek, Senior News & Features Writer. Well, it's a start and it's very early days. Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who took office on Monday, has shown he means business when he pledged business rates reform. For too long, retailers have borne an unfair burden when it comes to this tax and it needs to be addressed. The first beneficiaries of Burnham's reforms will be pubs and social clubs . Night clubs are not included, and nor are, more mysteriously, restaurants. As for bars, well, that apparently is a grey area and it may come down to local authorities to decide who should ultimately benefit from the 20% cut. Let's start by being positive because apparently more reforms are in the pipeline and it is to be hoped retail will be included in some form (particularly independent retailers) and anything that helps to keep life on our high streets has to be a good thing. Burnham has clearly chosen to go early with the pubs news since it fits with his personal branding, which centres on supporting "working class values" (though it sits awkwardly to suggest pubs are the preserve of the working class and that the working class will be brought onside thanks to tax relief for pubs) and also because the pub trade has a very high-profile lobbying campaign to push its interests to the top of the Government agenda. Many high profile people got behind the pub industry, including, curiously, former Chancellor Rachel Reeves (who seemed to be able to gloss over the fact that her employer's NI hikes were a major contributing factor to the sector's distress). Still, good for the pub trade, let's hope the retail industry can keep the pressure on and deliver a similar result. Lauretta Roberts, Co-founder, CEO and Editor-in-Chief. I have to say there always seems to be a feel-good factor among exhibitors at Scoop , and this week’s circus-themed edition was no different. It also always seems to offer up a lot of newness, testament to the research and curation skills of Scoop’s founder and Managing Director, Karen Radley, who this time around had partnered with the Italian Trade Agency (ITA) to bring an exclusive collective of 32 contemporary Italian designers to the show, many of which were making their debut. What’s also great is the people you meet and the stories behind the brands. Some are really fascinating, such as Eva Panagiotopoulou, founder and Creative Director of Come What May from Athens in Greece. Having been in the business for almost 30 years in various roles, the past 10 of which as a designer for other brands, this was the first outing for her very own brand – conceived when she fell in love with some very unique hand-block printed fabrics that she came across. Then there’s the story of Labdip, another first time showing at Scoop, with Director General Léa Wu explaining how her father had been a denim manufacturer, with his own factory, in Shanghai, China, specialising in washes and fits. Now retired, he passed on his knowledge and skill set to his daughter and son, and it was great to talk denim at a show such as Scoop, perhaps not usually associated with it. Another interesting one, and first-time exhibitor, was Valentina Urso, Creative Director of Opalina – one of the 32 Italian brands falling under the ITA partnership umbrella . Urso had previously worked for over 10 years behind the scenes in production for other brands. She then discovered an old factory originally established in 1954 in Puglia. She was fascinated by the women that worked in the factory, and thrilled to find the old ways of making still intact, so three year ago she set about launching her own brand specialising in modern interpretations of women’s shirts, with hand crafted details such as ruffle fronts, embroidery, pleating on the shoulder and puff sleeves. Another great find and confirmation that any womenswear buyer worth their salt should always aim to attend Scoop. It really is quite inspiring. Tom Bottomley, Contributing Editor. I really enjoyed writing a ‘Secret Shopper’ as it was my first feature for TheIndustry.fashion. It gave me the opportunity to experience a store not just as a shopper, but from a retail perspective, paying attention to how every part of the customer journey is designed to shape the shopping experience and influence purchasing decisions. What stood out to me most was Reformation's touchscreen fitting rooms. Being able to request different sizes and styles without leaving the changing room was genuinely useful, but I could also see how the technology created new challenges and contributed to longer waiting times. As more retailers look to incorporate digital convenience and increasingly AI into physical shopping, it will be interesting to see whether concepts like this become more common on the high street and, ultimately, which ones prove to be worthwhile investments. Read the full feature here . Catherine Rowe-Kosary, Junior News Writer.

article_title: Frasers Group acquires Glasgow-based Greaves Sports
sub_title: Frasers Group has acquired the intellectual property of Glasgow retailer Greaves Sports, with its Gordon Street shop and online store set to continue under the established name.
article_content: Frasers Group has acquired the intellectual property of Glasgow retailer Greaves Sports, with its Gordon Street shop and online store set to continue under the established name. No financial terms of the deal have been shared, although it was specified to be an IP transaction. In a statement, Greaves Sports reassured customers that its retail outlets would continue with the "same levels of service and expertise we’ve strived to provide for nearly 100 years". Its six-storey, 30,000 square feet flagship sports store is located at 23 Gordon Street in Glasgow. The family-run business has operated in Glasgow since 1930 and is currently run by Sandy Greaves and his sister Anne Leslie. Documents filed with Companies House show that Greaves changed its name to Clydesdale Sports Retail Limited in June. The deal brings another specialist name into Frasers Group’s portfolio, which includes Sports Direct, Flannels, Game, Evans Cycles and USC. The group also has Scottish retail property interests, including the Braehead Shopping Centre near Glasgow Airport and the Overgate Centre in Dundee. Frasers Group acquired House of Fraser in 2018 and holds the freehold to the building housing its department store on Buchanan Street in Glasgow. The group has also invested in sports, premium fashion and retail property. This builds on Frasers' recent acquisitions spree. In June 2026, the group put forward an unsolicited bid for German luxury brand Hugo Boss . This week, it then increased its holding in the company to 30.28% . Frasers followed up its initial bid for Hugo Boss with another takeover offer for Australia’s Accent Group for £166 million. In the past 18 months alone, Frasers has acquired a majority stake in Italian multi-sport retailer Maxi Sport , taken control of Norwegian sporting goods chain XXL, and added multiple UK designer outlets and shopping centres to its property portfolio. Yet, Hugo Boss would be the most prominent brand asset in Frasers' empire, which also includes Jack Wills and Gieves & Hawkes. As reported when the bid was announced, it would represent a major step in Frasers' "Elevation Strategy" of moving beyond its Sports Direct roots toward premium retail.

article_title: Trump imposes new 10% tariff on most UK imports
sub_title: The US has imposed a new 10% tariff on most UK goods, replacing a temporary levy at the same rate as Donald Trump continues his trade strategy under a different legal mechanism.
article_content: The US has imposed a new 10% tariff on most UK goods, replacing a temporary levy at the same rate, as Donald Trump continues his trade strategy under a different legal mechanism. The measure took effect on Friday morning and covers 60 trading partners, accounting for 99.4% of US imports. Rates range from 10% to 12.5%, with the UK placed in the lower band. For British fashion and retail businesses exporting goods covered by the US tariffs, the cost stays the same for now, as the previously set temporary global tariff rate remains in place. Tariffs are paid by importers, although those costs can be passed through supply chains and eventually reach consumers. The duties exclude goods already covered by Section 232 national-security tariffs, including automobiles, steel, aluminium and copper, alongside categories such as oil and gas, aircraft parts, critical minerals and certain food products. Shipments loaded before the measure took effect also receive a short exemption, provided they enter the US before 12.01am Eastern Time on 28 July. The UK government said its agreement with Washington remained in force and that the announcement produced “no negative change to the tariff rate facing UK businesses”, a UK government spokesperson told Reuters. However, the British Chambers of Commerce said the UK had lost a comparative advantage over the European Union. William Bain, the organisation’s head of trade policy, said the EU’s arrangement was all-inclusive, while the UK’s 10% universal tariff could apply alongside duties on individual products. “So there will be some concerns in the business community this morning about what the UK needs to do to get the same treatment the European Union has got here,” Bain told the BBC. The Trump administration imposed the tariffs under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 following investigations into trading partners’ controls on goods made with forced labour. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told the BBC that the tariffs would "begin to correct what is both a human rights abuse and a distortive trade practice, to improve the welfare of workers everywhere". The new legal basis follows a February 2026 Supreme Court ruling that struck down many of Trump’s earlier global tariffs imposed under emergency powers. The administration subsequently introduced a temporary 10% surcharge, limited to 150 days, which expired as the latest duties took effect. Trade experts have questioned whether Section 301 authorises tariffs on this scale, raising the prospect of another legal challenge. The administration is also investigating 16 countries over alleged manufacturing overcapacity, which could lead to further duties.

article_title: The Team
Scoop could expand Italian brands for AW27 show following fruitful debut ITA partnership
sub_title: This week’s edition of Scoop, held at Olympia National in London from 19-21 July, included the show’s debut partnership with the Italian Trade Agency (ITA).
article_content: This week’s edition of Scoop, held at Olympia National in London from 19-21 July, included the show’s debut partnership with the Italian Trade Agency (ITA). The collaboration saw an exclusive collective of 32 contemporary Italian designers make their debut at Scoop, spanning womenswear, knitwear, accessories and lifestyle collections. With the majority of the brands not yet having any existing UK distribution, it gave a rare opportunity for buyers to discover a new wave of ‘Made in Italy’ creativity and, deemed to be a success, it could see other Italian brands being added to Scoop’s roster for the next show for AW27, taking place at the same venue from 7-9 February 2027. Giving their insights into the collaboration, ITA Director Giovanni Sacchi, and Scoop’s founder and Managing Director Karen Radley, took time out for an exclusive Q&A with TheIndustry.fashion. Giovanni Saachi (GS): The partnership between the Italian Trade Agency and Scoop was born from a shared ambition to strengthen the presence of Italian fashion brands in the UK market. Our London office has closely followed Scoop’s growth over the years, recognising its strong reputation and its perfect alignment with the profile of many Italian contemporary brands. Combined with the increasing interest from Italian companies in the UK and Italy’s strategic focus on boosting exports, this created the ideal opportunity to re-establish an official Italian presence at the show after several years. The strong response from Italian brands confirmed that this was the right moment to build a strategic collaboration. Karen Radley (KR): For me, the partnership came from a shared belief in what Scoop represents. I've always been incredibly selective about the designers we bring to the show because our buyers trust us to introduce them to collections they may not discover elsewhere. When I began working with the Italian Trade Agency, it quickly became clear that we shared the same philosophy. Together, we spent months personally selecting every designer to ensure they reflected the quality, creativity and contemporary positioning that Scoop is known for. Rather than simply creating an Italian pavilion, we wanted to present the designers and their collections within their brand adjacencies. GS: This partnership is particularly beneficial for Italian brands because, as a public institution, ITA provides significant support to reduce the barriers that companies often face when approaching a new market. ITA covers a large part of the costs related to the participation of Italian companies within the collective presence at the event and, most importantly, promotes their involvement through targeted activities designed not only to create awareness around their participation but also to attract the right buyers and industry professionals. Our presence and support have undoubtedly encouraged many companies that, on their own, may not have been able to sustain the costs of exhibiting in London, to recognise that this was the right moment to explore the UK market. Among the 32 participating companies, many are joining Scoop for the first time, while others are returning after several years, and some have confirmed their participation as part of a structured programme carefully developed and managed by the ITA London office. KR: For our buyers, the partnership creates something genuinely special. Instead of having to search across multiple events or showrooms, they can discover an exceptional edit of contemporary Italian designers, all carefully selected to complement the wider Scoop curation. Every collection has been chosen because it offers something distinctive while remaining commercially relevant for premium retailers. It gives buyers confidence that the time they spend at Scoop will be rewarded with new discoveries and meaningful business opportunities. GS: Brexit was certainly a significant turning point that, together with other external factors, has influenced the UK economy in recent years. Five years ago, following the Italian Government’s guidance, our London office established a dedicated Brexit Desk to support Italian companies in understanding the new regulations and adapting to the changes introduced. After an initial period of adjustment, the situation has now largely stabilised. Most Italian companies are already strongly export oriented, and many have experience trading outside the EU, meaning they are familiar with the procedures and costs involved in international business. While Brexit introduced new challenges, companies have progressively adapted their processes and today exporting to the UK has become more structured and predictable. The importance of the UK market remains clear: in 2025, the UK continues to be the 7th largest destination market for Italian clothing exports, after France, the USA, Germany, China, Spain and Switzerland, and before Japan. It also ranks among the top markets for Italian footwear and leather goods, confirming its strategic relevance for Italian brands. Image by FEEL O GS: We have brought a total of 32 Italian brands to Scoop this season through the Italian Trade Agency’s national collective. In addition to these, several other Italian brands are exhibiting independently. The vast majority of the Italian presence at the show is therefore supported by ITA. It is still too early to measure the commercial results, and we will assess the companies' feedback once the event has concluded. However, bringing such a strong national delegation has certainly generated interest and attracted considerable attention within the industry. Combined with Scoop's growing reputation, this enthusiasm gives us every reason to be optimistic about the success of this edition and the potential for future collaborations. KR: Welcoming 32 designers through our partnership with the Italian Trade Agency is a real milestone for Scoop and reflects the growing international confidence in the show. It's also important to remember that these designers sit alongside many other established Italian collections and agents exhibiting independently, making this one of the strongest Italian representations we've ever hosted. The response from buyers throughout the show has been incredibly encouraging, with the Italian designers attracting strong interest from both long-standing retailers and those looking to discover something new. GS: Absolutely. As the Italian Trade Agency, our mission is to promote genuine Made in Italy products around the world, and this is much more than a marketing slogan. The companies we support must meet strict eligibility requirements, including having their production in Italy. This ensures not only the authenticity of the products but also guarantees that the businesses we promote truly represent Italian manufacturing and craftsmanship. The UK remains one of the world's most influential fashion markets and a key destination for Italian exports. British consumers place great value on quality, craftsmanship, authenticity and creativity - qualities that are synonymous with Made in Italy. The premium consumer is also increasingly focused on sustainability and transparency, with more than 60% of UK consumers willing to pay more for products with transparent supply chains. That’s an area in which many Italian companies have invested significantly. GS: It is still too early to make a proper assessment of which brands have received the strongest reaction from UK buyers. Furthermore, as a public institution, we believe it is important to give equal visibility and support to all the companies within our collective, so highlighting one brand over another would not be appropriate. GS: What we can say is that some of the participating brands already have an established presence in the UK and are currently selling through selected retailers or online platforms. However, the majority of the companies are approaching the British market for the first time and see Scoop as an important opportunity to introduce their collections, meet potential partners and identify the right commercial opportunities. Some brands already have strong international recognition, while many others are small and medium-sized designer companies that are highly appreciated within their regions or specialist sectors. That’s a distinctive feature of the Italian fashion industry, where craftsmanship, creativity and niche expertise play a central role. GS: Once we have collected and analysed the feedback from the participating companies, we will have a clearer understanding of where to focus our efforts and how to further develop the initiative. In coordination with our headquarters, we will evaluate the best possible approach for future editions. Our ambition is always to improve and build on previous experiences. If all the right conditions continue to align, we are confident that we will be able to replicate and potentially further strengthen our presence at future editions of Scoop. KR: From Scoop's perspective, this has been an incredibly exciting collaboration. The response from both buyers and designers has reinforced what we hoped to achieve, creating an inspiring destination for contemporary Italian fashion within the wider Scoop edit. We see this as the beginning of a long-term relationship and would love to continue building on it in future seasons, bringing even more exceptional Italian designers to the UK market while maintaining the careful curation that defines Scoop.

article_title: Deckers sales rise as HOKA and international markets drive growth
sub_title: Deckers Brands, the US footwear group behind HOKA, UGG and Teva, reported net sales of $1.020 billion (£765 million) for the three months ended 30 June 2026, making it Deckers' first first-quarter result above $1 billion (£750 million).
article_content: Deckers Brands, the US footwear group behind HOKA, UGG and Teva, reported net sales of $1.020 billion (£765 million) for the three months ended 30 June 2026, an increase of 5.7%, with performance driven by HOKA and international sales growth. Deckers’ first-quarter performance was led by HOKA, which generated about 69% of group revenue. Sales increased 7.7% from $653.1 million (£489.8 million) to $703.5 million (£527.6 million). UGG remained the second-largest brand, growing 4.9% from $265.1 million (£198.8 million) to $278 million (£208.5 million). Revenue from other brands, including footwear brand Teva, declined 18.1% to $37.9 million (£28.4 million). Deckers said this reflected, in part, the impact of phasing out Koolaburra’s standalone operations. International sales rose 8.4% to $502.1 million (£376.6 million), accounting for nearly half of group sales. The company did not break down the performance of the UK market. Domestic sales were also up 3.2% to $517.4 million (£388.1 million). During the quarter, HOKA opened its first UK outlet pop-up at Gunwharf Quays in Portsmouth , offering footwear and apparel at discounts of at least 30% off full retail prices. Direct-to-consumer revenue rose 13% to $352.8 million (£264.6 million), with comparable DTC sales up 6.8%. Wholesale remained the larger channel at $666.7 million (£500.0 million), representing an increase of 2.2%. Although gross margin improved from 55.8% to 56.4%, selling, general and administrative expenses increased from $372.6 million (£279.5 million) to $419.9 million (£314.9 million). Operating income consequently fell 6% to $155.3 million (£116.5 million), while net income declined to $130 million (£97.5 million) from $139.2 million (£104.4 million). President and CEO Stefano Caroti said: “Deckers delivered a solid start to the fiscal year, surpassing $1 billion of first quarter revenue for the first time.” Deckers maintained its fiscal 2027 sales guidance of $5.86 billion (£4.40 billion) to $5.91 billion (£4.43 billion). The company expects low-double-digit growth from HOKA and mid-single-digit growth from UGG.

Heatwave and online shopping rebound delivers boost to June retail spending
sub_title: Hot weather boosting clothes and air conditioning purchases and summer discounting helped lift UK retail sales last month, official figures show.
article_content: Hot weather boosting clothes and air conditioning purchases and summer discounting helped lift UK retail sales last month, official figures show. Online shopping has also rebounded to a five-year high, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS). The ONS said the total volume of retail sales, which measures the quantity bought, increased by 1% in June. This compared with a 1.2% rise in May, which was unchanged from a previous estimate. It was also an unexpected increase for most economists who had been predicting a 0.1% monthly decline. Retailers suggested that June’s hot spell and more sales promotions helped increasing shopping in clothing stores and online. The ONS also said sports sales were higher last month and pointed to an increase in alcohol and tobacco sales amid the early matches of the Fifa World Cup helping drive spending. Between April and June, retail sales are estimated to have risen by 0.6% compared with the first three months of the year, according to the ONS. ONS Senior Statistician Hannah Finselbach said: “Internet retailers did especially well, with businesses telling us that this was because of promotions and the warm weather, with strong demand in June for outdoor products, air conditioning and clothing. “Sports merchandise also sold well online. “With internet retailers faring well, the proportion of online sales has risen to its highest since spring 2021 when coronavirus restrictions were ending.” The share of online sales was 29.4% in June, the highest since April 2021. Non-store retailers, which are primarily online shops but also includes sellers like street stalls and markets, benefited from the biggest boost in June with sales up 4.4%. Clothing and footwear sales were up by 1.9% in June, the biggest monthly rise for the category since September last year. The ONS highlighted sales of items like fans and air conditioning and outdoor furniture selling well last month, while art galleries enjoyed more visitors suggesting people opting for activities to keep cool. Hot spells last month made it the second warmest June on record for the UK, according to the Met Office. On the other hand, motor fuel sales dropped sharply over the second quarter, with retailers suggesting that motorists made fewer journeys and delayed filling tanks since April as prices rose after the start of the US-Israel’s war with Iran. Sandra Prince, Head of Consumer at Lloyds, said: “Warmer weather and World Cup excitement have helped deliver another positive month for retailers, encouraging spending across clothing, garden furniture and other seasonal ranges. “While the weather may have put some shoppers off heading to the high street, many simply switched to online with strong digital sales helping to maintain momentum for retailers. However, experts have cautioned that consumer spending could be set to weaken in the months ahead as cost-of-living pressures take hold. Harvir Dhillon, Lead Economist at the British Retail Consortium, said: “While retailers have been enjoying the boost to sales, there are challenges ahead, particularly as hostilities in the Middle East resume. “Household budgets remain under pressure, consumer confidence is fragile, and retailers are facing rising operating costs.” Jonathan Moyes, Head of Investment Research at Wealth Club, added: “The resumption of the Iran war in July has seen Brent crude oil touch 100 US dollars a barrel again overnight. “This will undoubtedly weigh on consumers in the latter half of this year as inflation again begins to take its toll. “Whilst the sun was shining on retailers in June, there are some dark clouds in the distance that are likely to keep a lid on sentiment for the remainder of the year.”

article_title: Fabletics reunites with Stephen and Erica Malbon for second golfwear collaboration
sub_title: Fabletics has teamed up once again with golf lifestyle duo Stephen and Erica Malbon to launch a second limited-edition capsule collection, building on the success of their first collaboration with a range inspired by coastal style and performance dressing.
article_content: Fabletics has teamed up once again with golf lifestyle duo Stephen and Erica Malbon to launch a second limited-edition capsule collection, building on the success of their first collaboration with a range inspired by coastal style and performance dressing. The latest collection combines lightweight, breathable performance fabrics with ocean-inspired design details, including sea urchin motifs, across men’s and women’s apparel designed for wear both on and off the golf course. The launch reflects the continued evolution of golfwear, as brands increasingly blend technical performance with lifestyle appeal to attract both established players and a new generation of consumers. Don Ressler, Co-Founder of Fabletics, said: “Stephen and Erica have such a distinct point of view on the culture of golf, and together we saw an opportunity to build on the momentum of our first collection with something that feels fresh, elevated and unexpected, without losing sight of performance or accessibility.” “Golf has become more than a sport, it’s a lifestyle, and this collection brings a fresh spin to golfwear for people who love the game, the energy and the culture around it.” Stephen and Erica Malbon said the collection drew inspiration from the ocean, particularly the patterns, colours and textures of sea urchins, which feature throughout the range in graphics, logos and fabric detailing. The capsule includes technical separates designed for everything from golf rounds and practice sessions to travel and everyday wear. The collection is also size-inclusive, with men’s styles available from XS to XXL, with selected pieces up to 4XL, and women’s styles ranging from XXS to 4XL. The collaboration follows growing investment in fashion-led golf collections as brands respond to rising interest in the sport among younger consumers and position golf apparel as part of a broader lifestyle wardrobe rather than performance wear alone. The Stephen & Erica Malbon for Fabletics collection is available now online and in selected Fabletics stores. In February we sat down with Mark Ralea, Fabletics' General Manager on his career journey and how the industry has evolved since his first role at Stylebop.com. He also highlighted what he finds most rewarding about his current role and how he creates an environment where others can thrive.

article_title: Frasers CEO says business rates are deterring high street investment
sub_title: Frasers Group Chief Executive Michael Murray has criticised the UK business rates system, arguing that higher bills following store upgrades are discouraging investment in town centres.
article_content: Frasers Group boss Michael Murray has criticised the UK business rates system, arguing that higher bills following store upgrades are discouraging investment in town centres. The retail group spends tens of millions of pounds on upgrading its store estate, but those projects can push up property rateable values and the resulting tax bills, Murray said in an interview with The Telegraph at the opening of a new Sports Direct flagship in Dublin. Murray described the current business rate system, which he said penalised retailers for upgrading their shops, as making “zero sense”. He added that rising operating costs were making it harder to run high street stores profitably. Murray's remarks come amid wider demands to scrap the property tax . The Real Rates Reform Alliance, which says it speaks for more than 28,000 firms and business leaders, has suggested a 2% levy on online sales to pay for a 37% cut in business rates for bricks-and-mortar companies. Research cited by the alliance found that 55% of firms viewed business rates as a major or moderate cost. Around 17% had cut jobs in response to the burden, while 31% had raised prices. This would be a “major shot in the arm” for many high streets and communities, which it said have been forced into cutting jobs, investment and raising prices due to the pressures of rising business rate bills, according to the alliance. In addition to business rates, Murray noted that Frasers is dealing with higher employment costs after increases in the national minimum wage and employers’ National Insurance contributions. Murray also took aim at plans to grant pubs and music venues a 20% business rates discount while imposing extra charges on large warehouses. He said warehouses serving physical shops should not be treated the same as distribution centres run by online-only retailers. Murray also called for lower rates on shops to reduce the tax disparity between online pureplays and retailers maintaining town-centre estates. Despite the hurdles presented by business rates, Frasers is continuing to grow and refresh its physical estate under its Elevation Strategy. Its new Sports Direct and Everlast Gyms+ flagship in Dublin spans 85,000 sq ft over four floors at the former Debenhams site on Henry Street. The “landmark” opening, which has created 75 new roles, marks a major €80 million investment in Dublin city centre and also signals the official launch of HOKA in Sports Direct stores, further strengthening the retailer's position as a strategic partner for the world’s biggest sports brands

article_title: Fred Perry partners Westminster Menswear Archive ahead of 75th anniversary
sub_title: Fred Perry has unveiled a new research partnership with the Westminster Menswear Archive ahead of its 75th anniversary in 2027. The collaboration with the
article_content: Fred Perry has unveiled a new research partnership with the Westminster Menswear Archive ahead of its 75th anniversary in 2027. The collaboration with the Westminster Menswear Archive will be led by its Director, Professor Andrew Groves, who will take a deep dive into Fred Perry’s founding years, drawing on personal archives, company records, patents and sporting press to document the brand’s sporting origins from 1952. Rob Gaitt, Fred Perry Brand Director, said: “Andrew’s focus on the founding years has given us a wonderful blueprint for our approach to 2027. A brand founded on product that was fit for purpose, aspirational not elitist, which talked directly to fans and players. Using selective distribution, authenticated by champions via collaborations. Sportswear, not just tennis.” The Westminster Menswear Archive is a teaching, research and collecting resource at the University of Westminster. It holds over 3,000 garments and related objects, particularly sportswear, workwear, military pieces and designer fashion. To set the tone for the 75th anniversary year, Fred Perry put on a fashion show at the V&A East Storehouse in June. It centred on ‘Fred Perry Retold’, which “celebrates what came before to look forward”. It gave a snapshot of a new sportswear range that will be presented throughout 2027. Richard Gilmore, Managing Director of Fred Perry, said: “As we commemorate this landmark anniversary, we honour the heritage of our brand and the principles set on and off the court by the man himself, all whilst looking forward to many decades more of championing the Laurel Wreath. “We remain modernists, our ambition and absolute dedication set a brave new agenda for where the next 75 years will take us.” As well as its strong heritage in sport and its links to the British music scene, along with its connections to style tribes including mods, skinheads and rude boys, Fred Perry has long championed UK designers including Craig Green, Charles Jeffrey and Nicolas Daley through collaborations. In a nod to its continued support of up-and-coming design talent, Fred Perry has also announced a patronage with the British Fashion Council. The partnership will work to amplify and celebrate some of the most creative designers in the UK, using the brand’s global platform and targeted distribution around the world to further promote the talented roster of collaborators, past and present. Natalie Porter, Director of Network at The British Fashion Council, said: “We are delighted to welcome Fred Perry as a Patron of the British Fashion Council. “Ours is a shared commitment to championing British designer talent, celebrating the strength of community, and recognising the powerful connection between fashion and culture. We look forward to building a meaningful partnership that supports the future of British creativity.” In March, Fred Perry opened a new flagship Soho store at 40-42 Lexington Street, adding to its long-standing store around the corner at 12 Newburgh Street. Described as “not just a shop, but a meeting point for like-minded individuals and an event-ready space to celebrate all things Fred Perry”, it signified the brand’s first steps towards celebrating its 75th year.

article_title: Gymshark promotes ex-ASOS director as Chief Supply Chain Officer
sub_title: Gymshark's continues to add to its executive team, with founder and Chief Executive Ben Francis MBE announcing that Matt Rogers, the brand's Global Supply Chain Director, has been promoted to the position of Chief Supply Chain Officer.
article_content: Gymshark continues to add to its executive team with founder and Chief Executive Ben Francis MBE announcing that Matt Rogers, the brand's Global Supply Chain Director, has been promoted to the position of Chief Supply Chain Officer. "Since joining Gymshark in 2023 as our Supply Chain Director, Matt has made a huge impact," Francis shared in a LinkedIn post. "Over the past few years, he's helped strengthen and evolve our supply chain and more recently, has done an outstanding job leading the function as Interim General Manager for Sourcing and Supply Chain." "Matt has consistently demonstrated the leadership, judgement and ambition needed to build a supply chain that's ready for the next chapter of Gymshark. This marks the second appointment to Gymshark's senior leadership team this month. The brand appointed former Boden Executive Shaun Perkinson to lead its technology function as Chief Technology Officer. Perkinson took over the position from John Douglas, who joined Gymshark five years ago and was looking to retire. Francis had also announced Perkinson's appointment on LinkedIn, highlighting the 20 years of experience he is bringing to the CTO role, and in particular his "combination of technical expertise, commercial instinct and collaborative approach". "Technology will continue to play a pivotal role in helping us create better experiences for our community and supporting the next stage of our growth. Shaun joins us at an exciting time and I'm confident we'll do great things together," Francis added. Both appointments followed the announcement that Francis was in negotiations to buy back part of the 21% stake held by US private equity firm General Atlantic, according to reports by the Financial Times. Francis, who still owns a majority stake in the company he founded out of his parents' garage in 2012, is now looking to further tighten his control over the company. Sources told the publication that while Francis had considered buying back the entirety of the General Atlantic stake, he is more likely to buy part of it.

article_title: LVMH revenues rise as fashion division returns to growth in Q2
sub_title: LVMH reported revenue of €38.6 billion for the first half of 2026, with growth accelerating in the second quarter as its Fashion & Leather Goods division returned to organic growth despite continued geopolitical and economic uncertainty.
article_content: LVMH reported revenue of €38.6 billion for the first half of 2026, with growth accelerating in the second quarter as its Fashion & Leather Goods division returned to organic growth despite continued geopolitical and economic uncertainty. The luxury group posted revenue of €38.6 billion for the six months to 30 June, down 3% year-on-year on a reported basis, while organic revenue increased 2%. Profit from recurring operations declined 4% to €8.7 billion, with an operating margin remaining high at 22.5%. Net profit was broadly flat at €5.7 billion. LVMH said organic revenue growth accelerated to 3% in the second quarter, or 4% excluding the impact of the conflict in the Middle East, supported by stronger performances in the US and Asia excluding Japan. Fashion & Leather Goods, the group's largest division, generated revenue of €18.1 billion, down 5% on a reported basis and 1% organically over the half year. However, the business returned to 1% organic growth in the second quarter, marking an improvement on the first quarter when the division reported a 2% organic decline as disruption linked to the conflict in the Middle East weighed on performance. The group credited the recovery to the strong debut of Jonathan Anderson's first collections for Christian Dior, alongside the performance of Louis Vuitton's new flagship stores in Beijing and Seoul. Bernard Arnault, Chairman and CEO of LVMH, said: “LVMH demonstrated its solidity and effective strategy. Our Maisons, which remained focused on ensuring the utmost quality in our products, and several of which are pursuing their creative renewal, continued to inspire dreams and enhance their desirability.” He added that second-quarter growth was driven by “the success of Jonathan Anderson's first designs for Christian Dior, the remarkable performance of Louis Vuitton's exceptional new stores in Beijing and Seoul, and Tiffany and Bvlgari's iconic lines”. Christian Dior reported accelerating growth following the launch of Anderson's first designs, with the new Cigale bag receiving a strong customer response. Elsewhere, Loro Piana delivered another strong performance, while Rimowa and Berluti also recorded growth during the period. Across the wider group, Watches & Jewelry was among the strongest-performing divisions, with organic revenue increasing 9%, supported by Tiffany & Co. and Bvlgari. Selective Retailing, which includes Sephora, recorded 5% organic growth, while Wines & Spirits also returned to growth, with organic revenue up 5%. Looking ahead, LVMH said it remains confident despite an uncertain geopolitical and economic environment, maintaining its strategy of investing in creativity, product quality, and retail experiences to strengthen the desirability of its brands.

article_title: Burberry and V&A to stage display celebrating the history of the trench coat
sub_title: Rare catalogues, a coat worn by Hardy Amies and 19 runway looks will chart the evolution of Burberry’s best-known design during the British house’s 170th year.
article_content: Burberry and the V&A are set to stage a free display tracing the development of the Burberry trench coat, marking the iconic British brand’s 170th anniversary. The Burberry Trench: Crafting an Icon will run from 21 September 2026 to 3 January 2027 at V&A South Kensington; its opening coincides with the staging of Burberry's catwalk show at September's London Fashion Week. It will bring together rare objects from the Burberry Archive and the museum’s collection, including material being publicly exhibited for the first time. The display will occupy the Prince Consort Gallery, a seldom-seen space that once housed textiles in mahogany cabinets. It will follow the trench coat’s progression from protective outerwear and military clothing into one of Burberry’s central products and an internationally recognised fashion design. A men's metallic silk trench from 2013 by Christopher Bailey (Courtesy: Burberry) The opening section, Invention , will focus on Thomas Burberry’s creation of cotton gabardine in 1879. Its use gave the company’s outerwear protection from the weather while retaining a lightweight and practical construction. The exhibition will examine how this material helped establish the trench as a sought-after coat before its adoption as a fashion staple. Burberry was founded by Thomas Burberry in 1856 and continues to use gabardine across its Heritage Trench range. A Burberry design from c. 1937-1944 pictured in a catalogue (Courtesy: Burberry) Craft will examine the practical details that have shaped the coat for more than a century. These include its hand-finished collar and House Check lining, as well as the storm flap and detachable throat latch, which provide additional protection. Burberry says its trench collar is assembled from eight parts and can require up to 200 stitches. The company first used its check to line rainwear during the 1920s. The final section, Creativity , will present 19 runway looks produced over the past 25 years. The selection will include designs by current Chief Creative Officer Daniel Lee and former Chief Creative Officer Christopher Bailey, showing how successive collections have revised the trench’s proportions, construction and styling. Hardy Amies' personalised Burberry car coat from 1979 (Courtesy: Burberry) Early 20th-century catalogues and a Burberry trench coat worn by British fashion designer Hardy Amies will also feature. Carly Eck, brand curator at Burberr, said: “A myriad of objects from the brand’s Archive will be publicly exhibited for the first time – from early 20th-century catalogues to a Burberry trench coat worn by fashion designer Hardy Amies.” Oriole Cullen, senior curator of fashion and textiles at the V&A, said the display would highlight how the British fashion staple “continues to evolve over a century on”. Fringed women's trench from AW25 by Daniel Lee (Courtesy: Burberry) The display forms part of Burberry’s multi-year partnership with the V&A, which will lead to the opening of The Burberry Gallery in autumn 2028. The project will transform the museum’s existing Fashion Gallery into a redesigned space for its collection, which spans five centuries. The Burberry Trench: Crafting an Icon will remain free and open to all throughout its run.

article_title: UK retailers keep prices low as shop price inflation eases
sub_title: UK shop price inflation slowed to 0.9% in July, according to the British Retail Consortium's (BRC) Shop Price Monitor, as retailers increased promotional activity across clothing, footwear and food to help consumers manage the cost of living.
article_content: UK shop price inflation slowed to 0.9% in July, according to the British Retail Consortium's (BRC) Shop Price Monitor, as retailers increased promotional activity across clothing, footwear and food to help consumers manage the cost of living. The rate of shop price inflation fell from 1.2% in June, while non-food inflation eased to 0.2% from 0.6%. Food inflation also slowed to 2.2%, down from 2.4% the previous month, although fresh food inflation edged up to 3.1%. The BRC said retailers competed to limit price rises with a wave of summer promotions. Clothing and footwear retailers offered significant discounts to clear seasonal stock, while shoppers also benefited from deals on snacks and alcoholic drinks during the football World Cup. Helen Dickinson, Chief Executive of the BRC, said: “Good news for households in July as shop price inflation slowed. Retailers competed hard to limit price rises, with a wave of summer promotions across food and other goods.” She added that categories including electricals and health & beauty saw higher inflation as rising chip prices and manufacturing costs fed through to prices. Despite the slowdown in inflation, Dickinson warned that retailers continue to face mounting cost pressures from higher employment costs, packaging taxes, global instability and climate-related disruption. “The best way to keep the cost of living down is to keep the cost of doing business down. Cutting unnecessary taxes and levies on energy bills would help retailers keep prices low, invest locally and support jobs in every town and city,” she said. Mike Watkins, Head of Retailer and Business Insight at NIQ, said lower shop price inflation would provide some relief for households facing rising energy and fuel costs. “We can expect promotions to continue to be an important part of driving demand for the rest of the summer,” he added. The figures come after official data from the Office for National Statistics showed UK retail sales rose unexpectedly in June , with clothing and footwear retailers benefiting from warm weather and increased promotional activity. Online shopping also reached its highest share of retail sales since spring 2021. However, retailers continue to warn that trading conditions remain challenging. Last week, the BRC renewed its calls for wider business rates reform , arguing that the sector has faced an additional £6.5 billion in employment costs since 2024, alongside higher business rates and other operating expenses.

Frasers to advance Harvey Nichols bid as Hugo Boss clears German merger control
sub_title: Frasers continues to push forward with two of its recent takeover bids for Harvey Nichols and Hugo Boss.
article_content: Frasers continues to push forward with two of its recent takeover bids. The retail group is expected to submit a bid for department store Harvey Nichols and has also received merger control clearance from the European Commission to take forward its takeover offer of Hugo Boss. Frasers Group and NEXT both face a 28 July deadline to submit offers for Harvey Nichols, according to Sky News, while unidentified international bidders are reportedly working to a separate timetable. Harvey Nichols is being sold through advisers at FTI Consulting after 35 years under the ownership of Hong Kong businessman Sir Dickson Poon. The process places its Knightsbridge flagship and wider store estate in play, although reaching the bid deadline does not guarantee that a transaction will be completed. Frasers Group entered the process two weeks ago , despite concerns among some Harvey Nichols suppliers about its potential ownership. Frasers owns Sports Direct, Flannels and House of Fraser. The Harvey Nichols deadline coincides with Frasers’ pursuit of German premium fashion group Hugo Boss, with its offer becoming unconditional today, following the takeover bid's approval by German authorities. Bidders for Harvey Nichols have been asked to commit between £50 million and £60 million over the medium term to fund the luxury department store's transformation plan, Sky News previously reported. The proposed investment, which would be separate from the acquisition price, would support a refurbishment of the Edinburgh store, international expansion, digital development and the management team’s business plan. Apart from Frasers Group and NEXT, potential bidders for the department store include Modella Capital, the owner of Hobbycraft and TGJones, as well as Dubai-based Chalhoub Group and India’s Reliance Retail. NEXT emerged as a potential bidder earlier this month . It remains unclear whether NEXT would retain Harvey Nichols’ regional store network or focus on the brand and its intellectual property. FTI Consulting will now assess the bids submitted under the auction timetable, including the proposed financial support for the retailer’s turnaround. In the latest developments on the Hugo Boss bid, Frasers Group said its takeover offer for the German luxury brand had received merger control clearance from the European Commission. The approval removes the final regulatory obstacle and means the cash offer for the German fashion company is now legally unconditional. Frasers Group also extended the acceptance period for the offer until midnight 13 August in Frankfurt local time. Frasers crossed Germany’s 30% mandatory-bid threshold last week, after it acquired a further 2,549,900 shares in the company. Yesterday, it was reported by The Times that Frasers Group was considering appointing its Chief Executive, Michael Murray, to lead Hugo Boss if its takeover of the German premium fashion company succeeds. The proposed appointment would give Frasers direct operational control of Hugo Boss and represent a change from its earlier support for incumbent CEO Daniel Grieder when it originally launched its offer in June. The group had previously declared its original €38 price as final . Frasers first launched its bid on 10 June, valuing the remaining 73.94% of the Hugo Boss brand at about €1.98 billion. Almost one month later, Hugo Boss’s management and supervisory boards unanimously recommended that shareholders should reject the unsolicited approach, calling it financially "inadequate". The retail group is also pursuing Australian footwear retailer Accent Group, which has, however, firmly rejected its approach . Last week, Frasers extended that offer until September , with its other terms unchanged.

Premier League shirt prices soar as fans hit by fresh cost hikes
sub_title: Football fans face paying up to £90 for replica shirts after eight Premier League clubs increased their prices.
article_content: Football fans face paying up to £90 for replica shirts after eight Premier League clubs increased their prices. Tottenham fans must now pay £90 for a replica adult first-team shirt, up £5 on last year, while a shirt for a child as young as three years old now costs £70, according to the club’s website. Chelsea has also increased the price of its shirts by £5 to £89.99. A shirt for just-promoted Coventry City is up £10 to £70 and the club’s children’s shirts are also up, by 25% to £60, while a baby kit costs £55. Ipswich Town shirts are up £6 to £65. Leeds, Bournemouth and Hull shirts are all £5 more expensive than last year. Ten clubs charge £80 or more for a shirt. Brentford’s kit will remain current for two years – they are the only Premier League club to take this move. Consumer expert Scott Dixon, from The Complaints Resolver, said: “These price rises will leave many loyal fans wondering when enough is enough. We see this year in, year out, and it smacks of blatant greed and an own goal that could backfire on clubs. “These kits are overpriced by anyone’s standards and will leave many fans priced out. “Children’s clothing is zero rated and there’s less material used to make their kits, so parents will rightly question how some clubs can justify increases of up to 25%. Clubs know how ‘pester power’ works from a marketing angle and how it puts pressure on parents to buy the latest shirts so they don’t feel left out. “Loyal fans deserve better. Clubs should be making it easier for the next generation of supporters to feel part of their club, not pricing them out. “Fans ought to vote with their feet and wallets and refuse to pay it. The unintended consequences will be fans buying cheap counterfeits, which is known to fund organised crime.” The prices follow the seizing of counterfeit football shirts worth over £18 million in the UK during the course of the World Cup because of safety concerns. More than 220,000 pieces of football merchandise were recovered by the Police Intellectual Crime Unit as part of Operation Bloxwich, a UK police enforcement effort targeting counterfeit goods. One raid involved 1,618 fake strips being taken from a warehouse in Birmingham, including replicas of shirts worn by star players such as France’s Kylian Mbappe and Norway’s Erling Haaland.

article_title: Primark turns SKIMS’ London launch into a marketing opportunity
sub_title: Primark placed a mobile billboard beside the queue for SKIMS’ newly opened Regent Street flagship, promoting its £9 shaping bodysuit as a lower-priced alternative to Kim Kardashian’s widely popular shapewear offering.
article_content: Primark placed a mobile billboard beside the newly opened SKIMS’ Regent Street flagship, promoting its £9 shaping bodysuit as a lower-priced alternative to Kim Kardashian’s widely popular shapewear offering. The high street retailer used the opening week of SKIMS’ first standalone UK store to put its product in front of customers looking to enter the newly opened 12,000 sq ft location. The tongue-in-cheek placement showcased Primark's version of the shapewear bodysuit, with the slogan reading "These Kim's prefer Primark £9 shaping bodysuit". In comparison, SKIMS Seamless Sculpt Thong Bodysuit, available in the Regent Street store, currently retails at £84. The campaign was shared on social media by Metro UK and the Daily Mail. The move follows Primark's announcement last week that it had lowered prices across hundreds of womenswear , menswear and kidswear products as part of a new “Iconic Value” initiative aimed at reinforcing its position as a destination for affordable fashion. A post shared by Metro UK (@metro.co.uk) The campaign highlights once again how UK brands and retailers have sharpened their competitive edge following SKIM's entry into the market. Since launching in 2019, SKIMS has positioned itself as a major player in the shapewear and lingerie market , with consumer spending reaching over £1.8 million in 2025, according to data from digital bank Monzo. As competition in the category intensifies, Marks & Spencer launched a 300-piece reimagined lingerie collection, BODY, in April, built around “a modern, modular and solution-focused design philosophy”. Starting at £16, the range covers bras, briefs, shapewear and essentials, using features including 360-degree stretch, laser-cut edges and targeted sculpting. M&S remains one of the key players within the category, according to the retailer, with a bra sold every two seconds. British underwear brand Lounge also recently introduced a 34-piece collection of engineered essentials , in an effort to “reclaim its stake in the category it helped shape” and reposition the brand to sit confidently alongside both SKIMS and M&S Body. Lounge highlighted that its new collection is very size-inclusive, spanning from 28A-40G and XS-3XL. Size inclusivity is one of the biggest selling points for Kim Kardashian's SKIMS brand. "We’ve refined and unified our offering into something that feels complete: a system of fit-led pieces designed to replace compromise with confidence," said Emily Blount, Product Director at Lounge, at the time of the launch. "It’s the result of years of listening, testing and perfecting, and it reaffirms Lounge as a benchmark in modern everyday lingerie." SKIMS opened its very first UK flagship on Friday 24 July, at 245-247 Regent Street. The opening further solidified the brand's retail presence in the UK. It had previously been available through wholesale partners including Selfridges, Harrods and END. The store, which was formerly occupied by Ted Baker, marks SKIMS’ largest European retail location. Jens Grede, co-founder and CEO of SKIMS, commented on the opening: “Our flagship stores play an important role in how customers experience SKIMS beyond the product.” Kim Kardashian, co-founder and Chief Creative Officer, added: "London has always been one of the most inspiring fashion cities in the world to me, so opening our first UK flagship on Regent Street feels especially exciting.” The London launch follows a period of rapid growth for the business. In late 2025, SKIMS secured a $225 million funding round that valued the company at $5 billion , fuelling further investment in physical retail as well as apparel and the NikeSKIMS partnership. The Regent Street flagship is one of a series of international openings, with a new flagship at Dubai Mall and stores also planned for Delhi and Mumbai. Founded by Kim Kardashian, Jens Grede and Emma Grede in 2019, SKIMS began as a direct-to-consumer shapewear brand before expanding into underwear, swimwear, loungewear and menswear.

article_title: Shein slumps to loss as sales hit by Trump’s tariff blow
sub_title: Shein has slumped to a loss as it revealed a sales hit from US president Donald Trump’s move to scrap an import duty exemption on small packages in an update ahead of its planned stock market debut in Hong Kong.
article_content: Shein has slumped to a loss as it revealed a sales hit from US president Donald Trump’s move to scrap an import duty exemption on small packages in an update ahead of its planned stock market debut in Hong Kong. The fast fashion group reported bottom line net losses of $99 million (£74 million) for the three months to the end of March against profits of $395 million (£296 million) a year earlier. Sales edged 1.1% higher to $9.05 billion (£6.78 billion). The group – which recently announced its decision to list its long-planned initial public offering in Hong Kong – said its first quarter loss was largely down to a $328 million (£246 million) hit from an accounting change for special investor shares. But the figures, which were made in its first filing since plans for the group’s Hong Kong listing emerged, laid bare the impact of Trump’s trade war on the group. In May last year, the US removed a so-called “de minimis” tariff exemption on small packages, which Shein had previously used to ship garments from China directly to customers. Earlier this month, the EU also made the same move by imposing a three euro (£2.56) duty on small parcels imported from outside the trading bloc. Shein said: “Since May 2025, the removal of the US de minimis exemption has had an adverse impact on our sales in the US and the overall growth of our net revenues.” It said it had “since observed signs of normalisation in consumer purchasing behaviour and sales trends in the US”. The group added that the EU’s removal of the small parcel exemption may also have a “material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations”. Given that Shein made around a third of sales from Europe last year, it said the impact on the group could be larger than that from the US hit. “Although it remains too early to fully assess, it is possible that trends in the EU could be generally in line with or exceed the impact observed in the US after the removal of the US de minimis exemption,” Shein cautioned. The group said it was looking at raising prices across the US and Europe to offset the sales impact. “In response to the increased duties and taxes, we are pursuing a wide range of options, including increasing our prices in the US market to offset a portion of the increased costs,” it said. It said there may be a “short-term adverse impact” to sales in Europe as it also moves to hikes prices across the EU, but said the “long-term impact remains too early to fully assess”. The UK is also looking to close the small parcels loophole, but not for some years. Former Chancellor Rachel Reeves confirmed plans in the 2025 autumn budget to follow in the footsteps of the US and Europe and review the customs loophole, saying she wants to “support a level playing field in retail”. But the proposed reforms are not expected to be in place until 2029, which has prompted calls from high street retailers to bring this forward.

article_title: Frasers Group opens ‘landmark’ Sports Direct and Everlast Gyms+ flagship in Dublin
sub_title: Frasers Group has opened its first joint retail and fitness proposition outside the UK with a four-storey, 85,000 sq ft integrated Sports Direct and Everlast Gyms+ flagship.
article_content: Frasers Group has opened its first joint retail and fitness proposition outside the UK with a four-storey, 85,000 sq ft integrated Sports Direct and Everlast Gyms+ flagship at 54–62 Henry Street in Dublin, taking over the former Debenhams site. The “landmark” opening, which has created 75 new roles, marks a major €80 million investment in Dublin city centre and also signals the official launch of HOKA in Sports Direct stores, further strengthening the retailer's position as a strategic partner for the world’s biggest sports brands. Michael Murray, Chief Executive Officer at Frasers Group, said: “Building on the momentum of our ‘Elevation Strategy’, the opening of this Dublin flagship is another defining milestone for Frasers Group. “As our first integrated Sports Direct and Everlast Gyms+ flagship in Europe, it reflects our ambition to accelerate international growth while delivering an unrivalled retail and fitness experience.” To celebrate the opening and the city’s rich sporting heritage, the flagship hosted a weekend of exclusive appearances from Irish athletes, including John O'Shea, Caoimhin Kelleher, Conor Murray and Erin King, alongside New Balance, Adidas and ASICS run clubs, fitness masterclasses, DJ sets and giveaways. With a focus on the local market, the opening weekend also included a Gaelic Athletic Association (GAA) Challenge in the form of an AR Gaelic football simulator, which invited customers to test their accuracy from increasing distances to win instant rewards and prizes. Spanning 60,000 sq ft, Sports Direct occupies the first three floors of the building, giving customers access to the world's leading sports brands, including Nike, Adidas, Under Armour, On, Columbia and The North Face across men’s, women’s and kidswear. In addition to enhanced retail experiences for Frasers Group’s own brands Everlast and Slazenger, customers can also shop a curated selection of premium lifestyle and denim brands at USC, including HUGO, Lacoste, Tommy Hilfiger and C.P. Company, as well as the latest in gaming at Game. Designed to enrich the customer journey, Sports Direct’s signature ‘Running’, ‘Outdoor’ and ‘Football’ concepts have been reimagined to provide “best-in-class experiences”. Complementing the experience is a footwear delivery system that uses a dumbwaiter to streamline product collection, ensuring customers receive their selected footwear – from lifestyle through to elite performance – quickly and seamlessly. Situated on the top floor is the 25,000 sq ft Everlast Gyms+, marking the brand’s debut outside the UK and bringing its next-generation ‘fitness ecosystem’ to Ireland for the first time. Combining elite training, recovery, nutrition and community, Everlast Gyms+ provides members with a holistic cross-functional fitness experience where athletes of all levels can achieve their fitness goals. Tapping into one of the fastest-growing fitness phenomena, Everlast Gyms+ will serve as Ireland’s first official HYROX Performance Centre (HPC), featuring specialist performance turf and tailored programming designed to effectively train competing athletes. It is also the first gym in the world to receive Centr’s limited-edition white Elite-15 competition-grade equipment to simulate HYROX race-day conditions. Additional key features of Everlast Gyms+ Dublin include a Reformer Pilates Studio, a dedicated Nike ‘Strength’ area with high-performance Nike ‘Grind’ equipment, and a recovery space with three Brass Monkey ice baths and a sauna. The redevelopment of the former Debenhams site also includes an almost twofold expansion of Zara's store as a key tenant.
