Landsec closes in on £500m Metrocentre acquisition
sub_title: Landsec is reportedly close to completing a deal worth about £500 million for Gateshead’s Metrocentre, with the property group potentially seeking shareholder funding for the acquisition, according to The Times.
article_content: Landsec is reportedly close to completing a deal worth approximately £500 million for Gateshead’s Metrocentre, with the property giant potentially seeking shareholder funding for the acquisition, according to The Times. The proposed purchase would give Landsec control of one of the UK’s largest shopping centres, following competition from Frasers Group and Hammerson. Earlier this year, the Metrocentre Partnership put the centre up for sale. The asset is owned by a group of investors that acquired it after Intu - a major corporate shopping centre operator and the centre's former owner - entered administration in 2020. More than £60 million has been invested in upgrades at Metrocentre by the Metrocentre Partnership in recent years. This work included refurbishing The Crescent, a 10,000 sq ft retail destination intended to support local and independent brands. In March, Metrocentre said that footfall had exceeded 16 million since the pandemic for the first time, after rising 5.4% annually. It attributed the improvement to a Sovereign Centros-led investment programme that brought changes to the centre, introduced new brands and upgraded facilities for existing operators. The centre has continued to secure retailer investment during the sale process. In July, New Look opened its biggest concept store to date at Metrocentre, taking up 11,000 sq ft in the Red Mall. The store includes expanded womenswear and accessories ranges, as well as digital browsing and services for Click & Collect, order-in-store and self-service returns. Stradivarius and Hollister have also joined the fashion offer over the past year, while Bershka and Lefties have been signed for future openings. The shopping centre forms part of a 52-acre brownfield development area planned to become Metro Riverside, a 4,500-home neighbourhood being advanced through an agreement involving Metrocentre and Gateshead Council. Plans include homes, retail, a hotel, workspaces and leisure facilities. The proposed MetroGreen Area Action Plan included 990 homes around Metrocentre by 2030, with the wider district planned around a “20 minute destination” model. Landsec’s acquisition would extend beyond ownership of the existing retail asset, bringing the group into a development area that includes future residential and commercial uses.

article_title: Stella McCartney and pushchair brand Bugaboo unveil multi-year partnership
sub_title: British fashion house Stella McCartney has partnered with premium pushchair brand Bugaboo on a special-edition collection launching globally in September 2026.
article_content: British fashion house Stella McCartney has partnered with premium pushchair brand Bugaboo on a special-edition collection launching globally in September 2026. The agreement marks the start of a multi-year partnership focused on parenting products that combine fashion, functionality and lower-impact materials. It is Bugaboo’s first major collaboration in more than 10 years, following previous projects with fashion brands including Missoni and Kith. The Amsterdam-founded company expects the partnership to strengthen its position among design-conscious parents while extending its reach within fashion and culture. Stella McCartney said: “As a mother, I want the things I design to reflect the world I want to build. Working with Bugaboo felt completely natural, as it’s a brand that shares our commitment to innovation and responsibility. “This collection is for every mum who wants to bring her own individuality and playfulness into parenthood.” The companies said the collection will use recycled polyester fabrics made from plastic bottles, water-free dye technology, recycled aluminium and bio-based materials. The materials are intended to reduce environmental impact while maintaining product quality and performance. Responsible materials have long been central to Stella McCartney’s brand positioning. In May, the latest H&M collaboration included recycled content , organic cotton and wool that was certified to the Responsible Wool Standard, plus coated materials made using industrial corn and recycled vegetable oil. The fashion house also recently announced a new licensing partnership for the development, production and distribution of Stella McCartney Kids with Altana, which also develops kidswear for Moschino, CP Company and Paul & Shark. That licensing partnership covers the childrenswear line’s production chain while keeping design under Stella McCartney’s in-house team. Founded in Amsterdam, Bugaboo built its premium position around engineering-led pushchairs and design. The Stella McCartney deal forms part of a wider strategy to develop collaborations and link parenting products more closely with personal style. Adriaan Thierry, CEO of Bugaboo, said modern parents expect their purchases to reflect both their design preferences and values. “Stella has transformed expectations around luxury fashion and responsible design, while Bugaboo has spent more than two decades redefining mobility for parents through category-leading innovation,” he said. “By combining Stella McCartney’s distinctive creative perspective with Bugaboo’s heritage of purposeful design and engineering excellence, we’ve created a collection that speaks to a new generation of parents who refuse to choose between performance, style and values.” The collaboration gives Stella McCartney a route into the parenting category beyond childrenswear, while providing Bugaboo with access to the designer’s global fashion audience. The first products from the partnership will become available worldwide in September 2026.

article_title: Frasers raises Hugo Boss stake above 30%, takeover offer remains open
sub_title: Frasers Group raises its Hugo Boss stake to 30.28%, crossing the mandatory bid threshold as its €38-per-share takeover offer remains open.
article_content: Frasers Group has increased its stake in Hugo Boss to 30.28%, crossing Germany’s mandatory bid threshold, although its €38-per-share offer remains unchanged. Frasers Group has today announced that following up from its initial takeover offer of the German luxury brand Hugo Boss , it has now acquired an additional 2,5+ million Hugo Boss shares. This translate to around 3.69% of the share capital and voting rights of the business. At that time of the initial takeover offer in June, Frasers Group owned just over 18 million shares, equal to 26.06% of the Hugo Boss' share capital. The latest transaction means that the British retail group, which owns Sports Direct and Flannels, now owns in aggregate close to 21 million shares in Hugo Boss, which amounts to a 30.28% stake of the share capital and voting rights of the German brand, excluding additional shares that have been tendered into the offer. The latest offer remains open at €38 for each Hugo Boss share not held by Frasers, which the Group has previously said marks its final price. T he initial acceptance period for the offer is due to end at midnight Frankfurt time (GMT+2) on 27 July. Now that Frasers owns over 30% of the German company it has crossed the mandatory bid threshold under Germany’s Takeover Code, which, similar to the UK takeover code means it is now required to make an offer for all remaining Hugo Boss shares. It also reaffirms its position as the company's controlling shareholder. Full ownership would give Frasers direct control over a premium apparel brand with revenues of €4.26 billion and a global store network, at a time when the British group has been expanding its European footprint. Yet, this does not mean though that its offer will be accepted. Hugo Boss' board has previously recommended that shareholders reject Frasers takeover offer , which they called "inadequate". In 2024, Frasers faced a similar situation, when it launched a takeover bid for British luxury brand Mulberry, in which it held around 37%. Yet Mulberry's biggest shareholder, Challice, which owned a 56% stake, opposed Frasers bid, so while it remains a major stakeholder it does not control the business. Frasers Group spent the last six years building up its stake in Hugo Boss , culminating in a voluntary public takeover offer on 10 June, which valued the shares outside Frasers’ ownership at around €1.98 billion (£1.73 billion). The bid landed as Hugo Boss had been working through a strategic reset after falling sales, while Frasers has been expanding its influence across European. Frasers presented the move as “long-term value creation”. On July 9 Hugo Boss’s management and supervisory boards unanimously advised shareholders not to accept Frasers Group's initial, unsolicited, takeover bid, describing it as "inadequate". Daniel Grieder, Chief Executive Officer of Hugo Boss, commented at the time: “Hugo Boss has a well-defined strategy, a strong financial profile, and a compelling path to superior long-term value creation. “We focus on further strengthening our brands, structurally improving profitability, and accelerating cash generation over the coming years. “Against this backdrop, we firmly believe that the offer price fails to capture the company’s intrinsic value and long-term potential.” Frasers followed up its initial bid for Hugo Boss with another takeover offer for Australia’s Accent Group for £166 million . Frasers Group is already a majority shareholder (almost 23%) of Accent Group, which sells brands including Hype in Australia as well as operating multi-brand retailer Platypus Shoes. It is also reported to handle Frasers Group’s Sports Direct in the region. Accent Group rejected Frasers Group's "unsolicited, highly opportunistic" takeover bid on 29 June . These are not the only examples of Frasers Group's appetite to takeover companies. In the past 18 months alone, Frasers has acquired a majority stake in Italian multi-sport retailer Maxi Sport , taken control of Norwegian sporting goods chain XXL and added multiple UK designer outlets and shopping centres to its property portfolio. Yet, Hugo Boss would be the most prominent brand asset in Frasers' empire, which also includes Jack Wills, Gieves & Hawkes and USC. As was reported when the bid was announced, it would represent a major step in Frasers' "Elevation Strategy" of moving beyond its Sports Direct roots toward premium retail. The Hugo Boss update also came one day after Frasers launched a share buyback programme with newly appointed joint broker Panmure Liberum. The arrangement permits the broker to acquire up to 10 million Frasers ordinary shares, with the total purchase price capped at £80 million. Purchases can continue until the trading day immediately before the group’s next annual general meeting, currently expected in mid-September. Shares acquired through the programme will be held in treasury. Frasers said the sole purpose of the purchases is to reduce its share capital. The Hugo Boss offer is still subject to the published terms and the relevant regulatory clearances, and completion had previously been targeted for the second half of 2026.

article_title: Depop teams up with Zara Larsson for global campaign
sub_title: Resale fashion marketplace Depop has launched a new global campaign starring Grammy-nominated artist Zara Larsson, celebrating personal style, creativity and second-hand fashion.
article_content: Resale fashion marketplace Depop has launched a new global campaign starring Grammy-nominated artist Zara Larsson, celebrating personal style, creativity and second-hand fashion. The four-part content series, directed by filmmaker Dave Meyers, explores Depop’s role as a platform for discovering, buying and selling unique fashion pieces, with Larsson bringing her own approach to styling into the campaign. Shot in Sweden and styled by Caterina Ospina, the campaign reflects Larsson’s personal mix of vintage and contemporary fashion, highlighting how consumers are increasingly using resale platforms to create individual wardrobes beyond traditional fashion trends. "Fashion has always been one of the ways I express myself,” said Larsson. “I love mixing vintage with newer pieces and finding things that feel unexpected. That’s why I’ve always loved Depop.” A post shared by Depop (@depop) To coincide with the campaign launch on 21 July, Depop is introducing The Zara Larsson Edit, an exclusive Depop Shop featuring 20 to 30 pieces curated from the artist’s personal wardrobe, alongside upcycled merchandise and one-of-a-kind fashion finds including designer items. The collection aims to give fans access to Larsson’s personal style while reinforcing Depop’s focus on circular fashion and extending the life cycle of clothing. Steve Dool, Brand and Creative Director at Depop, said: “Zara has an incredible eye for style because she approaches fashion with curiosity rather than rules.” “Her mix of vintage, emerging designers and personal treasures feels effortless, and that’s exactly the spirit of Depop.” Founded in 2011, Depop has grown into one of the leading resale fashion marketplaces, with approximately 56 million registered users globally. The platform has positioned itself around community-led shopping, encouraging users to buy and sell second-hand clothing while creating a more circular approach to fashion consumption. The campaign comes as Depop enters a new phase of growth following eBay’s proposed $1.2 billion acquisition of the platform from Etsy . The deal was cleared by the UK Competition and Markets Authority earlier this month, removing a key regulatory hurdle and allowing the transaction to proceed. The acquisition forms part of eBay’s wider strategy to strengthen its position in fashion resale, while Depop is expected to retain its name, brand, platform and community focus following completion of the deal.

article_title: London Fashion Week September 2026 schedule announced
sub_title: The British Fashion Council (BFC) has announced the provisional schedule for London Fashion Week September 2026, with the event set to feature the return of major British fashion houses alongside new talent and increased retail participation.
article_content: The British Fashion Council (BFC) has announced the provisional schedule for London Fashion Week September 2026, with the event set to feature the return of major British fashion houses alongside new talent and increased retail participation. Taking place from 17 to 21 September 2026, the schedule will see McQueen return with Seán McGirr presenting his London debut for the house, showcasing both menswear and womenswear Spring/Summer 2027 collections. Mulberry will also return to the official schedule under new Creative Director Christopher Kane, who will present his debut collection for the brand. The season will also feature established British names including Burberry, Barbour, Emilia Wickstead, Erdem, Harris Reed, Richard Quinn, Roksanda and Simone Rocha, alongside emerging designers supported through initiatives including BFC NEWGEN. Francesca Lake, Gui Rosa and Petra Fagerström will make their London Fashion Week debuts as BFC NEWGEN recipients , while Fashion East will return to the schedule following further investment from the BFC into the talent support scheme. Laura Weir, Chief Executive of the British Fashion Council, said: “This season marks an exciting moment for London Fashion Week, with the return of leading British brands alongside an exceptional new generation of creative talent.” “This schedule reflects the confidence and momentum of British fashion today, bringing together established houses, emerging designers and industry partners on a platform that continues to shape global fashion.” The September edition will also highlight the increasing role of retail and consumer engagement within London Fashion Week. Marks & Spencer will make its debut on the official schedule with its first exclusive runway collection , featuring a “see now, buy now” womenswear and menswear collection to mark its centenary year. Elsewhere, eBay will return with its Endless Runway pre-loved fashion show , available to shop through eBay Live, while Selfridges will spotlight participating LFW brands through dedicated in-store highlights and a curated edit of British designers. H&M will also collaborate with photographer Nick Knight and SHOWstudio on a new interpretation of the fashion show format. The BFC said the September schedule will continue to position London Fashion Week as a platform for creative innovation, cultural impact and commercial growth, bringing together fashion houses, emerging designers, retailers and industry partners.

article_title: What new Prime Minister Andy Burnham needs to do to put the feelgood factor back into the UK high street
sub_title: Former Mayor of Greater Manchester and self-styled ‘King of the North’ Andy Burnham has today, 20 July, officially taken over from Keir Starmer as Prime Minister.
article_content: Former Mayor of Greater Manchester and self-styled ‘King of the North’ Andy Burnham has today, 20 July, officially taken over from Keir Starmer as Prime Minister. Now the real work begins, and Burnham is being urged by many retail industry big hitters to follow through on his pledges to address business rates reform, rising employment costs and put in place help for the UK’s high streets. In a recent speech, Burnham said his ambitions include “good growth in every postcode”. He also asked the question: “Shouldn’t we make our high streets the new symbol of Britain's renaissance?” With prominent fashion retail casualties in 2026 including LK Bennett , Russell & Bromley , Quiz and Claire’s , either facing significant collapses or entering administration - mainly driven by mounting bricks-and-mortar retail pressures - there’s never been a more burning time for direct action. Last week saw the British Retail Consortium (BRC) launch its ‘Buy into Retail Manifesto’, calling on Andy Burnham to work with retailers and back reforms to employment costs, business rates, energy, and regulation needed to support an incoming government’s ambition for jobs, growth and a thriving high street. Retailers are clear that such ambitions can only be achieved if businesses have the confidence and certainty to invest in jobs, growth and affordability. That will require greater partnership between the government and businesses, which is something Andy Burnham has promised to address. The BRC says the timing could not be more important, with youth unemployment rising and retailers have a vital role as the first step on the career ladder for almost a quarter of 18-24 year-olds. Retail employs 2.8 million people in every city, town and village, while millions more are employed within its supply chains. Those jobs are essential to deliver growth “in every postcode”, yet rising costs, including a £6.5 billion increase in employment and National Insurance in two years, are putting many jobs at risk, with 400,000 lost in the last decade. Andy Burnham has already begun to outline his focus for the government , including spreading jobs right across the country and reforming business rates. However, the ‘Buy into Retail Manifesto: Jobs, Growth and Affordability’ 10-point plan calls on the government to: 1. Cut the cost of employing young people to create more jobs 2. Deliver employment rights and skills reforms that keep people in work and training 3. Launch a government-retail taskforce to expand routes for young people into employment 4. Get a grip on retail crime - with zero tolerance 5. Fix business rates to unlock investment in high streets and support local jobs 6. Make electricity costs competitive for retailers so consumers don’t pay the price 7. Support investment in retail sites everywhere 8. Keep goods moving freely across borders and ensure fair competition 9. Strip back overlapping regulation that adds to prices 10. Join up government decisions so new costs and rules don’t land at once Helen Dickinson, Chief Executive of the BRC, said: “Retail is where the economy shows up in everyday life. It is where millions of people earn a living. Retail is part of the everyday economy, touching every community across the UK. “When retail thrives, more people are in work, investment flows into local communities, and fierce competition drives prices down for families. But cumulative costs and fragmented policy decisions are holding the industry back. “Retailers have absorbed £6.5 billion in additional employment costs since 2024, as well as billions more in new packaging taxes, business rates, and rising electricity costs. The consequences are clear: fewer jobs, less investment and higher prices for consumers. “Andy Burnham has made collaborating with business to drive growth, high streets, and living standards central to his ambition. Retail is a key partner to deliver it: with the right policies, retail can drive investment, support jobs in every postcode, and keep household essentials affordable. Our manifesto offers a path for Mr Burnham to support the millions of people that rely on retail every day.” Chris Brook-Carter, Chief Executive of the retail industry charity Retail Trust, believes the new Prime Minister should put greater emphasis on the people that work within the retail sector. He commented: “Andy Burnham has said he wants to make UK high streets ‘a symbol of Britain’s renaissance’ and provide greater support for the businesses that bring social value to their local communities. “The retail industry needs decisive leadership, and we hope our new Prime Minister listens carefully to concerns around the burden of business rates and employment costs and also builds on the milestone Crime and Policing Act and the protections this should provide staff. “We fully support his ambitions, but any plan to reinvigorate Britain’s high streets must place the nearly three million people who work in retail at its heart, as their collective wellbeing is fundamental to the energy, identity and economic prosperity of our towns and cities. “There is a plan for the buildings. There needs to be a plan for the people in them. Retail sites and high streets cannot thrive unless the people in them do.” Charlotte Broadbent, UK General Manager at online wholesale marketplace Faire, is another advocate for addressing the broken business rates model. She said: “Independent retailers are often the businesses that bring the most character, footfall and prosperity to our high streets and in a world where so much of daily life happens behind a screen, help make a place feel like somewhere special. “Business rates have been one of independent retailers’ biggest fixed financial burdens, so we fully welcome any support from our new Prime Minster to help bring them down. The shopkeepers using Faire in towns and villages across the country tell me that even modest reductions in their costs could lead to more ambitious and creative product ranges, new jobs and greater investment in their communities. “We would also urge Andy Burnham and local leaders to consider the wider conditions independent shops need to thrive. Whether it be more affordable and accessible parking, stronger support from councils or more investment in town centres, the future success of our high streets will be shaped as much by a strong sense of place as by the costs and strategies of individual businesses.” Last week, the new Real Rates Reform Alliance said Andy Burnham should tax online sales as part of a complete reform of Britain’s “broken and unsustainable” business rates system, as retailers come under increasing strain. The group, which represents more than 28,000 firms and business leaders, wants all online sales taxed at 2%, which it said would allow a 37% cut in business rates for bricks-and-mortar retailers. The alliance believes that would provide a “major shot in the arm” for many high streets and communities which it said have been forced into cutting jobs, investment and raising prices due to the pressures of rising business rate bills.

article_title: M&S appoints new Fashion and Beauty Director of Sourcing, Quality and Sustainability
sub_title: Marks & Spencer has appointed Jane Robson as its new Fashion, Home & Beauty Director of Sourcing, Quality and Sustainability, effective in August.
article_content: Marks and Spencer has appointed Jane Robson as its new Fashion, Home & Beauty Director of Sourcing, Quality and Sustainability, effective in August. Robson has most recently been in the role of Chief Operating Officer at Vogue Sourcing UK, a position she has held since May 2024. Previously she has held the position of Non-Executive Director at Threadbare, and was appointed as Non-Executive Director at Fanfare Label. She also served as Strategic Advisor for My Wardrobe HQ for almost seven years, as well as a Designer Mentor at the British Fashion Council for five years. Earlier roles include that of Managing Director of NEXT Sourcing Limited, from September 2004 to June 2010, based in Hong Kong. Having spent her career reshaping complex international sourcing offices, in her new role Robson will be based at M&S’s Waterside Stores Support Centre. She will start her role with a thorough induction, spending time in M&S stores, sourcing offices and supply base. She will be taking over from Monique Leeuwenburgh, who will be retiring from M&S in October after seven years with the business. On Leeuwenburgh’s pending departure, John Lyttle, Managing Director of M&S, commented: “Monique has been instrumental in shaping our global sourcing strategy, strengthening key supplier partnerships, and leading transformation across our international operations. “Monique is respected across the business for leading with integrity, professionalism, and collaboration, and we thank her for her commitment.” Last week M&S reported it had completed the renewal of its Pantheon flagship store at 173 Oxford Street , bringing food, fashion, home and beauty together across four floors. The store will operate as its first full-line research and development (R&D) site for fashion, home and beauty. The British high street retailer unveiled the Pantheon store’s remaining two upper floors on Monday, 13 July, adding its latest menswear, kidswear, lingerie and home collections to the renewed location. The transformation covers almost 100,000 sq ft and has been completed in stages while the store continued trading. M&S has occupied the building, identified by its green PANTHEON lettering, since 1938. Also last week, M&S revealed it is set to start work on its Marble Arch flagship redevelopment next year.

sub_title: German clog and sandal brand Birkenstock has joined forces with premium French ballet pump maker Repetto on three silhouettes that fuse design elements
article_content: German clog and sandal brand Birkenstock has joined forces with premium French ballet pump maker Repetto on three silhouettes that fuse design elements from both brands’ signature styles. Reinterpreted through Repetto’s refined lens, the iconic Birkenstock ‘Arizona’ sandal comes with exclusive oversized round buckles, lending a sculptural touch to the classic design. Next up is the ‘Scala’, which takes shape with a round toe, two delicate top straps and a graceful laced bow. Completing the trio, the ‘Opéra’ sabot style is adorned with long, fluid laces that wrap gently around the ankle like a dancer’s ribbon. The collection is unified by a Vichy-check footbed lining and all styles come in European sizes 35 to 42 as well as three Repetto-style shades, including pink “to capture the elegance, lightness and spirit of dance”, flame red and black. The collaboration forms part of Birkenstock 1774, the brand’s Paris-based special projects and collaborations unit. Repetto was founded in 1947 a ballet atelier. The house has since evolved into a symbol of French craftsmanship, refinement and innovation.

Zara’s sister brand Lefties confirms late August opening for first UK store
sub_title: Inditex’s budget fashion and lifestyle brand Lefties, a sister brand of Zara and a competitor of Primark, has confirmed it will be opening its first UK store at the Liverpool ONE shopping centre at the end of August 2026.
article_content: Inditex’s budget fashion and lifestyle brand Lefties, a sister brand of Zara and a competitor of Primark, has confirmed it will be opening its first UK store at the Liverpool ONE shopping centre at the end of August 2026. That will be followed by a second UK store at the Lakeside shopping centre in West Thurrock, Essex, in early October, and a third at Gateshead’s Metrocentre in November. Lefties was founded in 1999 and launched its own-brand collections over a decade ago. It has its own headquarters just outside Barcelona, including commercial and design teams, who “aim to bring accessible quality fashion to its customers”. The new Lefties store at the Metrocentre will occupy a central unit at the interchange between Red and Green Mall on Town Square, directly above H Beauty. It will serve as “a key anchor” within Metrocentre’s dedicated fashion offer. Each new Lefties store will utilise technology already used at the retailer’s latest European branches, which includes robots to sort hangers and radio frequency identification self-checkouts in its minimalist stores. Lefties currently operates a total of 215 stores across 19 markets, with the UK set to become its 20th.

article_title: Burberry urges Burnham to restore tax-free shopping to support the North
sub_title: Burberry has urged Prime Minister in waiting Andy Burnham to reinstate tax-free shopping for overseas visitors, arguing the move would help revive luxury
article_content: Burberry has urged Prime Minister in waiting Andy Burnham to reinstate tax-free shopping for overseas visitors, arguing the move would help revive luxury retail spending and strengthen the UK’s fashion industry, including Burberry's northern manufacturing facilities . According to The Telegraph , Burberry CEO Joshua Schulman said the luxury brand’s tourist business has fallen by around 50% since 2019, which he attributed largely to the abolition of the VAT Retail Export Scheme in 2020. The scheme previously allowed international visitors to reclaim VAT on purchases made in the UK before it was scrapped by the Conservative government. Speaking to The Telegraph, Schulman said: “Our tourist business has gone down by 50% since 2019 and that is largely a consequence of the VAT refund scheme.” “We hope to see policies that enable competitiveness and make it more enticing for tourists to come to the UK and spend time in this beautiful country, and of course shop here.” Joshua Schulman, CEO at Burberry He also highlighted Burberry's contribution to the UK economy beyond its London retail presence, pointing to the brand's manufacturing operations in Yorkshire and office in Leeds. "We also have a strong manufacturing presence in Yorkshire and we have a back office facility in Leeds. We are present throughout the country," Schulman told The Telegraph, adding that Burberry was "the only luxury brand of scale to have Britishness at our core". The comments come as Burberry continues its turnaround under Schulman's leadership. In its latest trading update, the luxury house reported retail revenue of £455 million, with sales supported by a 12% increase in the Americas, and improved demand for core categories including outerwear and leather goods. Schulman's remarks also reignite debate over tax-free shopping, with retailers and industry bodies continuing to campaign for the return of the VAT refund scheme. They argue that overseas visitors are increasingly choosing to shop in destinations such as France and Italy, where tax-free purchases remain available. Last year, New West End Company estimated the removal of tax-free shopping resulted in £400 million of unrealised retail sales across London's West End in 2023 alone, despite international visitor numbers recovering. The organisation has continued to call for the policy's reinstatement, arguing it would boost retail, tourism and hospitality while improving the UK's competitiveness as a global shopping destination. Incoming Prime Minister Burnham has also pledged to reform the business rates system , which currently places an unfair burden on retailers given their high street locations.

article_title: Burberry delivers second consecutive quarter of growth as Gen Z and outerwear drive retail sales
sub_title: British luxury brand Burberry delivered a second consecutive quarter of comparable growth as its Burberry Forward plan focused demand on heritage products and expanded its customer base.
article_content: British luxury brand Burberry delivered a second consecutive quarter of comparable growth as its Burberry Forward plan focused demand on heritage products and expanded its customer base. Burberry reported retail revenue of £455 million for the 13 weeks ended 27 June 2026, up 5% from £433 million a year earlier, according to its first-quarter trading update. Off the back of the results the company raised its first-half wholesale guidance. The update comes after the company’s return to profit in the year ended 28 March 2026, when it reported a pre-tax profit of £49 million, compared with a £66 million loss the year before. Chief Executive Joshua Schulman commented on the results saying: “I am pleased with our progress in the first quarter and the momentum we are building with Burberry Forward.” Burberry's Q1 2026 results were defined by stronger trading in the Americas and Greater China, which offset weaker EMEIA sales, which fell 3%, reflecting disruption from the conflict in the Middle East and lower tourist spending. Excluding the Middle East, the region declined 1%. Comparable sales in the Americas meanwhile increased 12%, supported by local demand and customer acquisition. Greater China grew 9%, with Burberry reporting strong growth among Gen Z shoppers. E-commerce sales also increased at a mid-teens rate during the period. Retail sales increased 4% at constant exchange rates, with currency providing a one percentage point boost. Comparable retail sales rose 5%, compared with a 1% decline in the corresponding quarter last year, while the contribution from retail space was negative 1%. The company also increased its wholesale outlook following a positive response from retail partners. It now expects wholesale revenue to grow by a high-single-digit percentage in the first half of FY27. Outerwear sales rose in the double digits, with strong demand across heritage rainwear and lightweight jackets. The Portraits of an Icon campaign helped drive a 19% rise in new rainwear customers. Women’s handbags returned to growth and attracted new customers, while ready-to-wear benefited from demand for knitwear and polos. Burberry saw growth across womenswear, menswear, accessories and childrenswear for the first time in three years. The positive results follow news from earlier this week, when Burberry shareholders approved a revised executive remuneration policy that could raise Schulman’s total package to £12.24 million if maximum performance and share-price conditions are met. The policy passed with 64.6% support and 35.4% opposition. Burberry has also been focusing on fostering future design talent by formalising its partnership with Leeds Beckett University , which gives fashion students access to industry briefs, mentoring and work experience linked to its Yorkshire manufacturing operations.

Nobody’s Child continues UK retail expansion with new store in Cambridge
sub_title: Nobody’s Child is set to open a new 1,000 sq ft store at 3 Grand Arcade in Cambridge next week, marking its 10th UK standalone boutique and its third to open this year.
article_content: Nobody’s Child is set to open a new 1,000 sq ft store at 3 Grand Arcade in Cambridge next week, marking its 10th UK standalone boutique and its third to open this year. The other two store openings of 2026 include openings in Bluewater Shopping Centre and Harrogate. As per other Nobody’s Child stores, the Cambridge space will feature both reclaimed and vintage furniture carefully created by the brand’s in-house team, with the feel of the store designed to be both “timeless and welcoming”. Jody Plows, CEO of Nobody’s Child, said: “Opening our new Cambridge store marks an exciting milestone for Nobody’s Child as we continue to grow our physical retail presence across the UK. “For me personally, it’s especially meaningful to be opening a store in the city where I grew up, and it’s wonderful to bring Nobody’s Child to a place that has always felt like home.” Nobody’s Child has a flagship store at 3 Neal Street in London’s Covent Garden, which opened in August 2024, as well as stores on Carnaby Street, Spitalfields, St Albans, Brighton, Leeds, Windsor, Harrogate and Bluewater Shopping Centre in Kent. Nobody’s Child creates pieces that are as timeless as they are on-trend, offering a mix of minimalist elegance and playful femininity “for women who embrace their own unique style at any age”. Nobody's Child also recently strengthened its senior team with two new appointments spanning merchandising and retail, as the brand continues to grow. The fashion brand, led by CEO Jody Plows, has appointed Jennie Clarke as Head of Merchandising and Amy Boswell as Head of Retail on an interim basis.

article_title: John Lewis partners with RIXO on its biggest fashion collaboration to date
sub_title: Discover the John Lewis x RIXO 44-piece fashion collection. Shop vintage-inspired prints and archival designs starting October 2026.
article_content: John Lewis will launch its largest fashion collaboration to date with British womenswear brand RIXO, bringing a 44-piece, vintage-inspired collection to stores and online from 22 October 2026. The range covers dresses, knitwear, blouses, jackets, skirts, scarves, shoes and bags, giving the collaboration a broader category mix than a conventional occasionwear capsule, with prices starting at £65. The collection is also informed by John Lewis' own archives, marking the first time an archive print has been used in a John Lewis fashion collaboration. The  floral motif was inspired by block-printed textile from 1849 and was discovered during the collaborative design process. The signature print will feature across two dresses, a blouse, skirt and scarf. This marks a big step for RIXO, which has built its womenswear identity around vintage references, distinctive prints and dresses, as it is the first time the brand has collaborated with a retailer on this scale. To date RIXO operates seven standalone stores and has a wholesale network including Liberty London. For John Lewis, the collaboration reinforces its commitment to support British talent, while bolstering its premium brand portfolio. "RIXO is an iconic British brand adored by so many, much like John Lewis, so it felt natural to create something special together," commented Rachel Morgans, Fashion Director at John Lewis on collaboration. RIXO Co-Founder Orlagh McCloskey said: "This collaboration feels like a true extension of RIXO – taking the heritage of John Lewis, leaning into its incredible archive, and bringing it to life with that RIXO magic. "For me, if you’re going to do a collaboration, you have to do it properly. It should feel as strong, if not stronger, than anything you’ve created before – every piece considered, every detail cared for, and something you feel genuinely proud to put your name to. "We wanted the collection to do the talking. We can’t wait to see women across the UK, whether they’re longtime RIXO lovers or discovering us for the first time through John Lewis, style it in their own way and make it theirs. We feel incredibly proud to have created something that reaches a wider audience than our London stores." The collaboration follows RIXO’s spring/summer 2026 collection, We Are One , which marked the brand’s tenth year with bold colour and vintage-influenced prints. That collection also included plans for a capsule reworking designs from the Liberty archive. RIXO also expanded its physical presence at the end of 2025 by opening its seventh store at Bicester Village. The location took its design cues from eclectic English country estates, continuing the historic references seen across the brand’s clothing and retail environments. The full collection will launch simultaneously in stores and online on 22 October.

article_title: Frasers extends Accent Group offer to September with all other terms unchanged
sub_title: Frasers Group has extended its £166 million takeover offer for Australian footwear and lifestyle retailer Accent Group until 30 September, without changing its initial A$0.65-a-share bid.
article_content: Frasers Group has extended its £166 million takeover offer for Australian footwear and lifestyle retailer Accent Group until 30 September, without changing its initial A$0.65-a-share bid. The offer had initially been due to close on 30 July. Accent shareholders now have until the close of ASX (Australian Securities Exchange) trading at 4pm Sydney time on 30 September to sell into the offer, unless Frasers extends or withdraws it. The Sports Direct and Flannels owner said no other terms had changed. Frasers made an unconditional, all-cash bid on 15 June , seeking to acquire every fully paid Accent share outside the holdings it and its associates already have. It held approximately 22.9% of Accent when the offer was announced, making it the Australian company’s largest shareholder. The bid for the remaining shares was valued at approximately A$316 million (£166 million). Accent operates close to 900 stores across Australia and New Zealand, including multi-brand footwear retailer Platypus Shoes, and is Frasers’ partner for the regional Sports Direct rollout. Accent’s Independent Board Committee continues to oppose the offer and has unanimously recommended that shareholders reject it, with t he committee describing the bid as “opportunistic and materially inadequate”. Frasers’ A$0.65 offer matched Accent’s closing share price on 12 June, the final trading day before the bid was announced, and therefore included no premium. Accent also pointed out that Frasers paid A$1.718 per share under a subscription agreement in May 2025. Its on-market buying in February 2026 averaged more than A$0.92 per share. The committee said the bid did not capture Accent’s 2030 Strategic Growth Plan, which has targets of at least A$1.9 billion in sales and an EBIT margin of about 9%. The retailer plans to expand its estate to approximately 950 stores by 2030. The extension follows Frasers lifting its stake in German premium fashion company Hugo Boss to 30.28% two days earlier, a level that took it past the mandatory bid threshold under Germany’s takeover rules. Its €38-per-share Hugo Boss offer remains unchanged, with the initial acceptance period due to end on 27 July. Hugo Boss’ management and supervisory boards have advised shareholders to reject the bid as inadequate. Frasers has previously confirmed that its €38-a-share offer is final . Fraser had been steadily building up its stake in the German luxury brand over the last six years. Frasers has also begun a share buyback programme through newly appointed joint broker Panmure Liberum. Under the arrangement, the broker may acquire up to 10 million Frasers shares for a total of no more than £80 million before the group’s next annual general meeting, expected in mid-September.

article_title: Chanel appoints Hélène de Tissot as new CFO
sub_title: Chanel has appointed Hélène de Tissot as its new Chief Financial Officer, succeeding long-serving finance chief Phillipe Blondiaux as the luxury house continues a broader leadership transition.
article_content: Chanel has appointed Hélène de Tissot as its new Chief Financial Officer, succeeding long-serving Finance Chief Phillipe Blondiaux as the luxury house continues a broader leadership transition. De Tissot will join Chanel in October from French drinks group Pernod Ricard, where she has served as Executive Vice President of Finance & IT since 2018. She brings more than two decades of experience at the company, having previously held senior roles including Group Strategy & M&A Director, Senior Vice President Finance for Asia and Group Tax Director. She succeeds Blondiaux, who announced earlier this month that he would retire at the end of the year after 15 years with Chanel. During his tenure, Blondiaux oversaw a period of significant international expansion and investment across the business. The appointment comes as Chanel enters a new chapter under Global CEO Leena Nair and Artistic Director of Fashion Activities Matthieu Blazy, who joined the house last year. It also follows a return to growth for Chanel . For the year ended 31 December 2025, the luxury house reported revenues of $19.3 billion, up 2% year-on-year, while operating profit increased 5% to $4.7 billion. The company attributed the performance to continued investment in its brand, boutique network and creative strategy, alongside strong momentum across fashion, fragrance and beauty. Prior to joining Pernod Ricard in 2002, de Tissot spent almost nine years as a senior international tax lawyer at Arthur Andersen. She studied at Paris II Panthéon-Assas University, completed postgraduate studies at ESSEC Business School and qualified for the French Bar. De Tissot will take up the role in October, with Blondiaux remaining in post until the end of the year to support the leadership transition. As part of Chanel's continued investment in the future of its brand and people, the luxury brand announced at the beginning of the month that it was acquiring Charvet, the Paris-based, family-run shirtmaker , turning a runway collaboration into an investment in specialist craft under artistic director Matthieu Blazy. Blazy's tenure has already generated visible commercial results. His autumn/winter 2026 show at the Grand Palais in March drew reports of editors and buyers queueing for hours at Chanel's Paris boutiques to secure pieces from his early collections. For the year ended 31 December 2025, the house posted revenue of $19.3 billion , 2% higher than the previous year, while operating profit came in at $4.7 billion.

article_title: Secret Shopper: Reformation brings a digital-first approach to the high street
sub_title: Reformation has come a long way since it began as a vintage clothing boutique in Los Angeles in 2009. The sustainable womenswear brand has grown into a global fashion business, known for its vintage-inspired silhouettes, celebrity following and focus on lower-impact production.
article_content: Reformation has come a long way since it began as a vintage clothing boutique in Los Angeles in 2009. The sustainable womenswear brand has grown into a global fashion business, known for its vintage-inspired silhouettes, celebrity following and focus on lower-impact production. Now preparing to list on the New York Stock Exchange with a target valuation of up to $1bn , the retailer operates more than 70 stores across the US, UK, Canada and France. Since launching its Retail X concept in 2017, Reformation has attempted to merge the convenience of e-commerce with physical retail, using technology to simplify browsing and trying on clothes. TheIndustry.fashion visited its Covent Garden store to find out whether the concept really improves the shopping experience. Located on King Street in the heart of Covent Garden, Reformation sits among luxury fashion retailers, restaurants and independent boutiques. Just around the corner from the Piazza, cheers from the crowds gathered around the street performers remind you that you're shopping in one of London's busiest areas. A velvet rope was set up outside the entrance anticipating crowds, but thankfully there was no queue when I visited on a weekday afternoon. Reformation has built its reputation dressing Instagram's cool girls, but inside I found a much broader range of shoppers. There was a mix of Londoners, tourists, a man in a suit stopping by after work and two children playing on their phones while their family members tried things on. Like the brand itself, the exterior is understated. Large windows allow passers-by to see straight into the minimalist space and there are just a couple of mannequins showcasing simple outfits. A security guard welcomed every customer before giving us a small card with a QR code. At first, I wasn't entirely sure why. It wasn't immediately obvious that this was how you joined the virtual fitting room queue, and without a brief explanation it could easily be mistaken for a piece of marketing. Five members of staff moved around the shop floor, dressed in their own clothes rather than uniforms, but their earpieces helpfully gave away who actually worked there. They were friendly and approachable, checking whether shoppers wanted to try anything on without being overly pushy. My first impression was just how little product there appeared to be. In most cases, there is just one item of each design on display, giving the feel of a carefully curated showroom rather than a traditional high street store. At first, it felt too limited, but the staff quickly explained that additional sizes were held in the stockroom. Warm lighting and generous spacing between displays create a calm shopping environment, while indie music quietly plays in the background. During London’s July heatwave, the air conditioning was rather welcome and made it easy to spend longer browsing. I gravitated towards the summer dresses, unable to face trying on anything heavier. With many dresses sitting around the £200 mark, this isn't a brand built around impulse purchases. The quality largely reflects those prices too. Fabrics felt substantial, the construction appeared well finished and the pieces looked every bit as polished in person as they do online. I was told there would be a 20 to 25-minute wait for a fitting room but it ended up being around half an hour. I managed to grab a seat on one of the sofas while I waited, but others weren’t so fortunate. Several customers left before their names were called, leaving staff calling for them across the shop floor. It wasn't quite the seamless experience the technology promises. Once it was my turn, it became clear that the fitting rooms are meant to be the selling point of the entire store. Each changing room features a touchscreen displaying every item currently available in-store, along with every available colour and size. Until this point, first-time visitors could easily assume the product selection is much smaller than it actually is. Rather than getting dressed again and hunting through the store, you can tap the item you want and continue trying things on while a member of staff retrieves it. I requested a top I had seen on Reformation’s Instagram and it arrived within a couple of minutes. I also used the touchscreen to request a couple of items I hadn't spotted on the shop floor, which proved genuinely useful. That said, the system isn't perfect. Because shoppers can keep requesting additional items without ever leaving their fitting room, it's easy to see why waiting times begin to build. While the technology improves the experience once you're inside, it arguably creates a bottleneck for everyone still waiting outside. Reformation's technology genuinely improves the fitting room experience and makes it far easier to browse the full collection than in a traditional store. However, the lengthy wait, digital requests and staff ferrying garments between the stockroom and changing rooms suggest the system may struggle during busier periods. While the technology is useful, it gives the shopping experience an almost industrial feel that is slightly at odds with the sense of luxury the brand's price point suggests. I left empty-handed, not because I couldn't find anything I liked. The dresses were flattering, well made and true to size. They simply sat outside my budget. For shoppers willing to spend £200 to £300 on a dress, Reformation offers one of the most innovative retail concepts on the high street, even if the reality feels a little less effortless than the brand's carefully curated online image suggests.

article_title: Temperley London appoints new CEO and Design Director
sub_title: British luxury house Temperley London has appointed Morgaine McGee as Chief Executive Officer and Jack Isenberg as Design Director, completing its leadership team ahead of a new collection in September.
article_content: British luxury house Temperley London has appointed Morgaine McGee as Chief Executive Officer and Jack Isenberg as Design Director, completing its leadership team ahead of a new collection in September. The appointments follow the departure of founder and Creative Director Alice Temperley earlier this month. McGee replaces Sarita Jha, whose tenure as Interim CEO recently ended, while Isenberg will lead the house's design direction. Founded in 2000, Temperley London is known for hand embroidery and occasionwear. The London-headquartered business sells internationally through its stores, e-commerce operation and wholesale partners. McGee brings more than two decades of experience across apparel and accessories, including responsibility for design, product development, production and operations. Her previous senior leadership positions include Co-Chief Executive Officer of product development and manufacturing business The Vertical Collective, which she co-founded. and Managing Director of accessories company Signal Brands. Earlier in her career, she worked at RT Sourcing USA on design and product development for luxury houses including Dior, Chanel and Givenchy. McGee said: “This marks an exciting new chapter for Temperley London as we bring a fresh perspective to the brand, while honouring its legacy, our rich British heritage as well as our commitment to exceptional craftsmanship.” "The brand has created timeless pieces, beautifully created to celebrate women and the moments that shape their lives. I am aware of that history, what people expect of the brand and will work to ensure that continues." Isenberg joins Temperley London from Tom Ford after a career spanning luxury ready-to-wear and couture. A Central Saint Martins graduate, he began his career at Valentino and later held senior design positions at Giambattista Valli, Versace and Nina Ricci. He also held the positions of Head Designer at Ralph & Russo and Design Director at Jenny Packham. “What drew me to this house is its commitment to craft. The embroidery, the finishing. These are things that can only be done by people who know how,” Isenberg said. "It has been great to start working with the talented team here and continuing to bring the quality and craftsmanship that women across the world have come to expect from Temperley London." His first collection for the brand will be presented in September. The leadership changes come two and a half years after Times Square Group LLC and its investment arm, Luxutte Capital, took a majority stake in Temperley London in November 2023 . Alice Temperley and then-CEO Luca Donnini stayed in their roles at first after that deal. When confirming her departure on 8 July, Alice Temperley said the company had been her creative home for more than two decades. She plans to establish an independent creative practice, with further details to be announced.

article_title: Show report: The word from the stands at Scoop
sub_title: Yesterday, 21 July, saw a circus-themed Scoop wrap after three days at Olympia National in London. For many exhibitors, it certainly delivered, with buyers from stores including Fenwick and Liberty London, hungry to seek out fresh brands.
article_content: Yesterday, 21 July, saw a circus-themed Scoop wrap after three days at Olympia National in London. For many exhibitors, it certainly delivered, with buyers from stores including Fenwick, Liberty London, Cream, The Dressing Room, Pamela Schiffer, Cordelia James, Galeries Lafayette in France and El Corte Ingles in Spain hungry to seek out fresh brands – many new to the show – and standout SS27 collections. TheIndustry.fashion went along to get the word from the big top. Eva Panagiotopoulou, from Come What May I’m based in Athens, Greece, and Come What May is brand new. Scoop is the first time it’s been shown to buyers. I’ve been in the business for almost 30 years as a wholesaler, buyer, stylist and then as a designer for other brands for the past 10 years. Then I decided to create my own ready-to-wear brand. I came up with the idea to make luxury resort wear when I first saw the fabrics this collection has been created from. They are hand block printed and very unique. I loved them as soon as I saw them and I thought they would be perfect to create mix and match pieces. The colours are really beautiful, with stripes and prints as well as monochrome options. In terms of key pieces, we have very nice dresses which work from day to night, as well as kimonos, oversized blouses with voluminous sleeves, wraparound skirts, shirts and wide leg trousers that can be matched together or worn separately. The fabric is a modal satin, it’s not that expensive but it feels like silk. It just feels really nice when you wear it. We’ve had a good reaction to it at the show. It’s been very interesting because people haven’t seen anything else quite like this. That has pleased me as I wanted to do something different. We’re happy that we have seen some buyers we expected to see at the show, including those who have their own boutiques, and we have made some contacts regarding possible agents and distributors for the UK market. Nichola Morgan, showing Devotion Twins Devotion Twins is a Greek brand that’s celebrating its 25th anniversary this year. It’s developed from being very much a resort wear brand into a full ready-to-wear collection. It’s very contemporary with a lot of natural fabrics and real Greek heritage coming through in terms of silhouettes. It’s been in the UK market for 10 years now and we’ve been showing it at Scoop since about 2022. It’s very much a summer collection, but as we go further into ready-to-wear the autumn/winter collections will start to get stronger. We currently have around 25-30 UK accounts, including Daniel of Windsor, Brown Thomas, Very and Monsoon. Liberty has been on today and we’d obviously love to get it in there. We’ve been in Selfridges in the past and, where the brand has evolved from a certain look, we are hoping to get such stores back on board. The show has been fantastic for us. It’s been very busy, particularly straight off the bat for the first two days. We’ve taken on nine new accounts and previous accounts, who thought they might not do the brand any more, have seen the newness and come back. We’ve been writing orders, which is always a positive. After the show, we will have the collection at the Morris Fyfe showroom on Brick Lane in London, where we have another six brands including Sorena handbags and accessories, also from Greece, Emily Lovelock and Valentino handbags and shoes. Devotion Twins is the only one we’ve brought to Scoop. It’s the perfect platform for it because it attracts exactly the right audience. Stephanie Krausch from Chicosoleil I established Chicosoleil 14 years ago with my husband in Paris. It’s very much about the spirit of summer. We do a lot of trade shows and we sell the collection around the world as a result. My husband is currently showing it in Japan and, after the final day of Scoop, I will be travelling to Madrid to show it there, then at the end of September I will be showing in Milan. Having previously shown Chicosoleil at Pure London, I started with Scoop two years ago. It has been great and I am very happy with the response from customers. We currently sell to about 25 UK accounts, including Cleverly Wrapped and other independent boutiques, and we have had success with taking on some new accounts here. The collection is made in India, so my life is split between Paris and there as I manage all the design and production myself. The new collection features handloom fabrics, embroidery, embellishments and signature details such as coloured buttons in the shape of a flower. A key piece is an oversized shirt dress that can be belted in. There’s check and striped versions and it’s a very easy to wear on-trend summer style. We’re showing a collection for April/May 2027 delivery, including standout cotton/viscose fabric pieces with a ‘midnight diamond’ print, as well as a high summer 2027 collection. I always enjoy coming to London and showing at Scoop. Even if my English is not great, I can speak face-to-face with my customers and get a better understanding of what they want. So, it’s very important for me to come. Lea Wu, from Labdip We started the Labdip brand in 2012 in Paris, but my brother and I came into this market because our father was a denim manufacturer for other brands. He knew all about the fits and washes and we learned alongside him. We manufacture in a region next to Shanghai in China. We used to have a factory, but since my father retired the person working with him took it over – so we have continuity. The factory specialises in different denim washes. This is our first time at Scoop and we have managed to take some orders, including from Cordelia James which has three stores (in Hawkhurst, Rye and Lewes), as well as a store in Scotland and one in Ireland. We already work with Mercantile London as well as Ediit, which has two stores in London. We also came here to meet some agents, and we’ve had some interest from local partners, so we are happy. Karen Radley from Scoop has been helping a lot with some matchmaking! Our barrel fit jean is a trending silhouette for women and is currently our best-selling jean, particularly with a natural worn in look, not overdone. We also have a popular relaxed fit wide-leg style with a slightly lower waist. It has a real 90s feel to it. The collection reflects American denim history as we also have a very 70s style flared jean with two front patch pockets. That one is new and is all about really lengthening the silhouette. We have big hopes for that one. We’re also doing some coloured washes, such as dusty pink in the barrel leg which is proving very popular. Straight leg jeans are also coming back, so we have a selection of washes in that fit too, including a stonewash/snow wash combination. Complementing the denim, we have other pieces such as a western style suede shirt which again comes in a dusty pink as well as olive. We’ve also really been inspired by American college looks and we have raglan sleeve two-colour baseball style long-sleeved T-shirts, as well as bandanas and military influenced lightweight nylon long shorts – perfect for the warm weather. Valentine Urso, from Opalina It’s our first showing for the UK market and we are forming part of the Italian Trade Agency presence at Scoop. Opalina is a three-year old brand born out of a factory originally established in 1954 in Puglia. I’d previously worked for over 10 years behind the scenes in the production for other brands, but I always wanted to hone my own vision and use my creativity. I saw the women working at the factory on the old machines and my vision began to take shape for what I wanted the brand to look like. We do have dresses and skirts, but Opalina is primarily a brand that focuses on a modern interpretation of a shirt for women. So, when we’re talking about the key pieces it is really about the shirting which has had something added to it, such as ruffle fronts, embroidery, pleating on the shoulder and puff sleeves. It’s about something that is comfortable, versatile and elegant all in one, using high quality fabrics and natural fibres. One of the key pieces is a lightweight muslin cotton shirt, which is a reinterpretation of a men’s tuxedo shirt design. Instead of vertical pleats it features handmade ruffles on the front. It comes in yellow, which is a strong colour for the SS27 season. We’ve also got classic relaxed fit striped shirts with dropped shoulders and three-quarter length sleeves and plenty of Liberty print fabrics as well, which I love, including for a long skirt. Scoop has been a very important show for us to attend, and we are very happy with the contacts we have made. It’s been a great experience for us, particularly as a young brand. We will come back.

article_title: Dior to stage its first Ireland show at Trinity College Dublin
sub_title: Dior will stage its pre-fall 2027 show at Trinity College Dublin on 4 December 2026, marking the French fashion house’s first runway presentation in Ireland.
article_content: Dior will stage its pre-fall 2027 show at Trinity College Dublin on 4 December 2026, marking the French fashion house’s first runway presentation in Ireland. Jonathan Anderson will unveil the collection at the university’s Old Library. The event will also be the Northern Irish designer’s first fashion show in the country. Dior said: “The collection will be unveiled against the backdrop of the university’s Old Library, an 18th-century building housing a world-class academic and cultural resource.” The Dublin presentation follows Anderson’s Dior autumn/winter 2026/27 haute couture show in Paris . Since taking creative control of the house’s menswear, womenswear and couture divisions, he has become the first designer since Christian Dior to oversee all three. Anderson presented his first Dior haute couture collection at Paris Couture Week in January 2026 . The show brings Anderson back to the city where he started working in fashion. His first role in the industry was at Dublin department store Brown Thomas, while his J.W. Anderson label has previously collaborated with Irish brewer Guinness. In a social media post Anderson shared that he was "so excited and so proud" to be able to show the collection at Ireland's oldest university. "Showing at Trinity College Dublin is a dream come true. I began my career in fashion in Dublin, so returning here feels deeply personal," he added. "To present this collection in such an extraordinary setting – at an institution with such an important cultural history – is a real honour." The Old Library is set for its first major renovation in over 300 years. Trinity College’s redevelopment timetable says the building and its Long Room will remain open to visitors until the end of 2027, when restoration and construction work is scheduled to begin. The project covers structural and environmental upgrades alongside the conservation of the building, manuscripts and research collections. It will also create a Research Collections Study Centre and redesign the exhibition of the library’s treasures. The December runway marks a change from Dior’s pre-fall format under Anderson’s predecessor, Maria Grazia Chiuri. During her tenure, the house released its pre-fall collections through look books in December before staging travelling runway shows around their arrival in stores. Dior’s last pre-fall runway presentation took place in Kyoto in April 2025. The house has not provided a reason for the scheduling change. The Dublin location also links Dior to Carmel Snow, the Dublin-born former editor-in-chief of the US edition of Harper’s Bazaar. According to the Women’s Museum of Ireland, Snow came up with the term 'New Look' after she saw Christian Dior’s debut collection in 1947. Anderson’s save-the-date combines Snow’s description of Dior’s work with a four-leaf clover, an emblem the designer has used during his tenure at the house.

article_title: Mulberry cuts losses as turnaround strategy gains momentum
sub_title: Mulberry has significantly reduced its losses and returned to growth in its latest financial year, as the British luxury brand's turnaround strategy continued to gain momentum.
article_content: Mulberry has significantly reduced its losses and returned to growth in its latest financial year, as the British luxury brand's turnaround strategy continued to gain momentum. For the 52 weeks to 28 March 2026, Mulberry reported a loss before tax of £8.9 million, compared with £32.2 million the previous year. Underlying losses narrowed to £8 million from £24.1 million, while the business returned to positive underlying EBITDA of £0.8 million, an improvement of £17.6 million year on year. Group revenue increased 4% to £125.5 million, with growth accelerating in the second half of the year. Retail and digital like-for-like sales rose 9%, while gross margin improved from 67% to 72% as Mulberry focused on full-price trading and reduced promotional activity. The improvement comes as Mulberry continues to execute its "Back to the Mulberry Spirit" strategy under CEO Andrea Baldo, focusing on restoring profitability through stronger full-price trading, reduced promotional activity and renewed investment in the brand. Baldo said: "We returned the business to growth, significantly reduced our losses and strengthened gross margin through greater full-price discipline. Momentum built throughout the year, with a particularly strong second half, demonstrating that the actions we have taken are delivering tangible results." The retailer also reported a strong start to the new financial year, with group revenue rising 23% in the first 13 weeks to 27 June 2026. Retail and digital sales increased 18%, supported by double-digit like-for-like growth across all regions. The latest results build on the progress outlined in Mulberry's trading update earlier this year , when the company reported improving sales across all of its key markets as its turnaround strategy gained traction. They also follow the appointment of Christopher Kane as Ready-to-Wear Creative Director and the brand's planned return to London Fashion Week in September, marking a renewed focus on strengthening its creative credentials. Looking ahead, Mulberry said it remains focused on delivering sustainable long-term growth, with a medium-term target of generating more than £200 million in annual revenue alongside a 15% EBIT margin.

Clothing prices fall 0.5% in June as retail competition holds down prices
sub_title: ONS data showed clothing and footwear prices fell 0.5% in June after rising 0.2% in May, as supermarket competition and summer promotions helped limit price rises, although retailers continue to face pressure from employment, packaging and energy costs.
article_content: ONS data showed clothing and footwear prices fell 0.5 % in June after rising 0.2% in May, as supermarket competition and summer promotions helped limit price rises, although retailers continue to face pressure from employment, packaging and energy costs. The Consumer Prices Index rose by 2.6% in the 12 months to June 2026, down from 2.8% in May, according to figures released by the Office for National Statistics today. Inflation remains above the Bank of England’s 2% target. Harvir Dhillon, Economist at the British Retail Consortium, commented: “Retailers are already facing immense financial pressure, squeezed by higher National Insurance, the triple packaging tax, and other input cost increases tied to the conflict in Iran. "If retailers are to keep prices affordable for consumers in the long run, the Government needs to take practical steps to lower the everyday cost of doing business. "Andy Burnham has taken immediate action to ease pressure on household budgets; he must now look to do the same for businesses, by cutting non-commodity charges on energy, and reducing the employment cost burden to help tackle the youth unemployment crisis.” The latest figures follow a sustained period of discounting across food and non-food categories. Shop price inflation remained at 1.2% in June , with retailers promoting clothing, footwear and lighter household textiles in response to hot weather. Food shop-price inflation fell from 2.7% in May to 2.4% in early June, while non-food inflation edged up from 0.5% to 0.6%. Promotions also supported demand. Barclays data covering 23 May to 19 June showed clothing spending increased by 2.4% year on year , while clothing transactions rose by 3.5%. Department-store spending climbed 9.7%. Total UK card spending grew by 1.9%, improving from 0.8% in May but remaining below the CPIH inflation rate recorded for that month. The BRC said retailers were being squeezed by higher employer National Insurance contributions and more than £2 billion in annual packaging-related charges. The organisation has also linked higher production, shipping and distribution costs to the conflict in Iran. Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced his first household cost-of-living measure on 21 July, cutting VAT on domestic electricity from 5% to zero from 1 October. The policy is expected to reduce the average household electricity bill by about £45 a year. The BRC said comparable action for businesses would help retailers keep prices affordable over time. The next official UK inflation figures are scheduled for 19 August.

article_title: Never Fully Dressed sells stake to Refined Capital Partners
sub_title: Contemporary womenswear brand Never Fully Dressed (NFD) has sold a stake in the business to Refined Capital Partners, the London-based private equity and venture capital firm.
article_content: Contemporary womenswear brand Never Fully Dressed (NFD) has sold a stake in the business to Refined Capital Partners, the London-based private equity and venture capital firm, to support its continued growth. The transaction completed on 15 July 2026, and financial terms were not disclosed. According the brand it marks an exciting milestone, bringing together long-term investment and strategic support to support future growth for the business. Up until Refined Capital Partners acquired a stake in the brand, Founder Lucy Aylen held full ownership of the company. Following the transaction, Aylen ceased to be registered as a person with significant control of the company, according to filings on Companies House. According to the brand this does not change her position within the company, however. In a statement the brand specified that it remained the "same female-founded brand, led by the same leadership team, designing every print in-house with the same passion, creativity and attention to detail." Aylen is also still listed as CEO of the company on NFD's website and in her biography on LinkedIn. Nfd Holdco Limited became the company’s new person with significant control, according to Company House filings, which were published on 20 July. Nfd Holdco was incorporated in London on 18 May 2026 and lists Refined Capital Partners Founding Partner Benjamin Barnett as a Director. Barnett was also appointed to the Never Fully Dressed board on 15 July. Refined Capital Partners Founding Partner Anastasia Fadeeva and investor Helgi Thor Bergs joined the business as Directors at the same time. The published filings do not specify the percentage acquired, although it states that the relevant legal entity holds, directly or indirectly, 75% or more of the shares  and voting rights in the company. Aylen founded Never Fully Dressed in 2009, initially operating the label from her parents’ attic. The business now sells through its own website and stores in Essex and New York, alongside wholesale partners including John Lewis, Frasers and Harvey Nichols. "This partnership gives us the opportunity to invest in the future of Never Fully Dressed and our continued commitment to do better for our people and planet. We’ll continue to be open, honest and transparent as we grow, listening to our community every step of the way," Never Fully Dressed added in the statement. Refined Capital Partners provides growth funding and operational support to consumer brands and retail technology businesses. Its stated investment model covers transactions of between £5 million and £25 million, although that range does not confirm the value of the Never Fully Dressed deal. Recently, the firm also invested £4.75 million in British luxury womenswear brand The Fold London. It also owns a minority holding in Disturbia, a fashion and lifestyle brand, which has been expanding in the US. Its wider fashion portfolio includes Celtic & Co and childrenswear brand Frugi. Refined Capital also backs Kettlewell Colours and recycled cashmere specialist Turtle Doves. Barnett previously led Phase Eight through its £238 million sale to South African retail group TFG in 2015. Refined Capital's other Founding Partner Fadeeva also held senior finance and operations roles across TFG London, including at Hobbs, before the pair established Refined Capital Partners.
