Heatwave drives online retail sales as shoppers avoid stores
sub_title: UK retail sales increased 1.9% year-on-year in June as the heatwave prompted more shoppers to buy online, according to the latest BRC-KPMG Retail Sales Monitor.
article_content: UK retail sales increased 1.9% year-on-year in June as the heatwave prompted more shoppers to buy online, according to the latest BRC-KPMG Retail Sales Monitor. The figures, covering the five weeks from 31 May to 4 July, showed that online non-food sales increased 5.1% year-on-year, with 39% of non-food purchases made online, up from 37.7% in June 2025 and above the 12-month average. Meanwhile, in-store non-food sales fell 1.1% year-on-year, despite overall non-food sales increasing 1.2%. Helen Dickinson, Chief Executive of the British Retail Consortium, said: “Retail sales maintained momentum despite June’s heatwave. While in-store sales were stifled by soaring temperatures, the proportion of sales online was the highest of 2026, bolstered by well-timed promotions. "Electric fans and paddling pools performed well, as people looked to cool off, while the lure of the sunshine meant that gaming and big-ticket sales struggled. The heatwave doesn't just change how customers shop - it makes retail operations more challenging, from keeping shelves stocked to keeping products and people cool." Linda Ellett, UK Head of Consumer, Retail & Leisure at KPMG, said: "Demand for fans and air con units helped drive up home appliance sales, with some retailers struggling to restock fast enough, while the men’s football World Cup also brought a boost for home electrical sales and food and drink. "As the summer holiday season gets set to fully begin, retailers will be looking to build on the increase in clothing sales for both adults and children that was seen during June." Sarah Bradbury, CEO of IGD, said June’s record-breaking heat, easing food price inflation and the start of the World Cup encouraged more frequent top-up shopping trips. She added: "With both the warm weather and football tournament continuing this month, consumer confidence could receive a further uplift." The latest figures highlight the contrast between physical and online retail during June, with the heatwave accelerating digital shopping while challenging store performance. As retailers head further into the summer, many will be looking to build on online momentum while capitalising on seasonal demand for clothing, home and leisure categories. Separate data from Barclays showed consumer card spending grew 1.9% year-on-year in June, with a 1.7% increase in non-essential spending driven by a combination of stabilising consumer confidence, warm weather and the arrival of the World Cup. Jack Meaning, Chief UK Economist at Barclays, said: “While additional spending around the World Cup will be a welcome cushion for the hospitality sector, it remains true that the economy has slowed into the middle of the year. “Looking ahead to the second half of 2026, we expect growth to pick up modestly, as improving consumer sentiment and reduced uncertainty are partially offset by the temporary inflation bump.”

article_title: In Pictures: Marella’s new ‘Hero Blazer’ launching for AW26
sub_title: Contemporary Italian womenswear brand Marella is launching a single-breasted ‘Hero Blazer’ for AW26 with a campaign fronted by model Irina Shayk.
article_content: Contemporary Italian womenswear brand Marella is launching a single-breasted ‘Hero Blazer’ for AW26 with a campaign fronted by model Irina Shayk. The new signature tailoring piece is the focal point of the brand’s upcoming AW26 collection and is “designed to be worn as a second skin”, combining Italian craftsmanship with “effortless versatility”, making it a true wardrobe investment piece. A standout feature is a removable scarf, a distinctive detail that “introduces a gesture of lightness into the blazer’s construction”. Crafted in the same fabric as the garment or in a coordinating material, the scarf flows along the silhouette, amplifying its movement and adding a fluid, three-dimensional structure to the design. The blazer takes shape through various material interpretations that amplify its character. From the most essential version, offered in the timeless shades of black, white and camel, to the velvet variant with a silk habotai scarf embellished with lace inlays, through to the leather version completed by a silk twill scarf. Model Irina Shayk embodies the essence of the new Marella ‘Hero Blazer’ with her “magnetic presence and intense allure”. Marella was founded in Reggio Emilia, Italy, in 1971 and is a subsidiary of the Max Mara Fashion Group. Earlier this year, the brand opened its first standalone store in London at 8 Marylebone High Street . The 1,410-square-foot boutique is designed to reflect a modern Italian aesthetic, combining clean architectural lines with softer, understated elements. The opening marked a prominent step in Marella’s international expansion, adding to its more than 200 standalone stores. Other recent expansion efforts have included new openings in cities such as Paris and Munich. Marella’s collections are also available through its website and selected UK retailers, including Harrods, Harvey Nichols and John Lewis.

article_title: Lululemon launches padel pop-up at Manchester’s Trafford Centre
sub_title: Lululemon has launched a two-week padel pop-up at Manchester’s Trafford Centre to coincide with the opening of its expanded store, as retailers increasingly look beyond traditional shopping experiences to engage with consumers.
article_content: Lululemon has launched a two-week padel pop-up at Manchester’s Trafford Centre to coincide with the opening of its expanded store, as retailers increasingly look beyond traditional shopping experiences to engage with consumers. Running until 23 July, the Lululemon x Trafford Centre padel court invites visitors to book one-hour sessions, tapping into the growing popularity of the sport while encouraging shoppers to spend longer at the destination. A post shared by Trafford Centre (@thetraffordcentre) The activation accompanies the opening of Lululemon’s new 3,700 sq ft store, more than doubling the brand’s footprint at the shopping centre. Manchester is one of the UK’s strongest athleisure markets, while Greater Manchester has also emerged as one of the country’s fastest-growing regions for padel, making the location a natural fit for the initiative. Kate Pearson, Portfolio Leasing Director at Pradera, said: “Today’s consumers are looking for more than just a day of shopping; they’re seeking memorable experiences.” “Partnering with lululemon to bring this premium padel activation to Trafford Centre is a fantastic example of how brands and destinations can work together to create something genuinely engaging. As we continue to evolve our retail and leisure offering, experiences like this play an important role in attracting visitors and encouraging longer stays.” Visitors can book the court through the Playtomic app, with sessions available daily until the activation ends on 23 July. The launch reflects a broader shift towards experience-led retail, with brands increasingly using sport, wellness and cultural moments to create reasons for consumers to visit physical stores.

article_title: H&M teases new vision for runway ahead of London Fashion Week return
sub_title: The fashion brand is promising a new runway format for September, building on last year’s participatory London presentation while leaving its production plans under wraps.
article_content: H&M will return to London Fashion Week on 17 September 2026, partnering with photographer Nick Knight and digital fashion platform SHOWstudio to reconsider how a runway show can work. The fashion brand said the presentation would explore self-expression, human connection, creative innovation and wider access to fashion. WWD first reported the announcement, with H&M describing the event as a departure from its previous London show. At H&M, Ann-Sofie Johansson, Creative Adviser and Head of Design for Womenswear, said: “Our 2025 London Fashion Week event was a defining moment for the brand, so we are excited to be returning to the schedule to shake things up again.” Johansson said London’s position as a creative hub, along with the support of the British Fashion Council, contributed to H&M’s decision to return. The show will form part of the Spring 2027 schedule alongside brands including Mulberry and Alexander McQueen. It will also coincide with Marks & Spencer’s London Fashion Week runway debut this autumn, where the retailer will unveil a shoppable womenswear and menswear collection that customers can buy immediately online, in flagship UK stores and across key international markets. The debut coincides with the British retailer’s 100th year in the fashion industry. H&M’s September 2025 presentation at 180 Strand combined a catwalk with music, performance, styling and audience participation. The event unfolded across three acts and concluded with a performance by South London musician Lola Young. Seating 700 guests, the activation was part runway, part concert, part living magazine. Set in the architecturally striking courtyard of the 180 complex, models were surrounded by monumental screens and a dynamic soundscape, bringing energy and movement to disrupt the expected catwalk experience. The earlier show also used a see-now-buy-now model, with selected pieces made available online immediately and the remaining collection released later in the season. H&M said its 2026 presentation would adopt a different format, although it has not disclosed how the commercial element will operate. Knight said the runway “needs to constantly change and push creative boundaries”, adding that the partnership would explore new ways of presenting fashion while “asking questions of what a runway show can be.” SHOWstudio was founded by Knight in 2000 as an online fashion platform. According to the company, its work has explored digital forms of fashion communication, including fashion films, live-streamed runway shows and photo shoots, 3D imaging, avatar creation, artificial intelligence and interactive projects.

article_title: Slazenger unveils second ‘Off-Court’ collection and debuts womenswear
sub_title: Heritage British sports brand Slazenger has launched its second, more premium ‘Off-Court’ collection, also introducing womenswear for the first time.
article_content: Heritage British sports brand Slazenger, which was acquired by Frasers Group (formerly Sports Direct International) in 2004, has launched its second, more premium ‘Off-Court’ collection, also introducing womenswear for the first time. Drawing inspiration from Slazenger’s archives spanning tennis and golf, the collection reimagines Slazenger’s heritage through modern silhouettes under the guidance of TikToker-turned-Slazenger Creative Director Alexei Hamblin. Hamblin, 23, was brought to the attention of Slazenger and Michael Murray, CEO at Frasers Group, following the TikToker’s TT series in which he had been critiquing the brand for how it had gone downhill since its days as a leading British sports brand. Known in the TikTok world as ‘The Slazenger Guy’, he was then brought in “behind the scenes” to steer the brand towards a vision that feels relevant to Gen Z, before recently being appointed the brand’s Creative Director. Following the debut of Off-Court in April 2026, the new 14-piece collection, which is now exclusively available in-store at Flannels X on Oxford Street, as well as on both the Slazenger and Flannels websites, features Off-Court’s signature rich burgundies, navy and cream tones, with traditional plaid accents and houndstooth patterns throughout. The debut womenswear offering includes a knitted tennis dress, a contemporary interpretation of the traditional golf V-neck sweater, a ‘skort’ and a selection of elevated summer essentials. Meanwhile, the menswear collection expands on the design language established in the first capsule, featuring a terrace-inspired track jacket, Bermuda-style denim shorts and graphic shirts. The hero piece for the summer capsule is the ‘Back Page Woven Shirt’, featuring a cropped cut and old Slazenger newspaper advertisements to bring the brand’s rich history to life. Hamblin said: “This collection is where we really started digging into the depth of Slazenger's archive. Beyond tennis, the brand has such an incredible history across British sport, and we wanted to celebrate that while introducing new product categories and womenswear for the first time. “Every piece feels nostalgic but still really wearable today, and I'm excited to be bringing Off-Court back with a bang.” Continuing Off-Court's commitment to making premium design more accessible, the collection is priced between £40 and £90, combining “elevated fabrics, thoughtful detailing and fashion-led silhouettes” without compromising on offering customers good value. Last week saw Slazenger launch a new Summer 2026 video campaign in which Hamblin and Slazenger’s Head of Marketing, Joel Taberner, attempt to break the 11-hour, 5-minute record for the longest tennis match in history, set in 2010. Both the regular Slazenger performance range and Off-Court pieces feature in the video.

article_title: Marks & Spencer completes Pantheon flagship transformation and begins format test
sub_title: The nearly 100,000 sq ft Oxford Street site will trial new approaches to merchandising and customer service before successful features are introduced elsewhere.
article_content: Marks & Spencer has completed the renewal of its flagship at 173 Oxford Street, bringing Food, Fashion, Home and Beauty together across four floors. The store will operate as its first full-line research-and-development site for Fashion, Home and Beauty. The British high street retailer unveiled the Pantheon store’s remaining two upper floors on Monday, 13 July, adding its latest Menswear, Kidswear, Lingerie and Home collections to the renewed location. The transformation covers almost 100,000 sq ft and has been completed in stages while the store continued trading. M&S has occupied the building, identified by its green PANTHEON lettering, since 1938. Marks & Spencer CEO Stuart Machin said: “Pantheon on Oxford Street, where we’ve had a store since 1938, is our first full-line flagship and our R&D store for Fashion, Home and Beauty.” M&S has completely renewed the Fashion, Home and Beauty floors with a concept designed to test how customers navigate and shop its ranges. Successful features are intended to be introduced across the wider estate over time. Collections are arranged in dedicated rooms, with clearer zoning and architectural features separating product categories. The design combines ambient lighting, M&S heritage green, warm neutral tones, bespoke scents and curated playlists. Digital screens provide outfit inspiration, while product displays have been simplified to make ranges easier to browse. Integrated Click & Collect and payment facilities are designed to link online ordering with store visits. Pantheon also introduces a made-to-order suiting service, which M&S describes as a first for its menswear business. Customers can create a bespoke suit in store, supported by fitting and alteration services. Other category spaces include a dedicated Body Shop lingerie room, a Babywear room and a Beauty Hall carrying M&S ranges alongside third-party labels, including K-Beauty brands. Home contains a dedicated M&S x Kelly Hoppen edit within a space designed by the interior designer. The official Pantheon store listing also includes self-service collection and returns kiosks, personal suit fittings, bra-fitting services and tax-free shopping among the available facilities. M&S completed the project department by department while keeping the flagship open. The renewed 19,400 sq ft lower-ground Foodhall opened in August 2025, followed by Womenswear and Beauty in January 2026. The market-style Foodhall includes a Pizza Bar using hand-stretched sourdough bases, a Hot Chicken Counter, an in-store bakery and a dedicated Wine Shop. A coffee shop and British-inspired gifting area extend the food offer beyond grocery shopping. That format provides the model for the work now taking place across other departments. M&S began testing its modern Food format at Clapham St John’s Road in 2019 and has since renewed 160 Food stores. “In 2019, we built the blueprint to modernise our Food business, with a new food format designed to capture the soul of a fresh market,” Machin said. “Now we’re taking that same approach into Fashion, Home and Beauty.” Pantheon is one of six London stores that M&S plans to renew during the current financial year, alongside four new openings in the capital. Across the UK, the retailer is planning two new full-line stores, 18 new Food stores, four extensions and further renewals. The programme is focused on moving investment towards locations and formats that M&S believes can provide a stronger customer experience. An earlier M&S investment announcement outlined more than £90 million of spending across its London estate. That programme covered 17 new or improved stores and was expected to create 450 local jobs. Machin described Pantheon as an example of the company’s strategy to “protect the magic and modernise the rest”, retaining its established customer proposition while updating stores and services. “We’ve still got a lot to do modernising our estate, with 25 years of catching up to do,” he said. “But Pantheon is a big step forward.” The completed Pantheon comes as M&S marks 100 years in the fashion industry and prepares for its official debut on the London Fashion Week runway this autumn. Its womenswear and menswear collection will be available to buy immediately online, in selected international markets and through flagship UK stores. M&S also plans to live stream the runway show . Pantheon will now serve as a test site for the retailer’s next phase of store renewal, with successful features informing work elsewhere in its estate.

article_title: In Pictures: BOSS and Soho House celebrate Wimbledon’s biggest weekend in style
sub_title: BOSS joined forces with Soho House as the headline fashion and sportswear partner of ‘Soho Grand Slam’ at Soho Farmhouse over the weekend, to coincide with the Wimbledon tennis finals.
article_content: BOSS joined forces with Soho House as the headline fashion and sportswear partner of ‘Soho Grand Slam’ at Soho Farmhouse over the weekend, to coincide with the Wimbledon tennis finals. The special weekend, which included match screenings, tournaments, dining events, headline music and plenty of BOSS fashion, came as the brand continues to strengthen its presence in the sport, having provided American tennis star Taylor Fritz with a tailored walk-on look during the men’s tournament. BOSS had also dressed brand ambassador David Beckham in a custom look on day one of Wimbledon, looking as sharp as ever. Soho House members and guests enjoyed a programme of events over the entire weekend that kicked off last Friday with a one-off dining event on the transformed tennis courts at the 100-acre luxury members’ club and hotel estate, which is located in the Oxfordshire countryside near the Cotswolds villages of Great Tew and Chipping Norton. It featured a sharing menu from Pen Yen, Soho Farmhouse’s much-loved Japanese izakaya-style restaurant. Saturday then began with tennis legend Andre Agassi sharing his insights on contemporary tennis culture and lifestyle with a special panel discussion. Throughout Saturday and Sunday, members competed in tennis and padel through round-robin play and knockout stages, culminating in the Soho Grand Slam final, with prizes courtesy of BOSS. Live screenings of the women’s and men’s finals on the Lazy Lawn allowed guests to follow the action from the championship, while resident DJs and a headline performance by Katy B provided a fitting soundtrack. Meanwhile, BOSS showcased its lifestyle offering on and off the court with contemporary performance looks for play, sharp tailoring and elevated eveningwear for “intimate dinners” and social gatherings, as well as relaxed summer essentials – from activewear and swimwear to casual looks for guests. Visitors also discovered the athleisurewear-focused BOSS range at a dedicated pop-up in the gym, featuring event-exclusive Soho Grand Slam merchandise and special offers. Women’s professional tennis player and BOSS brand ambassador Noma Noha Akugue was also in attendance, as were actors Corey Mylchreest and Charithra Chandran. On Saturday evening, guests gathered at the Glasshouse, coming together in refined BOSS evening looks “to celebrate a standout moment of the weekend”. Collaborating with Soho House on Soho Grand Slam forms part of a tennis-filled summer for BOSS – a season-long celebration of the sport and the brand’s growing role both on and off the court. From the grass courts of Wimbledon to the brand’s next big chapter of tennis at the Australian Open, BOSS “continues to connect the energy of tennis with modern tailoring, performance and contemporary lifestyle”.

article_title: Wax London expands Fenwick partnership with new Kingston concession
sub_title: Following the success of its concession at Fenwick in Newcastle, Wax London is expanding the partnership with a new 500 sq ft space in the retailer’s department store in Kingston upon Thames.
article_content: Following the success of its concession at Fenwick in Newcastle, Wax London is expanding the partnership with a new 500 sq ft space in the retailer’s department store in Kingston upon Thames. The space has been designed with the same attention to detail Wax London is known for, including custom rails, dark tinted acrylic tops and a vintage 16-drawer oak glazed haberdashery counter giving the concession “a warm, considered feel”, while a wall mounted lightbox adds a clean, modern contrast. Roger Wightman, Managing Director of Wax London, said: “After our success in Newcastle, opening in Kingston was a simple decision. We've found a new customer at Fenwick with a real appetite for what Wax London stands for, and that connection to the brand feels genuinely exciting. “To see the concession model growing with such strong presence across the country is something we're incredibly proud of – and a big thank you to everyone who has made it possible.” Stephen Ayres, Concessions Director at Fenwick, added: “At Fenwick, we are focused on curating a compelling and differentiated brand mix for our customers, and Wax London is a fantastic example of this. “Since launching in Newcastle, the brand has demonstrated a strong affinity with our customer base, making Kingston a natural next step in the partnership. Wax London's commitment to quality, craftsmanship and contemporary British design aligns perfectly with the modern menswear offer we continue to build across our stores. “We are delighted to welcome the brand to Kingston and look forward to seeing it become part of the store's fashion destination.” At the heart of the floor plan of the new concession sits a central styling area, framed by side-hang wall rails and freestanding floor units. The existing balustrade glass panels have been treated with an orange-tint film, “a quiet nod to the brand’s earthy, sun-warmed palette”. Founded in 2015, Wax London unveiled its first ever in-store pop-up in Harrods, Knightsbridge, in May, described as “an exciting next step in its continued growth”, with further pop-up opportunities also now being considered to drive further brand awareness. Wax London currently operates five standalone UK stores, four of which are in London - on Soho’s Berwick Street, which was the first to open in 2023, Covent Garden’s Neal Street (2024), Spitalfields (2024), Canary Wharf (2025), as well as its first store outside of the capital in Victoria Leeds, which opened in October 2025.

ASOS introduces ARRANGE Bespoke to spotlight emerging fashion talent
sub_title: ASOS has launched ARRANGE Bespoke, a new collaboration series designed to spotlight emerging designers, with Central Saint Martins student Johannes Warnke selected as its first creative partner.
article_content: ASOS has launched ARRANGE Bespoke, a new collaboration series designed to spotlight emerging designers, with Central Saint Martins student Johannes Warnke selected as its first creative partner. Launching during Paris Couture Week, ARRANGE Bespoke debuts with a hand-crafted dress created by Warnke in collaboration with the ARRANGE design team. The piece combines repurposed off-cuts and surplus materials with ARRANGE’s signature naturally dyed peace silk, reflecting a shared focus on craftsmanship, construction and detail. Warnke, who is known for his distinctive draping style and experimental approach to design, reimagined ARRANGE’s signature sequins through movement and texture. The dress was created by collaging repurposed materials, combining different sequin sizes and shapes with layers of hand-dyed peace silk to create a softer, fluid silhouette. Johannes Warnke said: “I was interested in reimagining the ARRANGE signature sequins through movement, inspired by the streets of Paris and the way summer light filters through windows and curtains before falling onto the street.” The collaboration marks the first in an ongoing ARRANGE Bespoke series, which will invite emerging designers to reinterpret the label’s approach to occasionwear while showcasing the creative process behind each collection. ARRANGE is ASOS’ elevated fashion label, focused on premium occasionwear and statement designs. Through ARRANGE Bespoke, the retailer aims to highlight emerging creative talent and explore new perspectives on occasion dressing. Vanessa Spence, EVP Brand and Creative at ASOS, said: "ARRANGE Bespoke gives us an opportunity to celebrate fashion in its most expressive form while offering a glimpse into the creative thinking behind ARRANGE.” “By collaborating with emerging creative talent, we're able to spotlight the next generation of designers, bring fresh perspectives to each collection, and showcase the craftsmanship, creativity and storytelling that sits behind the product,” she added. The launch reflects how fashion brands are increasingly using designer collaborations to celebrate craftsmanship, creativity and emerging talent. The first ARRANGE Bespoke dress was photographed in Paris during Couture Week and will now be held in the ASOS archive as the first piece in the series. Further collaborations are planned as ARRANGE Bespoke continues to develop.

UK retail footfall falls 3.4% in June as heatwave keeps shoppers inside
sub_title: UK retail footfall fell 3.4% year-on-year in June as record temperatures kept shoppers indoors, with high streets experiencing the steepest decline, according to new data from the British Retail Consortium and Sensormatic.
article_content: UK retail footfall fell 3.4% year-on-year in June as record temperatures kept shoppers indoors, with high streets experiencing the steepest decline, according to new data from the British Retail Consortium and Sensormatic. The data, covering the five weeks from 31 May to 5 July, showed the decline worsened from a 2.6% fall in May. High street footfall dropped 6.2%, compared with a 1.5% decline the previous month, while shopping centre footfall fell 2.5%. Retail parks proved the most resilient, with footfall down just 0.3%. The figures suggest shoppers avoided outdoor retail destinations during June’s record temperatures, while indoor shopping centres and retail parks were less heavily affected. The regional picture also reflected the impact of the heatwave. Scotland was the only nation to record growth, with footfall rising 1.7%, while England saw the largest decline at 3%. Wales recorded a 2.3% fall and Northern Ireland was 0.9%. Helen Dickinson, Chief Executive of the British Retail Consortium, said: “Footfall dropped in June as the record heatwave kept many shoppers indoors. High streets saw the sharpest declines, while air-conditioned shopping centres and retail parks proved more resilient.” “While London and the South East, where temperatures were highest, registered the biggest decline, other regions performed markedly better. Scotland saw footfall rise, buoyed by cooler weather and the continued gradual opening of Glasgow City Centre after March’s devastating Union Corner fire.” Andy Sumpter, Retail Consultant EMEA at Sensormatic, said the figures suggested consumers were continuing to make “fewer, more considered trips” despite a slight improvement in consumer confidence. He added: “Exceptionally high temperatures are likely to have influenced behaviour, particularly in the South, where record heat and travel disruption made shopping trips less appealing.” Sumpter added that the World Cup had affected footfall, with key matches “drawing attention and occasionally keeping shoppers away”. The latest figures leave UK retail footfall down 3.3% year to date, with retailers hoping to convert increasingly deliberate shopping trips into stronger spending during the second half of the year.
