Nadine Merabi appoints new CEO as expansion continues
sub_title: Luxury womenswear brand Nadine Merabi announced the appointment of Briony Garbett as Chief Executive Officer.
article_content: Luxury womenswear brand Nadine Merabi announced the appointment of Briony Garbett as Chief Executive Officer, as it continues its expansion plans. Garbett joins the business from Karen Millen, where she has served as Managing Director since 2025. She replaces the former CEO Jacobo Hachuel, who left the brand in 2025. Her appointment marks another milestone for the brand, as it both celebrates its 10th anniversary and enters its next phase of global growth. The announcement follows the appointments of Nick Beighton and Hash Ladha as advisors to the business, earlier in the year. Both will now formally join the Board, with Beighton appointed Non-Executive Chair and Ladha appointed Non-Executive Director. Garbett brings extensive experience across fashion, digital and brand leadership to her new role, the brand said. She joined Oasis in 2012, progressing to Customer Director before departing in 2017. She subsequently joined Kurt Geiger as Chief Marketing Officer and has also held senior leadership roles including CEO at consumer health tech brand Naama Studios and CMO at maternity wear brand Seraphine. Nadine Merabi, Founder of Nadine Merabi, commented: "The moment I met Briony, I knew she was the perfect fit for MERABI. She brings exceptional leadership qualities, deep experience, strong commercial acumen and an energy that aligns completely with our culture and ambitions. "I cannot wait for her to join the team and help lead the business through its next stage of growth. We have incredibly exciting plans ahead, and I know Briony will play a pivotal role in bringing them to life." Garbett added: "This is an incredibly exciting opportunity to join a fast-growing global brand that is truly resonating with women. Merabi has built something very special — a distinctive brand with strong foundations, a highly engaged customer and significant opportunity for profitable international growth across DTC, wholesale and category expansion. "What makes the opportunity even more compelling is the chance to partner with such an exceptional founder with a very clear creative vision. It’s a dream role." Nadine Merabi, which launched in 2015 and built its reputation in occasionwear and partywear, has recently released its first denim capsule collection as it looks to expand into everyday wear.

article_title: Editorial Policy
Frasers builds 4.2% Burberry position through put options
sub_title: The derivatives position represents 15 million voting rights and expands Frasers Group’s luxury exposure as Burberry’s turnaround gains traction.
article_content: Frasers Group has built a derivatives position representing 4.155% of Burberry’s voting rights, extending the Sports Direct owner’s push into the luxury market and demonstrating its international ambitions. The group, which is controlled by Mike Ashley and led by CEO Michael Murray, has been on a drive upmarket in recent times which has led to bids being placed for German fashion giant Hugo Boss , while it is also circling upmarket department store group Harvey Nichols and is in active pursuit of Australian footwear retailer Accent Group . Its position in British luxury house Burberry equates to 15 million voting rights and is held entirely through financial instruments; it was revealed in a regulatory filing published on 28 July . Frasers disclosed no voting rights attached directly to Burberry shares. Frasers crossed the reporting threshold on 27 July, increasing its exposure from 3.047%, or 11 million voting rights. The increase represented four million additional voting rights and 1.108 percentage points. The position comprises two sold put options expiring in October 2026, representing 3.49 million and four million voting rights respectively. A third option covering 7.51 million voting rights expires in March 2027. If the options are exercised, Frasers may acquire the shares represented by the instruments. The filing does not disclose direct ownership of Burberry stock or any proxy voting arrangement. Burberry shares closed around 5% higher on Tuesday after the position became public, while Frasers shares gained 2.5%. Frasers has used minority positions to support its move upmarket. It operates luxury department store chain Flannels and owns approximately 37% of British luxury brand Mulberry. The group made two conditional approaches for Mulberry in 2024, but ended its pursuit after majority shareholder Challice said it would not sell. Mulberry later appointed Frasers executive James France as a non-executive director. Frasers has also crossed the 30% mandatory-bid threshold at Hugo Boss. Its €38-per-share offer for the German premium fashion group became legally unconditional after receiving European Commission merger-control clearance, though the Boss board has recommended that shareholders reject it. The disclosure comes as Burberry pursues a turnaround focused on recognisable British products, a wider price range and demand from younger shoppers. Burberry reported a 5% rise in comparable sales over the quarter to the end of June 2026, marking its fourth consecutive quarter of comparable growth. First-quarter revenue came in at £455 million, helped by demand for trench coats and scarves. Burberry has used British figures including actor and comedian Jennifer Saunders and tennis star Jack Draper in campaigns supporting its return to practical heritage products. Sales during the quarter were strong in the US and China, although the company said conflict in the Middle East was affecting tourist spending in Europe.

article_title: Farfetch launches new campaign with a focus on ‘transeasonal style’
sub_title: Luxury fashion platform Farfetch has launched a new ‘pre-fall’ campaign, which puts the focus on styles that fit the transition from late summer into autumn.
article_content: Luxury fashion platform Farfetch has launched a new ‘pre-fall’ campaign, which puts the focus on styles that fit the transition from late summer into autumn. Shot in Margate, Kent, and photographed by Alessandro Furchino Capria, the campaign “juxtaposes FARFETCH’s high-impact luxury offering with the quiet of 1960s suburban architecture and coastal landscapes”, featuring a balance between relaxed summer elegance and structured autumn tailoring “for the return to the office”. Doralice Belli, Head of Merchandising at Farfetch, said: "Defined for the post-holiday return, this exclusive selection offers versatile and polished pieces that transition seamlessly from late summer into fall. “For our discerning global community, customers who master their own style, this edit offers diverse options for the seasonal shift.” Key trends include red as the “must-have” colour of the season, whether as a bold statement coat or as a subtle pop of colour through accessories, while the ‘Sportif’ trend is set to evolve into the cooler weather with athletic-inspired silhouettes combined with luxury tailoring “for a sleek, modern look”. Elevated matching co-ord sets also set the tone for the transition season across both menswear and womenswear.

article_title: Kering returns to organic growth but Gucci remains in decline
sub_title: Kering recorded its first organic sales growth in three years, with revenues up 2% on a comparable basis in Q2 to €3.65 billion (£3.12 billion), building on a stable first quarter.
article_content: Kering recorded its first organic sales growth in three years, with revenues up 2% on a comparable basis in the second quarter to €3.65 billion (£3.12 billion), building on a stable first quarter. While Gucci remained in decline, stronger retail trends helped the Paris-based luxury group return to growth while store closures, cost controls and asset disposals supported profitability and a sharp reduction in net debt. First-half revenue for Kering rose 1% organically to €7.22 billion, and fell 3% on a reported basis. Directly operated retail sales were flat during the six months, while wholesale and other revenue increased 5%. The group noted that the situation in the Middle East "remained challenging" during Q2, with a 1 percentage point reduction in revenue growth, although retail trends improved sequentially. Kering noted that Saint Laurent, Bottega Veneta and Brioni continued to improve sequentially, with performance accelerating versus the first quarter. A recent leadership shake-up has seen Romain Spitzer appointed as Chief Executive Officer of Bottega Veneta earlier this mon th. Balenciaga faced a more challenging quarter, according to its parent company, as the House "continued to work through its creative transition and to restore balance across its business, with leather goods remaining a source of strength." Kering also noted that McQueen has accelerated the execution of initiatives aimed at "repositioning the brand as a British authority in tailoring and occasion wear", while it continues to rightsize its distribution network under its new CEO, Gianfranco D'Attis. McQueen, which has been undergoing a global strategic restructure to restore profitability, has seen its flagship store relocated to 27 Old Bond Street, while it has also been announcing layoffs in both its Italian operations and London headquarters. Gucci’s second-quarter revenue declined 2% on a comparable basis to €1.41 billion (£1.21 billion), against an 8% fall during the first quarter. Revenue from Gucci’s directly operated stores fell 2% to €1.28 billion (£1.10 billion), an improvement of seven percentage points from the previous quarter. Wholesale and other revenue increased 5% to €135 million (£116 million). North America was the brand’s main growth driver, while sales in Western Europe and Asia-Pacific began to recover. Mainland China remained difficult, despite an improvement during the quarter. Kering said the Borsetto and Paparazzo product lines supported demand, alongside attention generated by the Gucci Core show in New York. For the first half, Gucci’s comparable revenue fell 5% to €2.76 billion (£2.36 billion). Recurring operating income reached €468 million (£401 million ) , while its recurring operating margin increased by one percentage point to 17%. For the first half, Kering posted recurring operating income of €921 million (£789 million), with a recurring operating margin of 12.8%, up 40 basis points higher year-on-year. Net income attributable to the group came in at €189 million (£162 million). The group completed 84 net store closures during the half of the year, following 75 closures in 2025. It is targeting 100 net closures across 2026. Net debt fell from €8 billion (£6.85 billion) at the end of 2025 to €3.3 billion (£2.82 billion) as of 30 June. The reduction included proceeds from Kering Beauté’s sale to L’Oréal and a Milan property transaction. CEO Luca de Meo commented on the latest results: "Kering delivered improved performance in the second quarter, with revenue returning to growth. Across the Group, we are seeing early signs of progress in brand desirability, commercial momentum and operating performance. "These first-half results demonstrate the positive impact of the decisive measures we have taken to reinforce the distinctiveness of our brands, simplify our organization and increase effectiveness across the Group. "While the market environment remains demanding, we are focused on delivering our roadmap with discipline and consistency, creating the foundations for sustainable growth and long-term value creation." The results follow the April launch of ReconKering, the group’s plan to improve brand desirability , execution and operating efficiency.

article_title: Tod's launches Harrods pop-up for Red Dot sneakers
sub_title: Tod's, the Italian luxury footwear brand, is today opening a dedicated pop-up at Harrods, focusing on its Red Dot men's sneaker collection.
article_content: Tod's , the Italian luxury footwear brand, is today opening a dedicated pop-up at Harrods, focusing on its Red Dot men's sneaker collection. The pop-up showcases a curated edit of Red Dot sneaker styles for men, with the collection reflecting the brand's commitment to traditional hand craftsmanship combined with continuous product innovation. Each sneaker is identified by a red dot on the heel, which serves as a Tod's brand signature. The designs use selected materials alongside elastic lacing, while the lightweight sole is intended to allow customers to move seamlessly between work and leisure. The launch reflects Tod's efforts to apply its production expertise to contemporary casual footwear, with the brand saying the collection expresses "a contemporary vision of luxury defined by softness and lightness". Founded as a small shoe factory in Casette D'Ete more than a century ago, Tod's produces its collections entirely in Italy. The company remains closely associated with the Gommino driving shoe, introduced in the late 1970s with 133 rubber pebbles on its sole. The business later expanded beyond footwear, launching a full women's ready-to-wear collection in 2013 and a complete men's wardrobe the following year. Its wider group also includes luxury footwear label Hogan and fashion brand Fay.uxury footwear label Hogan and fashion brand Fay. The Tod's launch follows other temporary brand activations at Harrods, including Wax London's first in-store pop-up in May . The 150 sq ft menswear space combined the British brand's SS26 collection with a Harrods-exclusive knitwear colourway. Harrods has also continued investing in its permanent fashion offer. In June, the retailer opened the first of three International Designer Rooms as part of the overhaul of its first-floor womenswear department. The new rooms are designed to bring international labels together within a connected retail environment, supported by flagship spaces from individual luxury houses. Tod's smaller, product-led installation gives the store another way to present fashion brands. The Tod's Red Dot pop-up will be open from 29 July until the end of September in the menswear department on Harrods' second floor, at 87-135 Brompton Road, Knightsbridge, London.

article_title: LVMH revenues rise as fashion division returns to growth in Q2
sub_title: LVMH reported revenue of €38.6 billion for the first half of 2026, with growth accelerating in the second quarter as its Fashion & Leather Goods division returned to organic growth despite continued geopolitical and economic uncertainty.
article_content: LVMH reported revenue of €38.6 billion for the first half of 2026, with growth accelerating in the second quarter as its Fashion & Leather Goods division returned to organic growth despite continued geopolitical and economic uncertainty. The luxury group posted revenue of €38.6 billion for the six months to 30 June, down 3% year-on-year on a reported basis, while organic revenue increased 2%. Profit from recurring operations declined 4% to €8.7 billion, with an operating margin remaining high at 22.5%. Net profit was broadly flat at €5.7 billion. LVMH said organic revenue growth accelerated to 3% in the second quarter, or 4% excluding the impact of the conflict in the Middle East, supported by stronger performances in the US and Asia excluding Japan. Fashion & Leather Goods, the group's largest division, generated revenue of €18.1 billion, down 5% on a reported basis and 1% organically over the half year. However, the business returned to 1% organic growth in the second quarter, marking an improvement on the first quarter when the division reported a 2% organic decline as disruption linked to the conflict in the Middle East weighed on performance. The group credited the recovery to the strong debut of Jonathan Anderson's first collections for Christian Dior, alongside the performance of Louis Vuitton's new flagship stores in Beijing and Seoul. Bernard Arnault, Chairman and CEO of LVMH, said: “LVMH demonstrated its solidity and effective strategy. Our Maisons, which remained focused on ensuring the utmost quality in our products, and several of which are pursuing their creative renewal, continued to inspire dreams and enhance their desirability.” He added that second-quarter growth was driven by “the success of Jonathan Anderson's first designs for Christian Dior, the remarkable performance of Louis Vuitton's exceptional new stores in Beijing and Seoul, and Tiffany and Bvlgari's iconic lines”. Christian Dior reported accelerating growth following the launch of Anderson's first designs, with the new Cigale bag receiving a strong customer response. Elsewhere, Loro Piana delivered another strong performance, while Rimowa and Berluti also recorded growth during the period. Across the wider group, Watches & Jewelry was among the strongest-performing divisions, with organic revenue increasing 9%, supported by Tiffany & Co. and Bvlgari. Selective Retailing, which includes Sephora, recorded 5% organic growth, while Wines & Spirits also returned to growth, with organic revenue up 5%. Looking ahead, LVMH said it remains confident despite an uncertain geopolitical and economic environment, maintaining its strategy of investing in creativity, product quality, and retail experiences to strengthen the desirability of its brands.

article_title: Gymshark promotes ex-ASOS director as Chief Supply Chain Officer
sub_title: Gymshark's continues to add to its executive team, with founder and Chief Executive Ben Francis MBE announcing that Matt Rogers, the brand's Global Supply Chain Director, has been promoted to the position of Chief Supply Chain Officer.
article_content: Gymshark continues to add to its executive team with founder and Chief Executive Ben Francis MBE announcing that Matt Rogers, the brand's Global Supply Chain Director, has been promoted to the position of Chief Supply Chain Officer. "Since joining Gymshark in 2023 as our Supply Chain Director, Matt has made a huge impact," Francis shared in a LinkedIn post. "Over the past few years, he's helped strengthen and evolve our supply chain and more recently, has done an outstanding job leading the function as Interim General Manager for Sourcing and Supply Chain." "Matt has consistently demonstrated the leadership, judgement and ambition needed to build a supply chain that's ready for the next chapter of Gymshark. This marks the second appointment to Gymshark's senior leadership team this month. The brand appointed former Boden Executive Shaun Perkinson to lead its technology function as Chief Technology Officer. Perkinson took over the position from John Douglas, who joined Gymshark five years ago and was looking to retire. Francis had also announced Perkinson's appointment on LinkedIn, highlighting the 20 years of experience he is bringing to the CTO role, and in particular his "combination of technical expertise, commercial instinct and collaborative approach". "Technology will continue to play a pivotal role in helping us create better experiences for our community and supporting the next stage of our growth. Shaun joins us at an exciting time and I'm confident we'll do great things together," Francis added. Both appointments followed the announcement that Francis was in negotiations to buy back part of the 21% stake held by US private equity firm General Atlantic, according to reports by the Financial Times. Francis, who still owns a majority stake in the company he founded out of his parents' garage in 2012, is now looking to further tighten his control over the company. Sources told the publication that while Francis had considered buying back the entirety of the General Atlantic stake, he is more likely to buy part of it.

article_title: Frasers CEO says business rates are deterring high street investment
sub_title: Frasers Group Chief Executive Michael Murray has criticised the UK business rates system, arguing that higher bills following store upgrades are discouraging investment in town centres.
article_content: Frasers Group boss Michael Murray has criticised the UK business rates system, arguing that higher bills following store upgrades are discouraging investment in town centres. The retail group spends tens of millions of pounds on upgrading its store estate, but those projects can push up property rateable values and the resulting tax bills, Murray said in an interview with The Telegraph at the opening of a new Sports Direct flagship in Dublin. Murray described the current business rate system, which he said penalised retailers for upgrading their shops, as making “zero sense”. He added that rising operating costs were making it harder to run high street stores profitably. Murray's remarks come amid wider demands to scrap the property tax . The Real Rates Reform Alliance, which says it speaks for more than 28,000 firms and business leaders, has suggested a 2% levy on online sales to pay for a 37% cut in business rates for bricks-and-mortar companies. Research cited by the alliance found that 55% of firms viewed business rates as a major or moderate cost. Around 17% had cut jobs in response to the burden, while 31% had raised prices. This would be a “major shot in the arm” for many high streets and communities, which it said have been forced into cutting jobs, investment and raising prices due to the pressures of rising business rate bills, according to the alliance. In addition to business rates, Murray noted that Frasers is dealing with higher employment costs after increases in the national minimum wage and employers’ National Insurance contributions. Murray also took aim at plans to grant pubs and music venues a 20% business rates discount while imposing extra charges on large warehouses. He said warehouses serving physical shops should not be treated the same as distribution centres run by online-only retailers. Murray also called for lower rates on shops to reduce the tax disparity between online pureplays and retailers maintaining town-centre estates. Despite the hurdles presented by business rates, Frasers is continuing to grow and refresh its physical estate under its Elevation Strategy. Its new Sports Direct and Everlast Gyms+ flagship in Dublin spans 85,000 sq ft over four floors at the former Debenhams site on Henry Street. The “landmark” opening, which has created 75 new roles, marks a major €80 million investment in Dublin city centre and also signals the official launch of HOKA in Sports Direct stores, further strengthening the retailer's position as a strategic partner for the world’s biggest sports brands

article_title: Burberry and V&A to stage display celebrating the history of the trench coat
sub_title: Rare catalogues, a coat worn by Hardy Amies and 19 runway looks will chart the evolution of Burberry’s best-known design during the British house’s 170th year.
article_content: Burberry and the V&A are set to stage a free display tracing the development of the Burberry trench coat, marking the iconic British brand’s 170th anniversary. The Burberry Trench: Crafting an Icon will run from 21 September 2026 to 3 January 2027 at V&A South Kensington; its opening coincides with the staging of Burberry's catwalk show at September's London Fashion Week. It will bring together rare objects from the Burberry Archive and the museum’s collection, including material being publicly exhibited for the first time. The display will occupy the Prince Consort Gallery, a seldom-seen space that once housed textiles in mahogany cabinets. It will follow the trench coat’s progression from protective outerwear and military clothing into one of Burberry’s central products and an internationally recognised fashion design. A men's metallic silk trench from 2013 by Christopher Bailey (Courtesy: Burberry) The opening section, Invention , will focus on Thomas Burberry’s creation of cotton gabardine in 1879. Its use gave the company’s outerwear protection from the weather while retaining a lightweight and practical construction. The exhibition will examine how this material helped establish the trench as a sought-after coat before its adoption as a fashion staple. Burberry was founded by Thomas Burberry in 1856 and continues to use gabardine across its Heritage Trench range. A Burberry design from c. 1937-1944 pictured in a catalogue (Courtesy: Burberry) Craft will examine the practical details that have shaped the coat for more than a century. These include its hand-finished collar and House Check lining, as well as the storm flap and detachable throat latch, which provide additional protection. Burberry says its trench collar is assembled from eight parts and can require up to 200 stitches. The company first used its check to line rainwear during the 1920s. The final section, Creativity , will present 19 runway looks produced over the past 25 years. The selection will include designs by current Chief Creative Officer Daniel Lee and former Chief Creative Officer Christopher Bailey, showing how successive collections have revised the trench’s proportions, construction and styling. Hardy Amies' personalised Burberry car coat from 1979 (Courtesy: Burberry) Early 20th-century catalogues and a Burberry trench coat worn by British fashion designer Hardy Amies will also feature. Carly Eck, brand curator at Burberr, said: “A myriad of objects from the brand’s Archive will be publicly exhibited for the first time – from early 20th-century catalogues to a Burberry trench coat worn by fashion designer Hardy Amies.” Oriole Cullen, senior curator of fashion and textiles at the V&A, said the display would highlight how the British fashion staple “continues to evolve over a century on”. Fringed women's trench from AW25 by Daniel Lee (Courtesy: Burberry) The display forms part of Burberry’s multi-year partnership with the V&A, which will lead to the opening of The Burberry Gallery in autumn 2028. The project will transform the museum’s existing Fashion Gallery into a redesigned space for its collection, which spans five centuries. The Burberry Trench: Crafting an Icon will remain free and open to all throughout its run.

article_title: Frasers to advance Harvey Nichols bid as Hugo Boss clears German merger control
sub_title: Frasers continues to push forward with two of its recent takeover bids for Harvey Nichols and Hugo Boss.
article_content: Frasers continues to push forward with two of its recent takeover bids. The retail group is expected to submit a bid for department store Harvey Nichols and has also received merger control clearance from the European Commission to take forward its takeover offer of Hugo Boss. Frasers Group and NEXT both face a 28 July deadline to submit offers for Harvey Nichols, according to Sky News, while unidentified international bidders are reportedly working to a separate timetable. Harvey Nichols is being sold through advisers at FTI Consulting after 35 years under the ownership of Hong Kong businessman Sir Dickson Poon. The process places its Knightsbridge flagship and wider store estate in play, although reaching the bid deadline does not guarantee that a transaction will be completed. Frasers Group entered the process two weeks ago , despite concerns among some Harvey Nichols suppliers about its potential ownership. Frasers owns Sports Direct, Flannels and House of Fraser. The Harvey Nichols deadline coincides with Frasers’ pursuit of German premium fashion group Hugo Boss, with its offer becoming unconditional today, following the takeover bid's approval by German authorities. Bidders for Harvey Nichols have been asked to commit between £50 million and £60 million over the medium term to fund the luxury department store's transformation plan, Sky News previously reported. The proposed investment, which would be separate from the acquisition price, would support a refurbishment of the Edinburgh store, international expansion, digital development and the management team’s business plan. Apart from Frasers Group and NEXT, potential bidders for the department store include Modella Capital, the owner of Hobbycraft and TGJones, as well as Dubai-based Chalhoub Group and India’s Reliance Retail. NEXT emerged as a potential bidder earlier this month . It remains unclear whether NEXT would retain Harvey Nichols’ regional store network or focus on the brand and its intellectual property. FTI Consulting will now assess the bids submitted under the auction timetable, including the proposed financial support for the retailer’s turnaround. In the latest developments on the Hugo Boss bid, Frasers Group said its takeover offer for the German luxury brand had received merger control clearance from the European Commission. The approval removes the final regulatory obstacle and means the cash offer for the German fashion company is now legally unconditional. Frasers Group also extended the acceptance period for the offer until midnight 13 August in Frankfurt local time. Frasers crossed Germany’s 30% mandatory-bid threshold last week, after it acquired a further 2,549,900 shares in the company. Yesterday, it was reported by The Times that Frasers Group was considering appointing its Chief Executive, Michael Murray, to lead Hugo Boss if its takeover of the German premium fashion company succeeds. The proposed appointment would give Frasers direct operational control of Hugo Boss and represent a change from its earlier support for incumbent CEO Daniel Grieder when it originally launched its offer in June. The group had previously declared its original €38 price as final . Frasers first launched its bid on 10 June, valuing the remaining 73.94% of the Hugo Boss brand at about €1.98 billion. Almost one month later, Hugo Boss’s management and supervisory boards unanimously recommended that shareholders should reject the unsolicited approach, calling it financially "inadequate". The retail group is also pursuing Australian footwear retailer Accent Group, which has, however, firmly rejected its approach . Last week, Frasers extended that offer until September , with its other terms unchanged.

article_title: Primark turns SKIMS’ London launch into a marketing opportunity
sub_title: Primark placed a mobile billboard beside the queue for SKIMS’ newly opened Regent Street flagship, promoting its £9 shaping bodysuit as a lower-priced alternative to Kim Kardashian’s widely popular shapewear offering.
article_content: Primark placed a mobile billboard beside the newly opened SKIMS’ Regent Street flagship, promoting its £9 shaping bodysuit as a lower-priced alternative to Kim Kardashian’s widely popular shapewear offering. The high street retailer used the opening week of SKIMS’ first standalone UK store to put its product in front of customers looking to enter the newly opened 12,000 sq ft location. The tongue-in-cheek placement showcased Primark's version of the shapewear bodysuit, with the slogan reading "These Kim's prefer Primark £9 shaping bodysuit". In comparison, SKIMS Seamless Sculpt Thong Bodysuit, available in the Regent Street store, currently retails at £84. The campaign was shared on social media by Metro UK and the Daily Mail. The move follows Primark's announcement last week that it had lowered prices across hundreds of womenswear , menswear and kidswear products as part of a new “Iconic Value” initiative aimed at reinforcing its position as a destination for affordable fashion. A post shared by Metro UK (@metro.co.uk) The campaign highlights once again how UK brands and retailers have sharpened their competitive edge following SKIM's entry into the market. Since launching in 2019, SKIMS has positioned itself as a major player in the shapewear and lingerie market , with consumer spending reaching over £1.8 million in 2025, according to data from digital bank Monzo. As competition in the category intensifies, Marks & Spencer launched a 300-piece reimagined lingerie collection, BODY, in April, built around “a modern, modular and solution-focused design philosophy”. Starting at £16, the range covers bras, briefs, shapewear and essentials, using features including 360-degree stretch, laser-cut edges and targeted sculpting. M&S remains one of the key players within the category, according to the retailer, with a bra sold every two seconds. British underwear brand Lounge also recently introduced a 34-piece collection of engineered essentials , in an effort to “reclaim its stake in the category it helped shape” and reposition the brand to sit confidently alongside both SKIMS and M&S Body. Lounge highlighted that its new collection is very size-inclusive, spanning from 28A-40G and XS-3XL. Size inclusivity is one of the biggest selling points for Kim Kardashian's SKIMS brand. "We’ve refined and unified our offering into something that feels complete: a system of fit-led pieces designed to replace compromise with confidence," said Emily Blount, Product Director at Lounge, at the time of the launch. "It’s the result of years of listening, testing and perfecting, and it reaffirms Lounge as a benchmark in modern everyday lingerie." SKIMS opened its very first UK flagship on Friday 24 July, at 245-247 Regent Street. The opening further solidified the brand's retail presence in the UK. It had previously been available through wholesale partners including Selfridges, Harrods and END. The store, which was formerly occupied by Ted Baker, marks SKIMS’ largest European retail location. Jens Grede, co-founder and CEO of SKIMS, commented on the opening: “Our flagship stores play an important role in how customers experience SKIMS beyond the product.” Kim Kardashian, co-founder and Chief Creative Officer, added: "London has always been one of the most inspiring fashion cities in the world to me, so opening our first UK flagship on Regent Street feels especially exciting.” The London launch follows a period of rapid growth for the business. In late 2025, SKIMS secured a $225 million funding round that valued the company at $5 billion , fuelling further investment in physical retail as well as apparel and the NikeSKIMS partnership. The Regent Street flagship is one of a series of international openings, with a new flagship at Dubai Mall and stores also planned for Delhi and Mumbai. Founded by Kim Kardashian, Jens Grede and Emma Grede in 2019, SKIMS began as a direct-to-consumer shapewear brand before expanding into underwear, swimwear, loungewear and menswear.

article_title: Duke + Dexter appoints new Creative Director to shape broader fashion vision
sub_title: British footwear and lifestyle brand Duke + Dexter has promoted Connor Boon to Creative Director, marking a new chapter for the business as it continues to expand beyond footwear.
article_content: British footwear and lifestyle brand Duke + Dexter has promoted Connor Boon to Creative Director, marking a new chapter for the business as it continues to expand beyond footwear. Boon has spent almost seven years at the company, joining as an intern in 2018 before progressing through a series of creative roles. Most recently serving as Head of Creative, he has helped shape the brand's visual identity across campaigns, collaborations and product development, including designing Duke + Dexter's bestselling Wilde Penny Loafer. In his new role, Boon joins the executive leadership team and will oversee creative strategy across product, campaigns and brand storytelling. Commenting on the appointment, Boon said: "This brand has shaped my entire career. It's been the foundation of everything I've learned and achieved, filled with incredible highs, challenges and defining moments that have brought us to where we are." He added: "We'll be championing the artist-led approach that's been woven into the brand since the very beginning. As Creative Director, my focus is on pushing that even further, exploring how art and human touch can be applied across everything we do.” "We're collaborating with exceptional artists from around the world to create products and stories that feel authentic, original and true to the world our customers live in." Under Boon's creative leadership, Duke + Dexter plans to further develop its apparel and formalwear offering alongside its footwear collections, while continuing to invest in creative collaborations and brand storytelling. The appointment comes as the British brand continues its expansion, with ambitions to establish itself as a broader lifestyle label beyond its footwear roots.

Fabletics reunites with Stephen and Erica Malbon for second golfwear collaboration
sub_title: Fabletics has teamed up once again with golf lifestyle duo Stephen and Erica Malbon to launch a second limited-edition capsule collection, building on the success of their first collaboration with a range inspired by coastal style and performance dressing.
article_content: Fabletics has teamed up once again with golf lifestyle duo Stephen and Erica Malbon to launch a second limited-edition capsule collection, building on the success of their first collaboration with a range inspired by coastal style and performance dressing. The latest collection combines lightweight, breathable performance fabrics with ocean-inspired design details, including sea urchin motifs, across men’s and women’s apparel designed for wear both on and off the golf course. The launch reflects the continued evolution of golfwear, as brands increasingly blend technical performance with lifestyle appeal to attract both established players and a new generation of consumers. Don Ressler, Co-Founder of Fabletics, said: “Stephen and Erica have such a distinct point of view on the culture of golf, and together we saw an opportunity to build on the momentum of our first collection with something that feels fresh, elevated and unexpected, without losing sight of performance or accessibility.” “Golf has become more than a sport, it’s a lifestyle, and this collection brings a fresh spin to golfwear for people who love the game, the energy and the culture around it.” Stephen and Erica Malbon said the collection drew inspiration from the ocean, particularly the patterns, colours and textures of sea urchins, which feature throughout the range in graphics, logos and fabric detailing. The capsule includes technical separates designed for everything from golf rounds and practice sessions to travel and everyday wear. The collection is also size-inclusive, with men’s styles available from XS to XXL, with selected pieces up to 4XL, and women’s styles ranging from XXS to 4XL. The collaboration follows growing investment in fashion-led golf collections as brands respond to rising interest in the sport among younger consumers and position golf apparel as part of a broader lifestyle wardrobe rather than performance wear alone. The Stephen & Erica Malbon for Fabletics collection is available now online and in selected Fabletics stores. In February we sat down with Mark Ralea, Fabletics' General Manager on his career journey and how the industry has evolved since his first role at Stylebop.com. He also highlighted what he finds most rewarding about his current role and how he creates an environment where others can thrive.

article_title: Terms and Conditions
Chanel appoints Hélène de Tissot as new CFO
sub_title: Chanel has appointed Hélène de Tissot as its new Chief Financial Officer, succeeding long-serving finance chief Phillipe Blondiaux as the luxury house continues a broader leadership transition.
article_content: Chanel has appointed Hélène de Tissot as its new Chief Financial Officer, succeeding long-serving Finance Chief Phillipe Blondiaux as the luxury house continues a broader leadership transition. De Tissot will join Chanel in October from French drinks group Pernod Ricard, where she has served as Executive Vice President of Finance & IT since 2018. She brings more than two decades of experience at the company, having previously held senior roles including Group Strategy & M&A Director, Senior Vice President Finance for Asia and Group Tax Director. She succeeds Blondiaux, who announced earlier this month that he would retire at the end of the year after 15 years with Chanel. During his tenure, Blondiaux oversaw a period of significant international expansion and investment across the business. The appointment comes as Chanel enters a new chapter under Global CEO Leena Nair and Artistic Director of Fashion Activities Matthieu Blazy, who joined the house last year. It also follows a return to growth for Chanel . For the year ended 31 December 2025, the luxury house reported revenues of $19.3 billion, up 2% year-on-year, while operating profit increased 5% to $4.7 billion. The company attributed the performance to continued investment in its brand, boutique network and creative strategy, alongside strong momentum across fashion, fragrance and beauty. Prior to joining Pernod Ricard in 2002, de Tissot spent almost nine years as a senior international tax lawyer at Arthur Andersen. She studied at Paris II Panthéon-Assas University, completed postgraduate studies at ESSEC Business School and qualified for the French Bar. De Tissot will take up the role in October, with Blondiaux remaining in post until the end of the year to support the leadership transition. As part of Chanel's continued investment in the future of its brand and people, the luxury brand announced at the beginning of the month that it was acquiring Charvet, the Paris-based, family-run shirtmaker , turning a runway collaboration into an investment in specialist craft under artistic director Matthieu Blazy. Blazy's tenure has already generated visible commercial results. His autumn/winter 2026 show at the Grand Palais in March drew reports of editors and buyers queueing for hours at Chanel's Paris boutiques to secure pieces from his early collections. For the year ended 31 December 2025, the house posted revenue of $19.3 billion , 2% higher than the previous year, while operating profit came in at $4.7 billion.

article_title: Frasers extends Accent Group offer to September with all other terms unchanged
sub_title: Frasers Group has extended its £166 million takeover offer for Australian footwear and lifestyle retailer Accent Group until 30 September, without changing its initial A$0.65-a-share bid.
article_content: Frasers Group has extended its £166 million takeover offer for Australian footwear and lifestyle retailer Accent Group until 30 September, without changing its initial A$0.65-a-share bid. The offer had initially been due to close on 30 July. Accent shareholders now have until the close of ASX (Australian Securities Exchange) trading at 4pm Sydney time on 30 September to sell into the offer, unless Frasers extends or withdraws it. The Sports Direct and Flannels owner said no other terms had changed. Frasers made an unconditional, all-cash bid on 15 June , seeking to acquire every fully paid Accent share outside the holdings it and its associates already have. It held approximately 22.9% of Accent when the offer was announced, making it the Australian company’s largest shareholder. The bid for the remaining shares was valued at approximately A$316 million (£166 million). Accent operates close to 900 stores across Australia and New Zealand, including multi-brand footwear retailer Platypus Shoes, and is Frasers’ partner for the regional Sports Direct rollout. Accent’s Independent Board Committee continues to oppose the offer and has unanimously recommended that shareholders reject it, with t he committee describing the bid as “opportunistic and materially inadequate”. Frasers’ A$0.65 offer matched Accent’s closing share price on 12 June, the final trading day before the bid was announced, and therefore included no premium. Accent also pointed out that Frasers paid A$1.718 per share under a subscription agreement in May 2025. Its on-market buying in February 2026 averaged more than A$0.92 per share. The committee said the bid did not capture Accent’s 2030 Strategic Growth Plan, which has targets of at least A$1.9 billion in sales and an EBIT margin of about 9%. The retailer plans to expand its estate to approximately 950 stores by 2030. The extension follows Frasers lifting its stake in German premium fashion company Hugo Boss to 30.28% two days earlier, a level that took it past the mandatory bid threshold under Germany’s takeover rules. Its €38-per-share Hugo Boss offer remains unchanged, with the initial acceptance period due to end on 27 July. Hugo Boss’ management and supervisory boards have advised shareholders to reject the bid as inadequate. Frasers has previously confirmed that its €38-a-share offer is final . Fraser had been steadily building up its stake in the German luxury brand over the last six years. Frasers has also begun a share buyback programme through newly appointed joint broker Panmure Liberum. Under the arrangement, the broker may acquire up to 10 million Frasers shares for a total of no more than £80 million before the group’s next annual general meeting, expected in mid-September.

article_title: Prada Group sales rise as first half revenue tops €3bn
sub_title: The Prada Group has today reported a net revenue rise of 16% (+5% organic) to €3.048 billion year-on-year for the first half of the year ending 30 June 2026, with the second quarter up 7%.
article_content: The Prada Group has today reported a net revenue rise of 16% (+5% organic) to €3.048 billion year-on-year for the first half of the year ending 30 June 2026, with the second quarter up 7%. Retail sales reached €2.633 billion, up 12% year-on-year, with a “robust performance” for Prada, with retail sales up 3% year-on-year. The second quarter accelerated further to +6%, driven by like-for-like full-price sales. Meanwhile, retail sales were also up 3% at Miu Miu, with Q2 in line with Q1, “notwithstanding a more pronounced exposure to the Middle East and against +40% in Q2-25”. All regions except the Middle East reported quarter-on-quarter improvements, with notable strength in the Americas, Japan and APAC. Versace progressed “in line with expectations”, contributing net revenue of €305 million for the half-year. That comes ahead of the debut of Pieter Mulier’s new creative direction. Patrizio Bertelli, Prada Group Chairman and Executive Director, said: “In a geopolitical and macroeconomic scenario that remained turbulent, we continued to execute with rigour. Our commitment to the highest standards of product excellence, nurturing craftsmanship and creativity as non-negotiable pillars, allowed us to reach 22 quarters of uninterrupted organic growth. “The environment is likely to remain volatile; we must stay nimble, innovate continuously, taking advantage of the strength of our manufacturing know-how, and continue to balance short-term discipline with long-term vision.” Andrea Guerra, Prada Group Chief Executive Officer, added: “We close the first six months of the year with solid results, accelerating in the second quarter on a positive Q1. At Prada, the team effort resulted in a strong Q2 performance, and we will continue to work relentlessly across product, retail and communication to drive the brand towards its full potential. “At Miu Miu, the foundations built during the years sustained relevance and desirability against a still challenging comparison base. The arrival of Pieter Mulier at Versace marks the beginning of the brand’s new creative journey, and we are excited to welcome his talent and vision into our Group. “Our strategy is clear, our backbone is strong and, while the environment remains disrupted, we are confident in the strength of our brands and their long-term potential. Looking ahead, we will remain disciplined and agile as we pursue our ambition of delivering above-market growth for the Group.”

article_title: Show report: The word from the stands at Scoop
sub_title: Yesterday, 21 July, saw a circus-themed Scoop wrap after three days at Olympia National in London. For many exhibitors, it certainly delivered, with buyers from stores including Fenwick and Liberty London, hungry to seek out fresh brands.
article_content: Yesterday, 21 July, saw a circus-themed Scoop wrap after three days at Olympia National in London. For many exhibitors, it certainly delivered, with buyers from stores including Fenwick, Liberty London, Cream, The Dressing Room, Pamela Schiffer, Cordelia James, Galeries Lafayette in France and El Corte Ingles in Spain hungry to seek out fresh brands – many new to the show – and standout SS27 collections. TheIndustry.fashion went along to get the word from the big top. Eva Panagiotopoulou, from Come What May I’m based in Athens, Greece, and Come What May is brand new. Scoop is the first time it’s been shown to buyers. I’ve been in the business for almost 30 years as a wholesaler, buyer, stylist and then as a designer for other brands for the past 10 years. Then I decided to create my own ready-to-wear brand. I came up with the idea to make luxury resort wear when I first saw the fabrics this collection has been created from. They are hand block printed and very unique. I loved them as soon as I saw them and I thought they would be perfect to create mix and match pieces. The colours are really beautiful, with stripes and prints as well as monochrome options. In terms of key pieces, we have very nice dresses which work from day to night, as well as kimonos, oversized blouses with voluminous sleeves, wraparound skirts, shirts and wide leg trousers that can be matched together or worn separately. The fabric is a modal satin, it’s not that expensive but it feels like silk. It just feels really nice when you wear it. We’ve had a good reaction to it at the show. It’s been very interesting because people haven’t seen anything else quite like this. That has pleased me as I wanted to do something different. We’re happy that we have seen some buyers we expected to see at the show, including those who have their own boutiques, and we have made some contacts regarding possible agents and distributors for the UK market. Nichola Morgan, showing Devotion Twins Devotion Twins is a Greek brand that’s celebrating its 25th anniversary this year. It’s developed from being very much a resort wear brand into a full ready-to-wear collection. It’s very contemporary with a lot of natural fabrics and real Greek heritage coming through in terms of silhouettes. It’s been in the UK market for 10 years now and we’ve been showing it at Scoop since about 2022. It’s very much a summer collection, but as we go further into ready-to-wear the autumn/winter collections will start to get stronger. We currently have around 25-30 UK accounts, including Daniel of Windsor, Brown Thomas, Very and Monsoon. Liberty has been on today and we’d obviously love to get it in there. We’ve been in Selfridges in the past and, where the brand has evolved from a certain look, we are hoping to get such stores back on board. The show has been fantastic for us. It’s been very busy, particularly straight off the bat for the first two days. We’ve taken on nine new accounts and previous accounts, who thought they might not do the brand any more, have seen the newness and come back. We’ve been writing orders, which is always a positive. After the show, we will have the collection at the Morris Fyfe showroom on Brick Lane in London, where we have another six brands including Sorena handbags and accessories, also from Greece, Emily Lovelock and Valentino handbags and shoes. Devotion Twins is the only one we’ve brought to Scoop. It’s the perfect platform for it because it attracts exactly the right audience. Stephanie Krausch from Chicosoleil I established Chicosoleil 14 years ago with my husband in Paris. It’s very much about the spirit of summer. We do a lot of trade shows and we sell the collection around the world as a result. My husband is currently showing it in Japan and, after the final day of Scoop, I will be travelling to Madrid to show it there, then at the end of September I will be showing in Milan. Having previously shown Chicosoleil at Pure London, I started with Scoop two years ago. It has been great and I am very happy with the response from customers. We currently sell to about 25 UK accounts, including Cleverly Wrapped and other independent boutiques, and we have had success with taking on some new accounts here. The collection is made in India, so my life is split between Paris and there as I manage all the design and production myself. The new collection features handloom fabrics, embroidery, embellishments and signature details such as coloured buttons in the shape of a flower. A key piece is an oversized shirt dress that can be belted in. There’s check and striped versions and it’s a very easy to wear on-trend summer style. We’re showing a collection for April/May 2027 delivery, including standout cotton/viscose fabric pieces with a ‘midnight diamond’ print, as well as a high summer 2027 collection. I always enjoy coming to London and showing at Scoop. Even if my English is not great, I can speak face-to-face with my customers and get a better understanding of what they want. So, it’s very important for me to come. Lea Wu, from Labdip We started the Labdip brand in 2012 in Paris, but my brother and I came into this market because our father was a denim manufacturer for other brands. He knew all about the fits and washes and we learned alongside him. We manufacture in a region next to Shanghai in China. We used to have a factory, but since my father retired the person working with him took it over – so we have continuity. The factory specialises in different denim washes. This is our first time at Scoop and we have managed to take some orders, including from Cordelia James which has three stores (in Hawkhurst, Rye and Lewes), as well as a store in Scotland and one in Ireland. We already work with Mercantile London as well as Ediit, which has two stores in London. We also came here to meet some agents, and we’ve had some interest from local partners, so we are happy. Karen Radley from Scoop has been helping a lot with some matchmaking! Our barrel fit jean is a trending silhouette for women and is currently our best-selling jean, particularly with a natural worn in look, not overdone. We also have a popular relaxed fit wide-leg style with a slightly lower waist. It has a real 90s feel to it. The collection reflects American denim history as we also have a very 70s style flared jean with two front patch pockets. That one is new and is all about really lengthening the silhouette. We have big hopes for that one. We’re also doing some coloured washes, such as dusty pink in the barrel leg which is proving very popular. Straight leg jeans are also coming back, so we have a selection of washes in that fit too, including a stonewash/snow wash combination. Complementing the denim, we have other pieces such as a western style suede shirt which again comes in a dusty pink as well as olive. We’ve also really been inspired by American college looks and we have raglan sleeve two-colour baseball style long-sleeved T-shirts, as well as bandanas and military influenced lightweight nylon long shorts – perfect for the warm weather. Valentine Urso, from Opalina It’s our first showing for the UK market and we are forming part of the Italian Trade Agency presence at Scoop. Opalina is a three-year old brand born out of a factory originally established in 1954 in Puglia. I’d previously worked for over 10 years behind the scenes in the production for other brands, but I always wanted to hone my own vision and use my creativity. I saw the women working at the factory on the old machines and my vision began to take shape for what I wanted the brand to look like. We do have dresses and skirts, but Opalina is primarily a brand that focuses on a modern interpretation of a shirt for women. So, when we’re talking about the key pieces it is really about the shirting which has had something added to it, such as ruffle fronts, embroidery, pleating on the shoulder and puff sleeves. It’s about something that is comfortable, versatile and elegant all in one, using high quality fabrics and natural fibres. One of the key pieces is a lightweight muslin cotton shirt, which is a reinterpretation of a men’s tuxedo shirt design. Instead of vertical pleats it features handmade ruffles on the front. It comes in yellow, which is a strong colour for the SS27 season. We’ve also got classic relaxed fit striped shirts with dropped shoulders and three-quarter length sleeves and plenty of Liberty print fabrics as well, which I love, including for a long skirt. Scoop has been a very important show for us to attend, and we are very happy with the contacts we have made. It’s been a great experience for us, particularly as a young brand. We will come back.

article_title: Dior to stage its first Ireland show at Trinity College Dublin
sub_title: Dior will stage its pre-fall 2027 show at Trinity College Dublin on 4 December 2026, marking the French fashion house’s first runway presentation in Ireland.
article_content: Dior will stage its pre-fall 2027 show at Trinity College Dublin on 4 December 2026, marking the French fashion house’s first runway presentation in Ireland. Jonathan Anderson will unveil the collection at the university’s Old Library. The event will also be the Northern Irish designer’s first fashion show in the country. Dior said: “The collection will be unveiled against the backdrop of the university’s Old Library, an 18th-century building housing a world-class academic and cultural resource.” The Dublin presentation follows Anderson’s Dior autumn/winter 2026/27 haute couture show in Paris . Since taking creative control of the house’s menswear, womenswear and couture divisions, he has become the first designer since Christian Dior to oversee all three. Anderson presented his first Dior haute couture collection at Paris Couture Week in January 2026 . The show brings Anderson back to the city where he started working in fashion. His first role in the industry was at Dublin department store Brown Thomas, while his J.W. Anderson label has previously collaborated with Irish brewer Guinness. In a social media post Anderson shared that he was "so excited and so proud" to be able to show the collection at Ireland's oldest university. "Showing at Trinity College Dublin is a dream come true. I began my career in fashion in Dublin, so returning here feels deeply personal," he added. "To present this collection in such an extraordinary setting – at an institution with such an important cultural history – is a real honour." The Old Library is set for its first major renovation in over 300 years. Trinity College’s redevelopment timetable says the building and its Long Room will remain open to visitors until the end of 2027, when restoration and construction work is scheduled to begin. The project covers structural and environmental upgrades alongside the conservation of the building, manuscripts and research collections. It will also create a Research Collections Study Centre and redesign the exhibition of the library’s treasures. The December runway marks a change from Dior’s pre-fall format under Anderson’s predecessor, Maria Grazia Chiuri. During her tenure, the house released its pre-fall collections through look books in December before staging travelling runway shows around their arrival in stores. Dior’s last pre-fall runway presentation took place in Kyoto in April 2025. The house has not provided a reason for the scheduling change. The Dublin location also links Dior to Carmel Snow, the Dublin-born former editor-in-chief of the US edition of Harper’s Bazaar. According to the Women’s Museum of Ireland, Snow came up with the term 'New Look' after she saw Christian Dior’s debut collection in 1947. Anderson’s save-the-date combines Snow’s description of Dior’s work with a four-leaf clover, an emblem the designer has used during his tenure at the house.

article_title: Temperley London appoints new CEO and Design Director
sub_title: British luxury house Temperley London has appointed Morgaine McGee as Chief Executive Officer and Jack Isenberg as Design Director, completing its leadership team ahead of a new collection in September.
article_content: British luxury house Temperley London has appointed Morgaine McGee as Chief Executive Officer and Jack Isenberg as Design Director, completing its leadership team ahead of a new collection in September. The appointments follow the departure of founder and Creative Director Alice Temperley earlier this month. McGee replaces Sarita Jha, whose tenure as Interim CEO recently ended, while Isenberg will lead the house's design direction. Founded in 2000, Temperley London is known for hand embroidery and occasionwear. The London-headquartered business sells internationally through its stores, e-commerce operation and wholesale partners. McGee brings more than two decades of experience across apparel and accessories, including responsibility for design, product development, production and operations. Her previous senior leadership positions include Co-Chief Executive Officer of product development and manufacturing business The Vertical Collective, which she co-founded. and Managing Director of accessories company Signal Brands. Earlier in her career, she worked at RT Sourcing USA on design and product development for luxury houses including Dior, Chanel and Givenchy. McGee said: “This marks an exciting new chapter for Temperley London as we bring a fresh perspective to the brand, while honouring its legacy, our rich British heritage as well as our commitment to exceptional craftsmanship.” "The brand has created timeless pieces, beautifully created to celebrate women and the moments that shape their lives. I am aware of that history, what people expect of the brand and will work to ensure that continues." Isenberg joins Temperley London from Tom Ford after a career spanning luxury ready-to-wear and couture. A Central Saint Martins graduate, he began his career at Valentino and later held senior design positions at Giambattista Valli, Versace and Nina Ricci. He also held the positions of Head Designer at Ralph & Russo and Design Director at Jenny Packham. “What drew me to this house is its commitment to craft. The embroidery, the finishing. These are things that can only be done by people who know how,” Isenberg said. "It has been great to start working with the talented team here and continuing to bring the quality and craftsmanship that women across the world have come to expect from Temperley London." His first collection for the brand will be presented in September. The leadership changes come two and a half years after Times Square Group LLC and its investment arm, Luxutte Capital, took a majority stake in Temperley London in November 2023 . Alice Temperley and then-CEO Luca Donnini stayed in their roles at first after that deal. When confirming her departure on 8 July, Alice Temperley said the company had been her creative home for more than two decades. She plans to establish an independent creative practice, with further details to be announced.

article_title: Jonathan Saunders to lead Kate Spade creative after &Other Stories exit
sub_title: Kate Spade New York has appointed Jonathan Saunders as Executive Creative Director, effective 26 August, shortly after his departure from H&M Group-owned & Other Stories.
article_content: Kate Spade New York has appointed Jonathan Saunders as Executive Creative Director, effective 26 August, shortly after his departure from H&M Group-owned &Other Stories. Saunders will direct product design and the visual identity of the accessible luxury brand, reporting to Kate Spade President and CEO Eva Erdmann. He will relocate to New York for the role, and work from its Hudson Yards headquarters. The Scottish designer has spent more than two decades working with fashion businesses including Alexander McQueen, Diane von Furstenberg, Calvin Klein, Tiffany & Co. and Pucci. He also founded his namesake label in 2003. “Kate Spade is iconic, and it’s an honor to step into a brand that has such a strong identity and deep emotional connections,” Saunders said in the company announcement. “The brand has a genuine point of view, rich brand codes steeped in its 30-year history, and infinite potential. I’m looking forward to immersing in the brand heritage and connecting that soul with today’s consumers.” Kate Spade added that the Glasgow native and Central Saint Martins graduate "speaks our language: color, youthful femininity, and the unexpected detail that turns every day into something beautiful." Saunders joins as parent company Tapestry works to restore growth at Kate Spade, which it acquired in 2017. Sales fell 11% to $839.8 million during the nine months ended 28 March as the business reduced price promotions. Erdmann, who became Kate Spade President and CEO in October 2024, has been repositioning the brand around its established codes of colour, femininity and wit. Saunders has been tasked with translating that heritage for younger consumers while making its products more recognisable. Tapestry has pointed to early progress in customer acquisition. President and CEO Joanne Crevoiserat said in May that Kate Spade welcomed 400,000 new customers during its third quarter, while cautioning that turnarounds take time and do not follow a linear path. Saunders joined & Other Stories in spring 2025 as its first Chief Creative Officer , overseeing creative direction across product and brand expression. His work included the AW25 “A New Brand Spirit” campaign, which introduced a refreshed logo and tone of voice. His departure was announced in June , with the retailer saying he had decided to go back to the US to be nearer his family. He is due to remain with the business until mid-August to support its transition. &Other Stories had not named a successor when it announced his departure.

article_title: Mulberry cuts losses as turnaround strategy gains momentum
sub_title: Mulberry has significantly reduced its losses and returned to growth in its latest financial year, as the British luxury brand's turnaround strategy continued to gain momentum.
article_content: Mulberry has significantly reduced its losses and returned to growth in its latest financial year, as the British luxury brand's turnaround strategy continued to gain momentum. For the 52 weeks to 28 March 2026, Mulberry reported a loss before tax of £8.9 million, compared with £32.2 million the previous year. Underlying losses narrowed to £8 million from £24.1 million, while the business returned to positive underlying EBITDA of £0.8 million, an improvement of £17.6 million year on year. Group revenue increased 4% to £125.5 million, with growth accelerating in the second half of the year. Retail and digital like-for-like sales rose 9%, while gross margin improved from 67% to 72% as Mulberry focused on full-price trading and reduced promotional activity. The improvement comes as Mulberry continues to execute its "Back to the Mulberry Spirit" strategy under CEO Andrea Baldo, focusing on restoring profitability through stronger full-price trading, reduced promotional activity and renewed investment in the brand. Baldo said: "We returned the business to growth, significantly reduced our losses and strengthened gross margin through greater full-price discipline. Momentum built throughout the year, with a particularly strong second half, demonstrating that the actions we have taken are delivering tangible results." The retailer also reported a strong start to the new financial year, with group revenue rising 23% in the first 13 weeks to 27 June 2026. Retail and digital sales increased 18%, supported by double-digit like-for-like growth across all regions. The latest results build on the progress outlined in Mulberry's trading update earlier this year , when the company reported improving sales across all of its key markets as its turnaround strategy gained traction. They also follow the appointment of Christopher Kane as Ready-to-Wear Creative Director and the brand's planned return to London Fashion Week in September, marking a renewed focus on strengthening its creative credentials. Looking ahead, Mulberry said it remains focused on delivering sustainable long-term growth, with a medium-term target of generating more than £200 million in annual revenue alongside a 15% EBIT margin.

article_title: Secret Shopper: Reformation brings a digital-first approach to the high street
sub_title: Reformation has come a long way since it began as a vintage clothing boutique in Los Angeles in 2009. The sustainable womenswear brand has grown into a global fashion business, known for its vintage-inspired silhouettes, celebrity following and focus on lower-impact production.
article_content: Reformation has come a long way since it began as a vintage clothing boutique in Los Angeles in 2009. The sustainable womenswear brand has grown into a global fashion business, known for its vintage-inspired silhouettes, celebrity following and focus on lower-impact production. Now preparing to list on the New York Stock Exchange with a target valuation of up to $1bn , the retailer operates more than 70 stores across the US, UK, Canada and France. Since launching its Retail X concept in 2017, Reformation has attempted to merge the convenience of e-commerce with physical retail, using technology to simplify browsing and trying on clothes. TheIndustry.fashion visited its Covent Garden store to find out whether the concept really improves the shopping experience. Located on King Street in the heart of Covent Garden, Reformation sits among luxury fashion retailers, restaurants and independent boutiques. Just around the corner from the Piazza, cheers from the crowds gathered around the street performers remind you that you're shopping in one of London's busiest areas. A velvet rope was set up outside the entrance anticipating crowds, but thankfully there was no queue when I visited on a weekday afternoon. Reformation has built its reputation dressing Instagram's cool girls, but inside I found a much broader range of shoppers. There was a mix of Londoners, tourists, a man in a suit stopping by after work and two children playing on their phones while their family members tried things on. Like the brand itself, the exterior is understated. Large windows allow passers-by to see straight into the minimalist space and there are just a couple of mannequins showcasing simple outfits. A security guard welcomed every customer before giving us a small card with a QR code. At first, I wasn't entirely sure why. It wasn't immediately obvious that this was how you joined the virtual fitting room queue, and without a brief explanation it could easily be mistaken for a piece of marketing. Five members of staff moved around the shop floor, dressed in their own clothes rather than uniforms, but their earpieces helpfully gave away who actually worked there. They were friendly and approachable, checking whether shoppers wanted to try anything on without being overly pushy. My first impression was just how little product there appeared to be. In most cases, there is just one item of each design on display, giving the feel of a carefully curated showroom rather than a traditional high street store. At first, it felt too limited, but the staff quickly explained that additional sizes were held in the stockroom. Warm lighting and generous spacing between displays create a calm shopping environment, while indie music quietly plays in the background. During London’s July heatwave, the air conditioning was rather welcome and made it easy to spend longer browsing. I gravitated towards the summer dresses, unable to face trying on anything heavier. With many dresses sitting around the £200 mark, this isn't a brand built around impulse purchases. The quality largely reflects those prices too. Fabrics felt substantial, the construction appeared well finished and the pieces looked every bit as polished in person as they do online. I was told there would be a 20 to 25-minute wait for a fitting room but it ended up being around half an hour. I managed to grab a seat on one of the sofas while I waited, but others weren’t so fortunate. Several customers left before their names were called, leaving staff calling for them across the shop floor. It wasn't quite the seamless experience the technology promises. Once it was my turn, it became clear that the fitting rooms are meant to be the selling point of the entire store. Each changing room features a touchscreen displaying every item currently available in-store, along with every available colour and size. Until this point, first-time visitors could easily assume the product selection is much smaller than it actually is. Rather than getting dressed again and hunting through the store, you can tap the item you want and continue trying things on while a member of staff retrieves it. I requested a top I had seen on Reformation’s Instagram and it arrived within a couple of minutes. I also used the touchscreen to request a couple of items I hadn't spotted on the shop floor, which proved genuinely useful. That said, the system isn't perfect. Because shoppers can keep requesting additional items without ever leaving their fitting room, it's easy to see why waiting times begin to build. While the technology improves the experience once you're inside, it arguably creates a bottleneck for everyone still waiting outside. Reformation's technology genuinely improves the fitting room experience and makes it far easier to browse the full collection than in a traditional store. However, the lengthy wait, digital requests and staff ferrying garments between the stockroom and changing rooms suggest the system may struggle during busier periods. While the technology is useful, it gives the shopping experience an almost industrial feel that is slightly at odds with the sense of luxury the brand's price point suggests. I left empty-handed, not because I couldn't find anything I liked. The dresses were flattering, well made and true to size. They simply sat outside my budget. For shoppers willing to spend £200 to £300 on a dress, Reformation offers one of the most innovative retail concepts on the high street, even if the reality feels a little less effortless than the brand's carefully curated online image suggests.

article_title: JD Sports appoints Darren Shapland as interim Chair
sub_title: JD Sports Fashion has appointed Independent Non-Executive Director Darren Shapland as Interim Chair, following its Annual General Meeting on 21 July 2026.
article_content: JD Sports Fashion has appointed Independent Non-Executive Director Darren Shapland as Interim Chair, following its Annual General Meeting on 21 July 2026. Shapland takes up the position immediately and will remain in place until the global sports-fashion retailer appoints a permanent Chair, according to a JD Sports’ regulatory announcement from 21 July. His appointment follows the departure of Andrew Higginson , who announced in April that he intended to step down after almost four years with the group. JD began searching for a permanent successor at that time, with the process led by Senior Independent Director Kath Smith. As Interim Chair, Shapland has stepped down as Chair of JD’s ESG Committee but will remain a member. He has also left the Audit & Risk Committee for the duration of his interim appointment. Non-Executive Director Sarah Kuijlaars has chaired that committee since succeeding Ian Dyson on 1 June 2026. Shapland joined the JD board in June 2023 and has extensive experience across retail leadership, financial management and ecommerce operations. He trained as an accountant at Burton Group and later held senior roles at Superdrug and Sainsbury’s. He served as Sainsbury’s Chief Financial Officer from 2005 to 2010 before becoming Group Development Director. His other previous positions include CEO of home furnishings retailer Carpetright and Chair of Poundland and NotOnTheHighStreet. Higginson joined JD as Chair in July 2022 following the departure of former Executive Chairman Peter Cowgill . During his tenure, JD refocused on sports fashion, strengthened its governance and control systems, expanded overseas and bought out minority interests in subsidiaries. His planned exit came after reports of a disagreement over Chief Executive Régis Schultz . JD said the change had been mutually agreed with Higginson and denied any dispute over the board’s continued support for Schultz. The leadership transition comes as JD manages subdued demand across parts of its international business. For the year ended 31 January 2026, revenue was £12.66 billion , while profit before tax and adjusting items came in at £852 million, down from £923 million.

article_title: Depop teams up with Zara Larsson for global campaign
sub_title: Resale fashion marketplace Depop has launched a new global campaign starring Grammy-nominated artist Zara Larsson, celebrating personal style, creativity and second-hand fashion.
article_content: Resale fashion marketplace Depop has launched a new global campaign starring Grammy-nominated artist Zara Larsson, celebrating personal style, creativity and second-hand fashion. The four-part content series, directed by filmmaker Dave Meyers, explores Depop’s role as a platform for discovering, buying and selling unique fashion pieces, with Larsson bringing her own approach to styling into the campaign. Shot in Sweden and styled by Caterina Ospina, the campaign reflects Larsson’s personal mix of vintage and contemporary fashion, highlighting how consumers are increasingly using resale platforms to create individual wardrobes beyond traditional fashion trends. "Fashion has always been one of the ways I express myself,” said Larsson. “I love mixing vintage with newer pieces and finding things that feel unexpected. That’s why I’ve always loved Depop.” A post shared by Depop (@depop) To coincide with the campaign launch on 21 July, Depop is introducing The Zara Larsson Edit, an exclusive Depop Shop featuring 20 to 30 pieces curated from the artist’s personal wardrobe, alongside upcycled merchandise and one-of-a-kind fashion finds including designer items. The collection aims to give fans access to Larsson’s personal style while reinforcing Depop’s focus on circular fashion and extending the life cycle of clothing. Steve Dool, Brand and Creative Director at Depop, said: “Zara has an incredible eye for style because she approaches fashion with curiosity rather than rules.” “Her mix of vintage, emerging designers and personal treasures feels effortless, and that’s exactly the spirit of Depop.” Founded in 2011, Depop has grown into one of the leading resale fashion marketplaces, with approximately 56 million registered users globally. The platform has positioned itself around community-led shopping, encouraging users to buy and sell second-hand clothing while creating a more circular approach to fashion consumption. The campaign comes as Depop enters a new phase of growth following eBay’s proposed $1.2 billion acquisition of the platform from Etsy . The deal was cleared by the UK Competition and Markets Authority earlier this month, removing a key regulatory hurdle and allowing the transaction to proceed. The acquisition forms part of eBay’s wider strategy to strengthen its position in fashion resale, while Depop is expected to retain its name, brand, platform and community focus following completion of the deal.
