Cubitts opens first Manchester store in Northern Quarter
sub_title: British spectacle maker Cubitts has opened its first Manchester store, marking the brand's long-awaited arrival in the city after almost a decade of searching for the right location.
article_content: British spectacle maker Cubitts has opened its first Manchester store, marking the brand's long-awaited arrival in the city after almost a decade of searching for the right location. Situated at 16 Smithfield Buildings on Hilton Street in the Northern Quarter, the new shop becomes Cubitts' 21st worldwide and 19th in the UK. The opening follows the launch of The Yard, the brand's new headquarters and optical manufactory in King's Cross, London, earlier this year. Cubitts said it had deliberately waited to secure a site that reflected its focus on craftsmanship, fitting and spectacle repair, rather than opening simply to establish a presence in Manchester. The store occupies part of the former Affleck & Brown department store, a landmark building dating back to the 1860s that was once known as the "Harrods of the North". Designed in partnership with Manchester-based studio YOUTH, the space has been conceived as a working optician, with eye examination rooms, a dedicated repairs desk, bespoke consultation areas and display space for optical frames and sunglasses. Tom Broughton, founder of Cubitts, said: “We've been looking for the right home in Manchester for almost a decade. We wanted to be in the Northern Quarter, but only if we could find a building with the history and character to justify our arrival. Smithfield Buildings felt immediately right.” “Manchester does not need another London brand telling it how interesting it is. We're simply pleased to finally be here, and hope to make ourselves useful.” Broughton added that it was important the shop was designed in Manchester rather than being "deposited" into the city, with references to the city's industrial and creative heritage incorporated through its materials, furnishings and artwork. Alongside its range of optical frames and sunglasses, the store will offer eye examinations, repairs, reglazing, made-to-measure frames and bespoke spectacle consultations. Cubitts also confirmed that a collection of Manchester-exclusive frames is in development and will be announced separately. Founded in King's Cross in 2013, Cubitts has built its reputation around handcrafted spectacles designed to be repaired rather than replaced. Last month, the company opened its 13,000 sq ft headquarters and optical manufactory , The Yard, bringing design, manufacturing, repairs and training together under one roof in central London. The Manchester opening represents the latest step in the brand's continued investment in its UK retail and service network. Mango on track for €4bn revenue target as first half sales climb
sub_title: Mango increased first-half turnover by 7.2% to €1.852 billion, with growth reaching 10.7% at constant exchange rates as it continued to expand its UK store network.
article_content: Mango increased first-half turnover by 7.2% to €1.852 billion (£1.61 billion), with growth reaching 10.7% at constant exchange rates as it continued to expand its UK store network. Summary of results: Mango’s first half performance keeps it within reach of its €4 billion (£3.48 billion) full-year revenue ambition, although the company did not publish interim EBITDA or net profit. The brand's womenswear offering continued to lead sales during the half-year, followed by menswear, as well as its kids and teen offering. Growth came from both stores and digital trading, with online revenues seeing double-digit growth, generating 32% of total sales. The brand noted that 77% of the company’s total turnover was generated by its international business, which Mango says is a reflection of its "strong global presence and geographic diversification". Spain remained Mango’s largest market and recorded double-digit growth during the half, followed by France, Turkey, Germany and the US. The UK remains one of the brand's strategic markets. The group also highlighted that it had invested nearly €90 million during the period to support expansion, operations, technology and its campus. Toni Ruiz, Chairman and CEO of Mango, said: “We are entering the final stretch of our 4Es 2024–2026 Strategic Plan with a clear ambition to reach €4 billion in revenue this year. Our first half results demonstrate continued positive momentum, with growth ahead of the wider market, further strengthening our position as one of the leading international fashion brands.” Under the Elevate pillar of its strategic plan, the brand had continued to strengthen its differentiated value proposition, centred on original design, quality and an aspirational brand position. Its appointment of Hailey Bieber as the face of its Woman line’s Summer 2026 campaign , as well as its collaborations with British tailoring house Richard James and American label Eckhaus Latta have formed part of its elevation strategy. The results follow a record 2025 financial year, which saw Mango's annual sales increase by 13% to €3.8 billion (£3.31 billion), while EBITDA rose 13% to €722 million (£628 million). Net profit grew 11% to €242 million (£211 million). At the publication of the full-year figures in March, Ruiz said the company had achieved “record growth across our key indicators” after investing in its business model and international expansion. The retailer continued its UK expansion with 10 openings during the half, including stores on Kensington High Street and King’s Road in London, as well as Cheltenham. Mango had previously outlined plans to add 15 UK stores during 2026 and opened its 26th London location at One New Change in May. Mango ended June with more than 2,960 points of sale across over 120 markets after opening 127 stores and renovating another 37. International operations accounted for more than three-quarters of turnover.

article_title: Harvey Nichols bidders asked to commit up to £60 million for turnaround
sub_title: Bidders for Harvey Nichols have been asked to commit between £50 million and £60 million over the medium term to fund the luxury department store group’s transformation plan.
article_content: Bidders for Harvey Nichols have been asked to commit between £50 million and £60 million over the medium term to fund the luxury department store's transformation plan, Sky News reported. The proposed investment, which would be separate from the acquisition price, would support a refurbishment of the Edinburgh store, international expansion, digital development and the management team’s business plan. Potential bidders currently include Frasers Group and Modella Capital, the owner of Hobbycraft and TGJones, as well as Dubai-based Chalhoub Group and India’s Reliance Retail. Indicative offers have reportedly been received from UK bidders, while international bidders are working to a different timetable. Sir Dickson Poon’s family, which owns Harvey Nichols, has appointed FTI Consulting to advise on the sale and regional advisers to attract interest from potential Gulf-based buyers. NEXT emerged as a potential bidder earlier in July , with sources saying the retailer intended to examine the business closely. It remains unclear whether NEXT would retain Harvey Nichols’ regional store network or focus on the brand and its intellectual property. Frasers Group then entered the process two weeks ago, despite concerns among some Harvey Nichols suppliers about its potential ownership. Frasers owns Sports Direct, Flannels and House of Fraser. A Harvey Nichols executive told suppliers at the time that the company was “obliged to allow Frasers Group to participate in the process alongside the other interested parties”. The memo said its admission was intended to ensure a competitive process and find the right partner for the retailer’s next phase. Harvey Nichols stocks hundreds of luxury labels. Supplier concerns have focused on whether a new owner would maintain its market positioning and existing brand relationships. The requested funding would extend a three-year transformation programme led by Chief Executive Julia Goddard, who joined Harvey Nichols in June 2024. The strategy has refocused the business on fashion, beauty and hospitality while reducing non-core operations. The department store has also continued to reshape its commercial leadership, including the promotion of Shaun Donnelly to Buying Director for Non-Apparel and Menswear. The retailer has already invested in its Knightsbridge flagship, including a fourth-floor wellness destination and a redesigned ground floor focused on jewellery , lifestyle products and flexible brand spaces. Its wider retail revival plan has also included digital investment and the addition of new fashion brands. For the year to 31 March 2024, Harvey Nichols posted revenue of £204.8 million, a 5% decline, while pre-tax losses increased to £34 million. That marked the group’s fifth consecutive annual loss. The business has about 1,200 employees in the UK and runs seven stores in the UK and Ireland, with large-format sites in London, Edinburgh, Birmingham, Leeds and Manchester, plus smaller-format branches in Bristol and Dublin. Internationally, it operates six large-format stores in Riyadh, Doha, Dubai, Hong Kong and Kuwait. The softer luxury goods market, together with the ending of VAT-free shopping for tourists after Brexit, has been pointed to as a major reason for the prolonged losses. Sir Dickson’s Dickson Concepts International acquired Harvey Nichols from Burton Group for £53 million in 1991. The retailer now operates seven stores across the UK and Ireland alongside an international network in the Middle East and Asia.

article_title: Meadowhall strengthens fashion line-up with Mint Velvet, Belstaff and Michael Kors deals
sub_title: Meadowhall has strengthened its luxury fashion offer after securing new stores from Mint Velvet and Belstaff, alongside a major refurbishment of Michael Kors’ existing flagship at The Avenue, the shopping centre’s premium fashion and lifestyle destination.
article_content: Meadowhall is strengthening its luxury fashion offer after securing new stores from Mint Velvet and Belstaff, alongside a major refurbishment of Michael Kors’ existing flagship at The Avenue, the shopping centre’s premium fashion and lifestyle destination. The latest deals form part of Meadowhall’s ongoing strategy to expand The Avenue with a curated mix of aspirational fashion brands and upgraded retail concepts. Mint Velvet will open a 1,700 sq ft store on The Avenue’s Upper Level, opposite Flannels and Sweaty Betty. The womenswear brand, known for its “relaxed glamour” aesthetic, will join the centre’s growing luxury fashion line-up later this year. Meanwhile, British heritage brand Belstaff has signed for a 1,400 sq ft store, strengthening Meadowhall’s menswear offer with its collection of outwear, clothing and accessories inspired by the brand’s motorcycling heritage. Michael Kors has also invested in a significant refurbishment of its existing 2,600 sq ft store, introducing the brand’s latest retail concept alongside a new double-height shopfront in line with The Avenue’s updated design principles. Richard Crowther, Retail Leasing Director at British Land, said: “We are focused on creating an aspirational, best-of-British and global mix on The Avenue, shaping a complete experience that responds to the way our visitors want to shop aspirational retail.” Liz Houghton, CEO and Co-Founder of Mint Velvet, added: “Our customers are at the heart of every decision we make, so opening at Meadowhall feels like a natural next step. We're excited to create a beautiful space where women can discover a capsule wardrobe and our take on the trends.” The latest signings follow a series of investments at Meadowhall as the shopping centre continues to attract international fashion brands. Earlier this year , Inditex announced regional debuts for Stradivarius and Pull&Bear at the destination, while Crew Clothing recently opened a new 2,000 sq ft store on The Avenue.

article_title: SKIMS opens first UK flagship on London’s Regent Street
sub_title: SKIMS has officially opened its first standalone UK store on London's Regent Street, marking a significant step in the brand's international retail expansion.
article_content: SKIMS has opened its first standalone UK flagship store on London's Regent Street, marking a significant step in the brand's international expansion. The 12,000 sq ft flagship occupies the former Ted Baker site at 245-247 Regent Street, following the announcement last year that the shapewear and lifestyle brand had signed a 10-year lease with The Crown Estate. The store offers SKIMS' full product range, including shapewear, underwear, loungewear, menswear and accessories, alongside seasonal collections and pieces from the NikeSKIMS collaboration. Designed by architect Rafael de Cárdenas, the space features open-plan interiors, sculptural displays and a large sculpture by artist Vanessa Beecroft. The opening marks SKIMS' first permanent retail store in the UK, where the brand has previously been available through wholesale partners including Selfridges, Harrods and END. Jens Grede, co-founder and CEO of SKIMS, said: “Our flagship stores play an important role in how customers experience SKIMS beyond the product.” “Opening on Regent Street is a significant milestone for the brand and reflects our continued investment in creating immersive retail destinations in the world’s leading shopping cities.” Kim Kardashian, co-founder and Chief Creative Officer, added: "London has always been one of the most inspiring fashion cities in the world to me, so opening our first UK flagship on Regent Street feels especially exciting.” The London launch follows a period of rapid growth for the business. In late 2025, SKIMS secured a $225 million funding round that valued the company at $5 billion , fuelling further investment in physical retail as well as apparel and the NikeSKIMS partnership. The Regent Street flagship is one of a series of international openings, with a new flagship at Dubai Mall and stores also planned for Delhi and Mumbai. Founded by Kim Kardashian, Jens Grede and Emma Grede in 2019, SKIMS began as a direct-to-consumer shapewear brand before expanding into underwear, swimwear, loungewear and menswear. The Regent Street opening reflects the brand's continued investment in physical retail, as SKIMS builds a global network of flagship stores to complement its online business and wholesale partnerships.

article_title: Editors' Top Reads: News from Reformation, Frasers, Scoop and more...
sub_title: Here are some of this week’s news and features highlights handpicked by TheIndustry.fashion team.
article_content: Here are some of this week’s news and features highlights handpicked by TheIndustry.fashion team. Frasers Group is continuing to push forward with its takeover plans for both German luxury brand Hugo Boss and Australia-based Accent Group. On Tuesday, Frasers Group increased its stake in Hugo Boss to 30.28% , crossing Germany’s mandatory bid threshold, meaning that it is now obligated to make a takeover offer. Frasers Group had previously doubled down on its €38-per-share offer and said that it would not increase the price. Hugo Boss' board responded with a recommendation for shareholders to reject Frasers takeover offer, which they called "inadequate". Just because the formal process for a takeover offer has now been triggered, it does not mean that the board will change its mind and accept the offer. Interestingly, Frasers has been in a similar position before. In 2024, the group launched a takeover bid for British luxury brand Mulberry, in which it held around a 37% stake. Yet Mulberry's biggest shareholder, Challice, which owned a 56.4% stake, opposed Frasers' bid and the offer did not go through. So, while Frasers remains a major stakeholder within Mulberry, it does not control the business. Just two days later, Frasers announced an extension for its £166 million takeover offer for Australian footwear and lifestyle retailer Accent Group, without, however, changing any other of its terms, including its initial A$0.65-a-share bid. So, Frasers again doubled down on its initial offer price, even though Accent’s Independent Board Committee had previously recommended that shareholders reject the bid, which it described as “opportunistic and materially inadequate”. The offer had initially been due to close on 30 July, but Accent shareholders now have until the close of ASX (Australian Securities Exchange) trading on 30 September to sell into the offer. I, for one, am very interested to see how both of these offers will play out. Camilla Rydzek, Senior News & Features Writer. Well, it's a start and it's very early days. Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who took office on Monday, has shown he means business when he pledged business rates reform. For too long, retailers have borne an unfair burden when it comes to this tax and it needs to be addressed. The first beneficiaries of Burnham's reforms will be pubs and social clubs . Night clubs are not included, and nor are, more mysteriously, restaurants. As for bars, well, that apparently is a grey area and it may come down to local authorities to decide who should ultimately benefit from the 20% cut. Let's start by being positive because apparently more reforms are in the pipeline and it is to be hoped retail will be included in some form (particularly independent retailers) and anything that helps to keep life on our high streets has to be a good thing. Burnham has clearly chosen to go early with the pubs news since it fits with his personal branding, which centres on supporting "working class values" (though it sits awkwardly to suggest pubs are the preserve of the working class and that the working class will be brought onside thanks to tax relief for pubs) and also because the pub trade has a very high-profile lobbying campaign to push its interests to the top of the Government agenda. Many high profile people got behind the pub industry, including, curiously, former Chancellor Rachel Reeves (who seemed to be able to gloss over the fact that her employer's NI hikes were a major contributing factor to the sector's distress). Still, good for the pub trade, let's hope the retail industry can keep the pressure on and deliver a similar result. Lauretta Roberts, Co-founder, CEO and Editor-in-Chief. I have to say there always seems to be a feel-good factor among exhibitors at Scoop , and this week’s circus-themed edition was no different. It also always seems to offer up a lot of newness, testament to the research and curation skills of Scoop’s founder and Managing Director, Karen Radley, who this time around had partnered with the Italian Trade Agency (ITA) to bring an exclusive collective of 32 contemporary Italian designers to the show, many of which were making their debut. What’s also great is the people you meet and the stories behind the brands. Some are really fascinating, such as Eva Panagiotopoulou, founder and Creative Director of Come What May from Athens in Greece. Having been in the business for almost 30 years in various roles, the past 10 of which as a designer for other brands, this was the first outing for her very own brand – conceived when she fell in love with some very unique hand-block printed fabrics that she came across. Then there’s the story of Labdip, another first time showing at Scoop, with Director General Léa Wu explaining how her father had been a denim manufacturer, with his own factory, in Shanghai, China, specialising in washes and fits. Now retired, he passed on his knowledge and skill set to his daughter and son, and it was great to talk denim at a show such as Scoop, perhaps not usually associated with it. Another interesting one, and first-time exhibitor, was Valentina Urso, Creative Director of Opalina – one of the 32 Italian brands falling under the ITA partnership umbrella . Urso had previously worked for over 10 years behind the scenes in production for other brands. She then discovered an old factory originally established in 1954 in Puglia. She was fascinated by the women that worked in the factory, and thrilled to find the old ways of making still intact, so three year ago she set about launching her own brand specialising in modern interpretations of women’s shirts, with hand crafted details such as ruffle fronts, embroidery, pleating on the shoulder and puff sleeves. Another great find and confirmation that any womenswear buyer worth their salt should always aim to attend Scoop. It really is quite inspiring. Tom Bottomley, Contributing Editor. I really enjoyed writing a ‘Secret Shopper’ as it was my first feature for TheIndustry.fashion. It gave me the opportunity to experience a store not just as a shopper, but from a retail perspective, paying attention to how every part of the customer journey is designed to shape the shopping experience and influence purchasing decisions. What stood out to me most was Reformation's touchscreen fitting rooms. Being able to request different sizes and styles without leaving the changing room was genuinely useful, but I could also see how the technology created new challenges and contributed to longer waiting times. As more retailers look to incorporate digital convenience and increasingly AI into physical shopping, it will be interesting to see whether concepts like this become more common on the high street and, ultimately, which ones prove to be worthwhile investments. Read the full feature here . Catherine Rowe-Kosary, Junior News Writer.

article_title: Fred Perry partners Westminster Menswear Archive ahead of 75th anniversary
sub_title: Fred Perry has unveiled a new research partnership with the Westminster Menswear Archive ahead of its 75th anniversary in 2027. The collaboration with the
article_content: Fred Perry has unveiled a new research partnership with the Westminster Menswear Archive ahead of its 75th anniversary in 2027. The collaboration with the Westminster Menswear Archive will be led by its Director, Professor Andrew Groves, who will take a deep dive into Fred Perry’s founding years, drawing on personal archives, company records, patents and sporting press to document the brand’s sporting origins from 1952. Rob Gaitt, Fred Perry Brand Director, said: “Andrew’s focus on the founding years has given us a wonderful blueprint for our approach to 2027. A brand founded on product that was fit for purpose, aspirational not elitist, which talked directly to fans and players. Using selective distribution, authenticated by champions via collaborations. Sportswear, not just tennis.” The Westminster Menswear Archive is a teaching, research and collecting resource at the University of Westminster. It holds over 3,000 garments and related objects, particularly sportswear, workwear, military pieces and designer fashion. To set the tone for the 75th anniversary year, Fred Perry put on a fashion show at the V&A East Storehouse in June. It centred on ‘Fred Perry Retold’, which “celebrates what came before to look forward”. It gave a snapshot of a new sportswear range that will be presented throughout 2027. Richard Gilmore, Managing Director of Fred Perry, said: “As we commemorate this landmark anniversary, we honour the heritage of our brand and the principles set on and off the court by the man himself, all whilst looking forward to many decades more of championing the Laurel Wreath. “We remain modernists, our ambition and absolute dedication set a brave new agenda for where the next 75 years will take us.” As well as its strong heritage in sport and its links to the British music scene, along with its connections to style tribes including mods, skinheads and rude boys, Fred Perry has long championed UK designers including Craig Green, Charles Jeffrey and Nicolas Daley through collaborations. In a nod to its continued support of up-and-coming design talent, Fred Perry has also announced a patronage with the British Fashion Council. The partnership will work to amplify and celebrate some of the most creative designers in the UK, using the brand’s global platform and targeted distribution around the world to further promote the talented roster of collaborators, past and present. Natalie Porter, Director of Network at The British Fashion Council, said: “We are delighted to welcome Fred Perry as a Patron of the British Fashion Council. “Ours is a shared commitment to championing British designer talent, celebrating the strength of community, and recognising the powerful connection between fashion and culture. We look forward to building a meaningful partnership that supports the future of British creativity.” In March, Fred Perry opened a new flagship Soho store at 40-42 Lexington Street, adding to its long-standing store around the corner at 12 Newburgh Street. Described as “not just a shop, but a meeting point for like-minded individuals and an event-ready space to celebrate all things Fred Perry”, it signified the brand’s first steps towards celebrating its 75th year.

article_title: Deckers sales rise as HOKA and international markets drive growth
sub_title: Deckers Brands, the US footwear group behind HOKA, UGG and Teva, reported net sales of $1.020 billion (£765 million) for the three months ended 30 June 2026, making it Deckers' first first-quarter result above $1 billion (£750 million).
article_content: Deckers Brands, the US footwear group behind HOKA, UGG and Teva, reported net sales of $1.020 billion (£765 million) for the three months ended 30 June 2026, an increase of 5.7%, with performance driven by HOKA and international sales growth. Deckers’ first-quarter performance was led by HOKA, which generated about 69% of group revenue. Sales increased 7.7% from $653.1 million (£489.8 million) to $703.5 million (£527.6 million). UGG remained the second-largest brand, growing 4.9% from $265.1 million (£198.8 million) to $278 million (£208.5 million). Revenue from other brands, including footwear brand Teva, declined 18.1% to $37.9 million (£28.4 million). Deckers said this reflected, in part, the impact of phasing out Koolaburra’s standalone operations. International sales rose 8.4% to $502.1 million (£376.6 million), accounting for nearly half of group sales. The company did not break down the performance of the UK market. Domestic sales were also up 3.2% to $517.4 million (£388.1 million). During the quarter, HOKA opened its first UK outlet pop-up at Gunwharf Quays in Portsmouth , offering footwear and apparel at discounts of at least 30% off full retail prices. Direct-to-consumer revenue rose 13% to $352.8 million (£264.6 million), with comparable DTC sales up 6.8%. Wholesale remained the larger channel at $666.7 million (£500.0 million), representing an increase of 2.2%. Although gross margin improved from 55.8% to 56.4%, selling, general and administrative expenses increased from $372.6 million (£279.5 million) to $419.9 million (£314.9 million). Operating income consequently fell 6% to $155.3 million (£116.5 million), while net income declined to $130 million (£97.5 million) from $139.2 million (£104.4 million). President and CEO Stefano Caroti said: “Deckers delivered a solid start to the fiscal year, surpassing $1 billion of first quarter revenue for the first time.” Deckers maintained its fiscal 2027 sales guidance of $5.86 billion (£4.40 billion) to $5.91 billion (£4.43 billion). The company expects low-double-digit growth from HOKA and mid-single-digit growth from UGG.

article_title: Reformation targets $1bn valuation as IPO process begins
sub_title: Sustainable womenswear brand Reformation is targeting a valuation of up to $1bn as it begins the roadshow for its initial public offering (IPO) on the New York Stock Exchange.
article_content: Sustainable womenswear brand Reformation is targeting a valuation of up to $1bn as it begins the roadshow for its initial public offering (IPO) on the New York Stock Exchange. The Los Angeles-based brand is offering 14.06 million shares of common stock priced between $15 and $17 per share. At the top end of the range, the offering could raise up to $293 million (£218.6 million), with the company’s valuation reaching approximately $1 billion (£746 million) once outstanding shares are taken into account. Of the shares being offered, around 9.5 million will be issued by Reformation, while the remaining shares will be sold by existing stockholders. Underwriters will also have the option to purchase an additional 2.1 million shares within 30 days of the offering. The IPO remains subject to market conditions, with Reformation stating there is no guarantee regarding whether or when the offering will be completed or its final size and terms. The company filed to list on the New York Stock Exchange last month under the ticker symbol REF, with J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley acting as lead bookrunners. Founded in 2009 as a vintage clothing boutique in Los Angeles, Reformation has grown into a global direct-to-consumer fashion business, operating more than 70 stores across the US, UK, Canada and France, while serving customers in more than 150 countries online. The brand reported revenue of $507.1 million (£378.3 million) for the year ended 27 December 2025, up from $438.2 million (£327.0 million) the previous year, although net profit declined from $33 million (£24.6 million) to $12.6 million (£9.4 million). In the first quarter of 2026, Reformation recorded revenue growth of 30.4% year-on-year to $112.3 million (£83.8 million). The IPO follows several years of expansion for the brand , which has positioned itself around sustainable materials, limited-edition collections and a vertically integrated manufacturing model. Around 90% of Reformation’s sales are generated through its own direct-to-consumer channels, with the company also working with wholesale partners including Selfridges, Harvey Nichols and Liberty in the UK. The listing will test investor appetite for scaled fashion brands built around sustainability, direct retail and strong brand identity, as Reformation joins a wider group of consumer companies exploring public markets. The owners of Alo Yoga, the Los Angeles athleisure brand , shed their wholesale T-shirt business Bella+Canvas last month, with analysts suggesting this clears a path toward an IPO or strategic deal. Authentic Brands Group, owner of Reebok, Ted Baker and GUESS, also recently announced a change in its leadership team, with plans to IPO within the next 12 months.

article_title: Frasers Group acquires Glasgow-based Greaves Sports
sub_title: Frasers Group has acquired the intellectual property of Glasgow retailer Greaves Sports, with its Gordon Street shop and online store set to continue under the established name.
article_content: Frasers Group has acquired the intellectual property of Glasgow retailer Greaves Sports, with its Gordon Street shop and online store set to continue under the established name. No financial terms of the deal have been shared, although it was specified to be an IP transaction. In a statement, Greaves Sports reassured customers that its retail outlets would continue with the "same levels of service and expertise we’ve strived to provide for nearly 100 years". Its six-storey, 30,000 square feet flagship sports store is located at 23 Gordon Street in Glasgow. The family-run business has operated in Glasgow since 1930 and is currently run by Sandy Greaves and his sister Anne Leslie. Documents filed with Companies House show that Greaves changed its name to Clydesdale Sports Retail Limited in June. The deal brings another specialist name into Frasers Group’s portfolio, which includes Sports Direct, Flannels, Game, Evans Cycles and USC. The group also has Scottish retail property interests, including the Braehead Shopping Centre near Glasgow Airport and the Overgate Centre in Dundee. Frasers Group acquired House of Fraser in 2018 and holds the freehold to the building housing its department store on Buchanan Street in Glasgow. The group has also invested in sports, premium fashion and retail property. This builds on Frasers' recent acquisitions spree. In June 2026, the group put forward an unsolicited bid for German luxury brand Hugo Boss . This week, it then increased its holding in the company to 30.28% . Frasers followed up its initial bid for Hugo Boss with another takeover offer for Australia’s Accent Group for £166 million. In the past 18 months alone, Frasers has acquired a majority stake in Italian multi-sport retailer Maxi Sport , taken control of Norwegian sporting goods chain XXL, and added multiple UK designer outlets and shopping centres to its property portfolio. Yet, Hugo Boss would be the most prominent brand asset in Frasers' empire, which also includes Jack Wills and Gieves & Hawkes. As reported when the bid was announced, it would represent a major step in Frasers' "Elevation Strategy" of moving beyond its Sports Direct roots toward premium retail.

article_title: The Team
Scoop could expand Italian brands for AW27 show following fruitful debut ITA partnership
sub_title: This week’s edition of Scoop, held at Olympia National in London from 19-21 July, included the show’s debut partnership with the Italian Trade Agency (ITA).
article_content: This week’s edition of Scoop, held at Olympia National in London from 19-21 July, included the show’s debut partnership with the Italian Trade Agency (ITA). The collaboration saw an exclusive collective of 32 contemporary Italian designers make their debut at Scoop, spanning womenswear, knitwear, accessories and lifestyle collections. With the majority of the brands not yet having any existing UK distribution, it gave a rare opportunity for buyers to discover a new wave of ‘Made in Italy’ creativity and, deemed to be a success, it could see other Italian brands being added to Scoop’s roster for the next show for AW27, taking place at the same venue from 7-9 February 2027. Giving their insights into the collaboration, ITA Director Giovanni Sacchi, and Scoop’s founder and Managing Director Karen Radley, took time out for an exclusive Q&A with TheIndustry.fashion. Giovanni Saachi (GS): The partnership between the Italian Trade Agency and Scoop was born from a shared ambition to strengthen the presence of Italian fashion brands in the UK market. Our London office has closely followed Scoop’s growth over the years, recognising its strong reputation and its perfect alignment with the profile of many Italian contemporary brands. Combined with the increasing interest from Italian companies in the UK and Italy’s strategic focus on boosting exports, this created the ideal opportunity to re-establish an official Italian presence at the show after several years. The strong response from Italian brands confirmed that this was the right moment to build a strategic collaboration. Karen Radley (KR): For me, the partnership came from a shared belief in what Scoop represents. I've always been incredibly selective about the designers we bring to the show because our buyers trust us to introduce them to collections they may not discover elsewhere. When I began working with the Italian Trade Agency, it quickly became clear that we shared the same philosophy. Together, we spent months personally selecting every designer to ensure they reflected the quality, creativity and contemporary positioning that Scoop is known for. Rather than simply creating an Italian pavilion, we wanted to present the designers and their collections within their brand adjacencies. GS: This partnership is particularly beneficial for Italian brands because, as a public institution, ITA provides significant support to reduce the barriers that companies often face when approaching a new market. ITA covers a large part of the costs related to the participation of Italian companies within the collective presence at the event and, most importantly, promotes their involvement through targeted activities designed not only to create awareness around their participation but also to attract the right buyers and industry professionals. Our presence and support have undoubtedly encouraged many companies that, on their own, may not have been able to sustain the costs of exhibiting in London, to recognise that this was the right moment to explore the UK market. Among the 32 participating companies, many are joining Scoop for the first time, while others are returning after several years, and some have confirmed their participation as part of a structured programme carefully developed and managed by the ITA London office. KR: For our buyers, the partnership creates something genuinely special. Instead of having to search across multiple events or showrooms, they can discover an exceptional edit of contemporary Italian designers, all carefully selected to complement the wider Scoop curation. Every collection has been chosen because it offers something distinctive while remaining commercially relevant for premium retailers. It gives buyers confidence that the time they spend at Scoop will be rewarded with new discoveries and meaningful business opportunities. GS: Brexit was certainly a significant turning point that, together with other external factors, has influenced the UK economy in recent years. Five years ago, following the Italian Government’s guidance, our London office established a dedicated Brexit Desk to support Italian companies in understanding the new regulations and adapting to the changes introduced. After an initial period of adjustment, the situation has now largely stabilised. Most Italian companies are already strongly export oriented, and many have experience trading outside the EU, meaning they are familiar with the procedures and costs involved in international business. While Brexit introduced new challenges, companies have progressively adapted their processes and today exporting to the UK has become more structured and predictable. The importance of the UK market remains clear: in 2025, the UK continues to be the 7th largest destination market for Italian clothing exports, after France, the USA, Germany, China, Spain and Switzerland, and before Japan. It also ranks among the top markets for Italian footwear and leather goods, confirming its strategic relevance for Italian brands. Image by FEEL O GS: We have brought a total of 32 Italian brands to Scoop this season through the Italian Trade Agency’s national collective. In addition to these, several other Italian brands are exhibiting independently. The vast majority of the Italian presence at the show is therefore supported by ITA. It is still too early to measure the commercial results, and we will assess the companies' feedback once the event has concluded. However, bringing such a strong national delegation has certainly generated interest and attracted considerable attention within the industry. Combined with Scoop's growing reputation, this enthusiasm gives us every reason to be optimistic about the success of this edition and the potential for future collaborations. KR: Welcoming 32 designers through our partnership with the Italian Trade Agency is a real milestone for Scoop and reflects the growing international confidence in the show. It's also important to remember that these designers sit alongside many other established Italian collections and agents exhibiting independently, making this one of the strongest Italian representations we've ever hosted. The response from buyers throughout the show has been incredibly encouraging, with the Italian designers attracting strong interest from both long-standing retailers and those looking to discover something new. GS: Absolutely. As the Italian Trade Agency, our mission is to promote genuine Made in Italy products around the world, and this is much more than a marketing slogan. The companies we support must meet strict eligibility requirements, including having their production in Italy. This ensures not only the authenticity of the products but also guarantees that the businesses we promote truly represent Italian manufacturing and craftsmanship. The UK remains one of the world's most influential fashion markets and a key destination for Italian exports. British consumers place great value on quality, craftsmanship, authenticity and creativity - qualities that are synonymous with Made in Italy. The premium consumer is also increasingly focused on sustainability and transparency, with more than 60% of UK consumers willing to pay more for products with transparent supply chains. That’s an area in which many Italian companies have invested significantly. GS: It is still too early to make a proper assessment of which brands have received the strongest reaction from UK buyers. Furthermore, as a public institution, we believe it is important to give equal visibility and support to all the companies within our collective, so highlighting one brand over another would not be appropriate. GS: What we can say is that some of the participating brands already have an established presence in the UK and are currently selling through selected retailers or online platforms. However, the majority of the companies are approaching the British market for the first time and see Scoop as an important opportunity to introduce their collections, meet potential partners and identify the right commercial opportunities. Some brands already have strong international recognition, while many others are small and medium-sized designer companies that are highly appreciated within their regions or specialist sectors. That’s a distinctive feature of the Italian fashion industry, where craftsmanship, creativity and niche expertise play a central role. GS: Once we have collected and analysed the feedback from the participating companies, we will have a clearer understanding of where to focus our efforts and how to further develop the initiative. In coordination with our headquarters, we will evaluate the best possible approach for future editions. Our ambition is always to improve and build on previous experiences. If all the right conditions continue to align, we are confident that we will be able to replicate and potentially further strengthen our presence at future editions of Scoop. KR: From Scoop's perspective, this has been an incredibly exciting collaboration. The response from both buyers and designers has reinforced what we hoped to achieve, creating an inspiring destination for contemporary Italian fashion within the wider Scoop edit. We see this as the beginning of a long-term relationship and would love to continue building on it in future seasons, bringing even more exceptional Italian designers to the UK market while maintaining the careful curation that defines Scoop.

article_title: Schuh appoints new President as Colin Temple retires after 38 years
sub_title: Schuh has appointed Tomas Petersson as its new president, succeeding Colin Temple, who is retiring after 38 years with the footwear retailer.
article_content: Schuh has appointed Tomas Petersson as its new President, succeeding Colin Temple, who is retiring after 38 years with the footwear retailer. Petersson will join the business at the end of July and work alongside Temple over the coming months to ensure a smooth leadership transition. He will report to Andy Gray, CEO of Journeys Global Retail Group, which brings together Schuh, Journeys and Little Burgundy under Genesco's youth-focused footwear division. Colin Temple (left) and Tomas Petersson (right) Petersson brings more than 30 years of international leadership experience across the footwear and sporting goods industries. He joins from a consultancy role, having previously served as Senior Vice President and General Manager for Europe, the Middle East and Africa at Foot Locker. Earlier in his career, he held senior executive positions at Intersport and Puma, leading retail, commercial and omnichannel operations across Europe and Asia. His appointment comes as Schuh continues to invest in its long-term growth strategy. Earlier this year , the retailer returned to Leeds with a new store at Trinity Leeds, appointed Laura King as Chief Marketing Officer and outlined plans to strengthen its digital capabilities after reporting a sharp decline in annual profits following weaker Black Friday and Christmas trading. Petersson said: “I am honoured to join Schuh and the Genesco family at such an exciting time.” “Colin and the team have built an outstanding business serving the youth customer with a unique culture, exceptional people and strong brand partnerships. I look forward to building on that foundation, accelerating growth, strengthening our footwear leadership, and delivering an even better experience for our customers, colleagues and brand partners.” Temple joined Schuh as a merchandiser in 1988 before becoming Managing Director in 2002 and later President. During his tenure, he helped establish the retailer as one of the UK's leading footwear specialists, building its omnichannel capabilities, strengthening brand partnerships and expanding its retail footprint. He said: “Serving as Schuh president has been the privilege of my career. I am incredibly proud of what we have achieved, and I want to sincerely thank the people at Schuh for their dedication, hard work and friendship.” “While I look forward to the next chapter, I leave knowing the business is in great hands and has a bright future ahead.” Andy Gray, CEO of Journeys Global Retail Group, thanked Temple for his contributions to the business and said Petersson's international retail experience and proven ability to grow retail businesses made him “the right leader” to guide Schuh through its next phase of growth.

Frasers raises Hugo Boss stake above 30%, takeover offer remains open
sub_title: Frasers Group raises its Hugo Boss stake to 30.28%, crossing the mandatory bid threshold as its €38-per-share takeover offer remains open.
article_content: Frasers Group has increased its stake in Hugo Boss to 30.28%, crossing Germany’s mandatory bid threshold, although its €38-per-share offer remains unchanged. Frasers Group has today announced that following up from its initial takeover offer of the German luxury brand Hugo Boss , it has now acquired an additional 2,5+ million Hugo Boss shares. This translate to around 3.69% of the share capital and voting rights of the business. At that time of the initial takeover offer in June, Frasers Group owned just over 18 million shares, equal to 26.06% of the Hugo Boss' share capital. The latest transaction means that the British retail group, which owns Sports Direct and Flannels, now owns in aggregate close to 21 million shares in Hugo Boss, which amounts to a 30.28% stake of the share capital and voting rights of the German brand, excluding additional shares that have been tendered into the offer. The latest offer remains open at €38 for each Hugo Boss share not held by Frasers, which the Group has previously said marks its final price. T he initial acceptance period for the offer is due to end at midnight Frankfurt time (GMT+2) on 27 July. Now that Frasers owns over 30% of the German company it has crossed the mandatory bid threshold under Germany’s Takeover Code, which, similar to the UK takeover code means it is now required to make an offer for all remaining Hugo Boss shares. It also reaffirms its position as the company's controlling shareholder. Full ownership would give Frasers direct control over a premium apparel brand with revenues of €4.26 billion and a global store network, at a time when the British group has been expanding its European footprint. Yet, this does not mean though that its offer will be accepted. Hugo Boss' board has previously recommended that shareholders reject Frasers takeover offer , which they called "inadequate". In 2024, Frasers faced a similar situation, when it launched a takeover bid for British luxury brand Mulberry, in which it held around 37%. Yet Mulberry's biggest shareholder, Challice, which owned a 56% stake, opposed Frasers bid, so while it remains a major stakeholder it does not control the business. Frasers Group spent the last six years building up its stake in Hugo Boss , culminating in a voluntary public takeover offer on 10 June, which valued the shares outside Frasers’ ownership at around €1.98 billion (£1.73 billion). The bid landed as Hugo Boss had been working through a strategic reset after falling sales, while Frasers has been expanding its influence across European. Frasers presented the move as “long-term value creation”. On July 9 Hugo Boss’s management and supervisory boards unanimously advised shareholders not to accept Frasers Group's initial, unsolicited, takeover bid, describing it as "inadequate". Daniel Grieder, Chief Executive Officer of Hugo Boss, commented at the time: “Hugo Boss has a well-defined strategy, a strong financial profile, and a compelling path to superior long-term value creation. “We focus on further strengthening our brands, structurally improving profitability, and accelerating cash generation over the coming years. “Against this backdrop, we firmly believe that the offer price fails to capture the company’s intrinsic value and long-term potential.” Frasers followed up its initial bid for Hugo Boss with another takeover offer for Australia’s Accent Group for £166 million . Frasers Group is already a majority shareholder (almost 23%) of Accent Group, which sells brands including Hype in Australia as well as operating multi-brand retailer Platypus Shoes. It is also reported to handle Frasers Group’s Sports Direct in the region. Accent Group rejected Frasers Group's "unsolicited, highly opportunistic" takeover bid on 29 June . These are not the only examples of Frasers Group's appetite to takeover companies. In the past 18 months alone, Frasers has acquired a majority stake in Italian multi-sport retailer Maxi Sport , taken control of Norwegian sporting goods chain XXL and added multiple UK designer outlets and shopping centres to its property portfolio. Yet, Hugo Boss would be the most prominent brand asset in Frasers' empire, which also includes Jack Wills, Gieves & Hawkes and USC. As was reported when the bid was announced, it would represent a major step in Frasers' "Elevation Strategy" of moving beyond its Sports Direct roots toward premium retail. The Hugo Boss update also came one day after Frasers launched a share buyback programme with newly appointed joint broker Panmure Liberum. The arrangement permits the broker to acquire up to 10 million Frasers ordinary shares, with the total purchase price capped at £80 million. Purchases can continue until the trading day immediately before the group’s next annual general meeting, currently expected in mid-September. Shares acquired through the programme will be held in treasury. Frasers said the sole purpose of the purchases is to reduce its share capital. The Hugo Boss offer is still subject to the published terms and the relevant regulatory clearances, and completion had previously been targeted for the second half of 2026.

Manolo Blahnik strengthens leadership as it targets further growth in the Americas
sub_title: Manolo Blahnik has appointed Kimberly Mimnaugh as Managing Director of the Americas, strengthening its leadership team as the luxury footwear brand continues to expand its presence across North America.
article_content: Manolo Blahnik has appointed Kimberly Mimnaugh as Managing Director of the Americas, strengthening its leadership team as the luxury footwear brand continues to expand its presence across North America. Effective immediately, Mimnaugh will lead the commercial strategy for Manolo Blahnik Americas across retail, wholesale and ecommerce, while overseeing the company's regional operations. Based in New York, she will report to Chief Commercial Officer Elodie Bougenault. Mimnaugh joins from Chloé, where she most recently served as Vice President of North America Retail, overseeing merchandising and buying, retail operations, learning and development, store planning and visual merchandising. During her tenure, she led the brand's transition from wholesale to retail concessions for handbags at a leading US department store and developed a regional client engagement programme that was later adopted globally. Prior to Chloé, Mimnaugh was Senior Vice President of North America Retail at Theory and Helmut Lang, where she oversaw retail operations, store design, visual merchandising and financial retail planning. She also previously served as Managing Director of North America at Brunello Cucinelli, driving market expansion, controlled distribution and the transformation of the brand's retail footprint. North America remains a key growth market for Manolo Blahnik, which currently operates four stores across the region, most recently opening a boutique at South Coast Plaza in California. Kristina Blahnik, CEO of Manolo Blahnik, said: “I am delighted to welcome Kimberly to Manolo Blahnik as Managing Director of the Americas. Kimberly brings an exceptional combination of luxury retail expertise and commercial leadership.” “Her proven ability to accelerate direct-to-consumer growth while maintaining a strong wholesale business makes her ideally placed to lead this next phase of our growth in the Americas.” Mimnaugh added: “I am thrilled to be joining Manolo Blahnik at such a pivotal moment for the brand in the Americas. Manolo Blahnik holds a rare and enduring position within luxury, built on unparalleled craftsmanship, and I am excited to help shape its next chapter of growth across the region.” Founded in 1970, Manolo Blahnik continues to expand its international retail footprint. Earlier this year, the luxury footwear brand opened its first boutique in Beijing , marking its second store in Mainland China, as it continues to invest in key international growth markets.

article_title: London Fashion Week September 2026 schedule announced
sub_title: The British Fashion Council (BFC) has announced the provisional schedule for London Fashion Week September 2026, with the event set to feature the return of major British fashion houses alongside new talent and increased retail participation.
article_content: The British Fashion Council (BFC) has announced the provisional schedule for London Fashion Week September 2026, with the event set to feature the return of major British fashion houses alongside new talent and increased retail participation. Taking place from 17 to 21 September 2026, the schedule will see McQueen return with Seán McGirr presenting his London debut for the house, showcasing both menswear and womenswear Spring/Summer 2027 collections. Mulberry will also return to the official schedule under new Creative Director Christopher Kane, who will present his debut collection for the brand. The season will also feature established British names including Burberry, Barbour, Emilia Wickstead, Erdem, Harris Reed, Richard Quinn, Roksanda and Simone Rocha, alongside emerging designers supported through initiatives including BFC NEWGEN. Francesca Lake, Gui Rosa and Petra Fagerström will make their London Fashion Week debuts as BFC NEWGEN recipients , while Fashion East will return to the schedule following further investment from the BFC into the talent support scheme. Laura Weir, Chief Executive of the British Fashion Council, said: “This season marks an exciting moment for London Fashion Week, with the return of leading British brands alongside an exceptional new generation of creative talent.” “This schedule reflects the confidence and momentum of British fashion today, bringing together established houses, emerging designers and industry partners on a platform that continues to shape global fashion.” The September edition will also highlight the increasing role of retail and consumer engagement within London Fashion Week. Marks & Spencer will make its debut on the official schedule with its first exclusive runway collection , featuring a “see now, buy now” womenswear and menswear collection to mark its centenary year. Elsewhere, eBay will return with its Endless Runway pre-loved fashion show , available to shop through eBay Live, while Selfridges will spotlight participating LFW brands through dedicated in-store highlights and a curated edit of British designers. H&M will also collaborate with photographer Nick Knight and SHOWstudio on a new interpretation of the fashion show format. The BFC said the September schedule will continue to position London Fashion Week as a platform for creative innovation, cultural impact and commercial growth, bringing together fashion houses, emerging designers, retailers and industry partners.

article_title: M&S appoints new Fashion and Beauty Director of Sourcing, Quality and Sustainability
sub_title: Marks & Spencer has appointed Jane Robson as its new Fashion, Home & Beauty Director of Sourcing, Quality and Sustainability, effective in August.
article_content: Marks and Spencer has appointed Jane Robson as its new Fashion, Home & Beauty Director of Sourcing, Quality and Sustainability, effective in August. Robson has most recently been in the role of Chief Operating Officer at Vogue Sourcing UK, a position she has held since May 2024. Previously she has held the position of Non-Executive Director at Threadbare, and was appointed as Non-Executive Director at Fanfare Label. She also served as Strategic Advisor for My Wardrobe HQ for almost seven years, as well as a Designer Mentor at the British Fashion Council for five years. Earlier roles include that of Managing Director of NEXT Sourcing Limited, from September 2004 to June 2010, based in Hong Kong. Having spent her career reshaping complex international sourcing offices, in her new role Robson will be based at M&S’s Waterside Stores Support Centre. She will start her role with a thorough induction, spending time in M&S stores, sourcing offices and supply base. She will be taking over from Monique Leeuwenburgh, who will be retiring from M&S in October after seven years with the business. On Leeuwenburgh’s pending departure, John Lyttle, Managing Director of M&S, commented: “Monique has been instrumental in shaping our global sourcing strategy, strengthening key supplier partnerships, and leading transformation across our international operations. “Monique is respected across the business for leading with integrity, professionalism, and collaboration, and we thank her for her commitment.” Last week M&S reported it had completed the renewal of its Pantheon flagship store at 173 Oxford Street , bringing food, fashion, home and beauty together across four floors. The store will operate as its first full-line research and development (R&D) site for fashion, home and beauty. The British high street retailer unveiled the Pantheon store’s remaining two upper floors on Monday, 13 July, adding its latest menswear, kidswear, lingerie and home collections to the renewed location. The transformation covers almost 100,000 sq ft and has been completed in stages while the store continued trading. M&S has occupied the building, identified by its green PANTHEON lettering, since 1938. Also last week, M&S revealed it is set to start work on its Marble Arch flagship redevelopment next year.

article_title: Zara’s sister brand Lefties confirms late August opening for first UK store
sub_title: Inditex’s budget fashion and lifestyle brand Lefties, a sister brand of Zara and a competitor of Primark, has confirmed it will be opening its first UK store at the Liverpool ONE shopping centre at the end of August 2026.
article_content: Inditex’s budget fashion and lifestyle brand Lefties, a sister brand of Zara and a competitor of Primark, has confirmed it will be opening its first UK store at the Liverpool ONE shopping centre at the end of August 2026. That will be followed by a second UK store at the Lakeside shopping centre in West Thurrock, Essex, in early October, and a third at Gateshead’s Metrocentre in November. Lefties was founded in 1999 and launched its own-brand collections over a decade ago. It has its own headquarters just outside Barcelona, including commercial and design teams, who “aim to bring accessible quality fashion to its customers”. The new Lefties store at the Metrocentre will occupy a central unit at the interchange between Red and Green Mall on Town Square, directly above H Beauty. It will serve as “a key anchor” within Metrocentre’s dedicated fashion offer. Each new Lefties store will utilise technology already used at the retailer’s latest European branches, which includes robots to sort hangers and radio frequency identification self-checkouts in its minimalist stores. Lefties currently operates a total of 215 stores across 19 markets, with the UK set to become its 20th.

article_title: John Lewis partners with RIXO on its biggest fashion collaboration to date
sub_title: Discover the John Lewis x RIXO 44-piece fashion collection. Shop vintage-inspired prints and archival designs starting October 2026.
article_content: John Lewis will launch its largest fashion collaboration to date with British womenswear brand RIXO, bringing a 44-piece, vintage-inspired collection to stores and online from 22 October 2026. The range covers dresses, knitwear, blouses, jackets, skirts, scarves, shoes and bags, giving the collaboration a broader category mix than a conventional occasionwear capsule, with prices starting at £65. The collection is also informed by John Lewis' own archives, marking the first time an archive print has been used in a John Lewis fashion collaboration. The  floral motif was inspired by block-printed textile from 1849 and was discovered during the collaborative design process. The signature print will feature across two dresses, a blouse, skirt and scarf. This marks a big step for RIXO, which has built its womenswear identity around vintage references, distinctive prints and dresses, as it is the first time the brand has collaborated with a retailer on this scale. To date RIXO operates seven standalone stores and has a wholesale network including Liberty London. For John Lewis, the collaboration reinforces its commitment to support British talent, while bolstering its premium brand portfolio. "RIXO is an iconic British brand adored by so many, much like John Lewis, so it felt natural to create something special together," commented Rachel Morgans, Fashion Director at John Lewis on collaboration. RIXO Co-Founder Orlagh McCloskey said: "This collaboration feels like a true extension of RIXO – taking the heritage of John Lewis, leaning into its incredible archive, and bringing it to life with that RIXO magic. "For me, if you’re going to do a collaboration, you have to do it properly. It should feel as strong, if not stronger, than anything you’ve created before – every piece considered, every detail cared for, and something you feel genuinely proud to put your name to. "We wanted the collection to do the talking. We can’t wait to see women across the UK, whether they’re longtime RIXO lovers or discovering us for the first time through John Lewis, style it in their own way and make it theirs. We feel incredibly proud to have created something that reaches a wider audience than our London stores." The collaboration follows RIXO’s spring/summer 2026 collection, We Are One , which marked the brand’s tenth year with bold colour and vintage-influenced prints. That collection also included plans for a capsule reworking designs from the Liberty archive. RIXO also expanded its physical presence at the end of 2025 by opening its seventh store at Bicester Village. The location took its design cues from eclectic English country estates, continuing the historic references seen across the brand’s clothing and retail environments. The full collection will launch simultaneously in stores and online on 22 October.
