ASOS confirms permanent hire to lead loyalty and returns strategy
sub_title: ASOS has confirmed the permanent appointment of Manoja Josyula as Director of Product Propositions, who has been serving in the role on an interim basis since joining the business in March.
article_content: ASOS has confirmed the permanent appointment of Manoja Josyula as Director of Product Propositions, who has been serving in the role on an interim basis since joining the business in March. In the role, Josyula leads the retailer's core customer propositions, overseeing its Premier offering -  ASOS' paid delivery membership, loyalty and returns. She will report into Ben Blake, EVP Customer & Commercial. Manoja Josyula, ASOS Josyula brings over a decade of experience leading customer-focused growth strategies across digital and consumer businesses to the role. Prior to joining ASOS, she was General Manager for Foreign Travel at Trainline, leading strategy and commercial performance across international markets. Before that, she held senior leadership positions at personalised photo product companies Storio Group and Photobox, overseeing trading, category management, partnerships and market growth. ASOS said the appointment reflects its "continued focus on strengthening the propositions that matter most to customers, while driving sustainable, profitable growth". Blake added that since joining ASOS, Manoja has "already made a significant impact across some of our most important customer propositions". "She brings a brilliant combination of strategic thinking, commercial expertise and customer obsession, and has quickly become a trusted leader across the business," he said. "Premier, loyalty and returns play a critical role in how customers experience ASOS. Manoja has a clear vision for how we continue to evolve these propositions, and I'm delighted she has chosen to continue that journey with us on a permanent basis." Josyula added: "There is a huge opportunity to strengthen how we engage and retain customers through Premier, loyalty and returns, and I'm looking forward to helping shape the next chapter of that journey." Returns have been a large cost pressure for the retailer, and it has tightened controls in recent years, including the introduction of return fees for customers with high return rates in October 2024. In January this year, it then introduced what it described as a "first-of-its-kind" returns transparency tool within its UK app , giving shoppers visibility over their individual return rate and clearer guidance on when fees apply. Just one month later, the retailer unveiled a new hybrid virtual try-on experience , allowing shoppers to either upload their own image or select an AI-generated model that reflects their likeness. It comes as ASOS, which has 17 million active customers across more than 100 markets, has been working through a broader turnaround under its CEO José Antonio Ramos Calamonte. This has seen it significantly reduce its operating losses for the six months ending 1 March 2026 , narrowing them by 52% to £100.9 million, despite a decline in overall revenue. The online retailer said that operational efficiency improvements played a central role in the cost reduction. Supply chain costs declined due to warehouse optimisation and renegotiated logistics contracts, continuing a multi-year trend of efficiency gains.

Schiaparelli brings silicone to couture in futuristic Paris collection
sub_title: Schiaparelli displayed a futuristic vision at the opening of Haute Couture Week in Paris, with creative director Daniel Roseberry introducing sculptural silicone into couture.
article_content: Schiaparelli displayed a futuristic vision at the opening of Haute Couture Week in Paris, with Creative Director Daniel Roseberry introducing sculptural silicone into couture. Celebrities sitting front row included singer Bad Bunny, and actors Emma Corrin and Michelle Yeoh. From the fashion world, Anna Wintour, Zendaya’s stylist Law Roach and designer Vera Wang also turned out to show their support. Titled The Abyss, the autumn/winter 2026/27 collection marked one of the house’s most experimental shows to date, combining traditional couture craftsmanship with synthetic materials in a presentation that explored the tension between reality and artifice. A post shared by Kristen Bateman (@kristenvbateman) Roseberry often takes his cues from the animal kingdom, such as a black gown featuring a giant lion’s head made of faux fur, first seen in the spring 2023 couture collection. The brand’s original designer, Elsa Schiaparelli, was equally known for her own surreal take on animalia – most famously Wallis Simpson’s scandalously sheer lobster dress. But for this collection, Roseberry took inspiration from more otherworldly creatures, with the show name perhaps taking inspiration from James Cameron’s 1989 sci-fi film. A post shared by Schiaparelli (@schiaparelli) Florals were depicted against silicone corsets, curling tentacles were imagined through latex, and coral-inspired collars were attached to illuminated LED, plastic jackets. At the centre of the collection was Roseberry’s continued experimentation with materials, most notably his development of what he described as ‘silicone silk’ – a lightweight, sheer variation of silicone designed to mimic the fluidity of fabric while retaining sculptural structure. The material was used to challenge the building blocks of couture, pairing traditional techniques with synthetic innovation. Amelia Gray, model and daughter of former Real Housewives Of Beverly Hills star Lisa Rinna, were among those presenting the looks, walking in the show wearing a silicone pink and pearl corseted midi dress that combined delicacy with an artificial edge. Roseberry said the collection was driven by uncertainty and creative surrender, describing The Abyss as an exploration of the “call of the void” – the moment when control gives way to instinct. It’s difficult not to see this collection as a reaction to the AI boom, as tech has been trickling its way into fashion recently – most notably through Kylie Jenner’s collaboration with Meta to create fashion-forward ‘Meta Glasses’. A post shared by Schiaparelli (@schiaparelli) Founded in 1927 by Elsa Schiaparelli, the house has long been associated with surrealism and avant-garde design. Since taking the helm in 2019, Roseberry has built on that legacy, attracting high-profile clients including Nicole Kidman, Demi Moore and Kylie Jenner, who are drawn to the label’s blend of elegance and eccentricity. Earlier this year, the label dressed Dua Lipa in a Bianca Jagger-inspired ivory suit and sculpted bustier for her London wedding to Callum Turner, underscoring Schiaparelli’s continued role in prominent fashion moments. Bad Bunny (Emma Da Silva/AP) The show’s front row was suitably star-studded, with Puerto Rican singer and rapper Bad Bunny sporting the colour of the season in a butter yellow double-breasted suit with idiosyncratic Schiaparelli gold buttons, a plaited gold tie and a Western-style belt with boots to match. The 32-year-old is continuing his relationship with the brand – at the Grammys earlier this year, he wore the first-ever custom haute couture menswear look designed by Daniel Roseberry. Emma Corrin (Emma Da Silva/AP) Emma Corrin, 30, wore a futuristic feathered blazer from Schiaparelli’s spring/summer 2026 haute couture collection, featuring pointed talon-like details and a wing collar, featuring feathers in colours graduating from pistachio to lilac to coral. Michelle Yeoh (Emma Da Silva/AP) Oscar-winning actress Michelle Yeoh, 63, opted for a more pared-back Roseberry design, in an off-the-shoulder black design with a monochromatic feather trim. The Wicked star paired the dress with a classic Schiaparelli ‘Face Bag’ in black calf skin leather and hammered gold brass.

article_title: Editors' Top Reads: News from Chanel, M&S, Levi's and more...
sub_title: Here are some of this week’s news and features highlights handpicked by TheIndustry.fashion team.
article_content: Here are some of this week’s news and features highlights handpicked by TheIndustry.fashion team. Marks & Spencer this week staged the first-ever fashion show on the Silverstone pit lane ahead of the Formula 1 British Grand Prix, transforming the circuit’s working garages into a runway. Around 50 models presented the brand’s “Dress to Thrill” summer collection, walking through an environment normally reserved for race-day engineering and high-performance machinery. The show forms part of Marks & Spencer’s broader multi-year partnership with Silverstone Circuit, reflecting a deliberate push by retailers to align with major cultural and sporting platforms. It also sits within a wider pattern: brands are increasingly using high-profile sporting moments - especially in Formula 1, football and tennis events like Wimbledon - to create immersive, shareable experiences. This isn’t an isolated move either, as other brands have been experimenting with activations like this too. Earlier this year, Topshop hosted an AI-powered shoppable catwalk in Manchester , which I attended - it was really cool. Taken together, these activations point to a clear shift: brands and retailers are increasingly moving towards entertainment-led experiences designed for social media reach, cultural relevance and audience engagement far beyond traditional marketing formats. Watch here . Chanel is acquiring France’s oldest shirtmaker, the Paris-based, family-run Charvet , following Matthieu Blazy’s collaboration with the brand for his first runway collection in October 2025. I love this story; it’s wonderful to see a luxury giant like Chanel investing in a heritage brand. It also makes sense. Charvet not only has an incredible history, but it has also been intertwined with Chanel since, when Coco Chanel was borrowing the Charvet shirts of her then-boyfriend, British shipping merchant and polo player Boy Capel. Since being founded in 1838 by none other than the son of Napoleon’s dressmaker, its patrons have included King Edward VII, John F. Kennedy, filmmaker Sofia Coppola, and former Creative Director of Chanel, Karl Lagerfeld. The two brands share many historical touchpoints, and while the Charvet acquisition is likely modest in financial terms relative to Chanel’s scale, it adds to the house’s vertical integration in specialist craft categories. By bringing shirtmaking expertise in-house, Chanel gains direct control over a production capability that proved its value on Blazy’s runway. And Blazy’s tenure has already generated visible commercial results. His autumn/winter 2026 show at the Grand Palais in March drew reports of editors and buyers queueing for hours at Chanel’s Paris boutiques to secure pieces from his early collections. For the current owners of Charvet, siblings Jean-Claude and Anne-Marie, the sale to Chanel ensures the legacy of the brand. Camilla Rydzek, Senior News & Features Writer. I really enjoyed writing about this launch because it addresses a challenge that affects millions of women and girls every month. The growth of period-proof clothing feels like a natural evolution within both fashion and sportswear, and it is perhaps surprising that dedicated performance swimwear has taken this long to reach the market. What stood out to me about WUKA’s new competition swimwear range is that it tackles a genuine barrier to participation in sport. The research behind the launch was compelling, if sadly unsurprising. Almost half of girls surveyed said periods affect their participation in swimming and sport, while 69% avoid swimming altogether during menstruation because of confidence and stigma. Importantly, this is not simply a period-proof swimsuit (which is already groundbreaking). Developed specifically for athletes, the collection combines leak protection with performance features such as compression fits and hydrodynamic construction. The focus is not only on managing periods, but also on supporting athletic performance in the water. It is interesting to see WUKA continue expanding beyond its core period underwear business into technical sportswear. As consumers increasingly seek products that solve real-world problems, this feels like a meaningful example of innovation that could actually help make sport more accessible for women and girls. Catherine Rowe-Kosary, Junior Writer. It would be very interesting to see how many Levi’s fans take up the brand’s new ‘Made to Order’ service at its ‘Soho Atelier’ at 40 Great Marlborough Street in London, with jeans priced at £650, or £950 for ‘bespoke’. Having had so many pairs of the premium-end selvedge Levi’s Vintage Clothing 501s over the years, including reissued models from the 1950s and 60s, I find that, though I’m now priced out of the game since they have reached the £300 mark (as at American Classics currently for Levi’s Vintage Clothing 1955 501 XX rigid denim jeans), this takes things up a notch further. The new offering provides a “personalised one-to-one tailoring experience”, allowing customers to choose from a curated selection of premium selvedge denims sourced from some of the world’s most respected mills, including Kaihara and Collect (Japan) and Cone Mills (United States), before working with a Levi’s artisan to create their preferred fit and silhouette. There’s even a choice of leather back patches, buttons, and 25 thread colour options. It sounds highly appealing, if not frighteningly expensive, and it’s not only restricted to jeans, also including bespoke chinos from £995 and bespoke jackets from £1,255. It would be a fun way to spend an afternoon after a lottery win! Tom Bottomley, Contributing Editor.

article_title: In Pictures: Selfridges unveils FIFA 1904 World Cup pop-up featuring first-ever licensed fashion collection
sub_title: Selfridges has well and truly got into the World Cup mood with the launch of a pop-up showcasing the first-ever official FIFA-licensed fashion collection, designed by Maison Kitsuné Creative Director Marcus Clayton.
article_content: Selfridges has well and truly got into the World Cup mood with the launch of a pop-up showcasing the first-ever official FIFA-licensed fashion collection, designed by Maison Kitsuné Creative Director Marcus Clayton. The FIFA 1904 collection - so named because that was the year the international football federation was established - has been created in collaboration with VFILES, the New York-based youth culture and fashion platform founded by Julie Anne Quay, who is also a minority owner of Barnsley Football Club. It is split into two distinct capsules: “Resort 2026”, described as “a considered edit merging timeless sportswear with contemporary streetwear” for both men and women, and “Rue Saint-Honoré”, which features elevated essentials that pay homage to FIFA’s founding address in Paris. The Rue Saint-Honoré collection also features refined tailoring pieces, premium materials, and clean lines, “priced to democratise the luxury football aesthetic”. In true Selfridges style, the dedicated space, which is set to run right up to and including World Cup final day on 19 July, offers far more than a traditional retail installation. Alongside the new clothing range, the pop-up also features exclusive content from the FIFA Museum, bringing the history and cultural significance of the global game into the heart of one of London’s most iconic retail destinations, as well as a designated seating area with a large screen to show World Cup matches. Julie Anne Quay said: “Football brings the world together. The moments we share through football empower us to see possibility and opportunity.” “FIFA 1904 is an emotional brand built on that shared intention and Selfridges is the perfect home to bring it to life in London this summer, in a way that feels genuinely new.” Prior to designer Marcus Clayton’s role at Maison Kitsuné, which he has held since December 2019, he was Design Director at LVMH’s Fenty (2018–2020), Creative Director at Golden Goose (2016–2018), Design Director for Womenswear at Givenchy (2015–2016), and Design Director for Womenswear at Alexander Wang (2011–2014).

Clarks plans up to 20 new European stores as expansion gathers pace
sub_title: Clarks has opened a new store in Italy as the heritage British footwear brand advances its European expansion plans, with between 15 and 20 new stores set to open across the continent this year.
article_content: Clarks has opened a new store in Italy as the heritage British footwear brand advances its European expansion plans, with between 15 and 20 new stores set to open across the continent this year. Its latest store is located at Santangelo Outlet Village, near the city of Pescara in Italy's Abruzzo region. Italy is one of Clarks' most important European markets, and the opening follows recent store launches across Italy and Spain, with further locations planned in France, Belgium and the UK. In Spain, Clarks has moved to direct management of the market, supported by a new Madrid-based team and showroom. The business has already opened stores in Barcelona and Bilbao and has an ambition to double the Spanish business within one to two years. The expansion follows Clarks' 200th anniversary year. Founded in Somerset in 1825, the business now operates across retail, wholesale, franchise and online channels in more than 100 markets. The growth push is underpinned by the company's return to profitability. In 2025, Clarks reported operating profit of £66.3 million and ended the year with no bank debt, creating what the business describes as "a platform for reinvestment and growth". Clarks is expanding across direct retail, wholesale, franchise partnerships and marketplaces. For autumn/winter 2026, the business has begun operating with 120 new multi-brand wholesale accounts in Europe and the UK, while wholesale orders in Italy for AW26 are up 55% compared with AW25. The brand has also launched on platforms including Secret Sales and eBay, and created its own UK marketplace featuring complementary brands . If successful, that model could be extended to Europe and the United States in 2027. Further European store openings are expected through the second half of 2026. The Santangelo opening sits alongside Clarks' first-ever pop-up at Kildare Village in Ireland , which went live in May with a blend of full-price and specially priced styles. Both outlet locations support the brand's stated push on competitive pricing and improved inventory management. On the full-price side, Clarks will this summer open a flagship store at 522 Oxford Street measuring 2,839 sq ft , with the updated retail identity first introduced at its Tottenham Court Road store last November. Joe Ulloa, President UK & Europe at Clarks, said: "Italy is one of our most important European markets, with a strong heritage for the brand and significant opportunity ahead. "Across Europe, we are investing in the right stores, strengthening wholesale, building new partnerships and improving the value we offer customers. Our focus is on sustainable market share growth, supported by a healthier, more disciplined business that gives us the confidence to reinvest for the future." Recent months have also seen the brand relaunch its 90s Cica football trainer ahead of the FIFA World Cup and introduce Clarks Originals apparel lines including T-shirts, caps and socks.

article_title: Chanel acquires France's oldest shirtmaker Charvet after Blazy runway collaboration
sub_title: Chanel has agreed to acquire Charvet, the Paris-based, family-run shirtmaker, turning a runway collaboration into an investment in specialist craft under artistic director Matthieu Blazy.
article_content: Chanel has agreed to acquire Charvet, the Paris-based, family-run shirtmaker, turning a runway collaboration into an investment in specialist craft under artistic director Matthieu Blazy. The acquisition follows Charvet's development of a trio of shirts for Blazy's debut Chanel show in October 2025. Yet the relationship between Charvet and Chanel goes back much further. Just under 100 years ago, Coco Chanel was borrowing the Charvet shirts of her then-boyfriend, British shipping merchant and polo player Boy Capel. Former Creative Director of Chanel, Karl Lagerfeld, was also a fan of the brand, continuing the legacy. Following the latest collaboration with Blazy, the Colbans, who had been seeking a succession plan for their family business, felt they had found a long-term partner in Chanel. Bruno Pavlovsky, Chanel's fashion president, said: "Charvet is a beautiful jewel. Now there's work to be done to set it up for its next steps." Charvet, based at Place Vendôme in Paris, has operated as an independent, family-run business across generations. It was founded as the world's first dedicated shirt shop in 1838, by the son of Napoleon's dresser, Joseph-Christophe Charvet. Its reputation as a specialist craft maker has been built since then, with patrons including King Edward VII, who even awarded the shirtmaker a royal warrant, a rare honour for a non-British brand. Loyal customers have also included John F. Kennedy, David Hockney and film maker Sofia Coppola. The business remained within the family until 1965, when it was sold to the owner of Charvet's fabric supplier, Denis Colban. The brand is now run by Colban's children, Jean-Claude and his sister Anne-Marie. Today, with the children of both siblings working in other fields, the question of succession created an opening for a buyer with both the resources and the creative alignment to preserve the business. Charvet has estimated revenues of €10-15 million (£8.6-12.9 million) a year, Luca Solca, a luxury analyst at Bernstein, told the New York Times. Its assets include 100 employees, an atelier outside Paris and one store, the building on Place Vendôme, which Chanel has also acquired. According to Chanel, Charvet will remain an independent company, with the Colban's staying on for at least one more year to ensure a smooth transition of ownership. The Charvet deal is part of a wider round of supplier takeovers at Chanel. For the year ended 31 December 2025, the house posted revenue of $19.3 billion , 2% higher than the previous year, while operating profit came in at $4.7 billion. During 2025, Chanel said it put more than $700 million into buying long-standing suppliers to secure "the finest materials and craftsmanship". Chanel's CFO Philippe Blondiaux said in May that the house "continued to invest in the future of our brand and our people" through its broader creative ecosystem, alongside record-level capital expenditure on real estate and boutique openings. The Charvet acquisition is likely modest in financial terms relative to Chanel's scale, but it adds to the house's vertical integration in specialist craft categories. By bringing shirtmaking expertise in-house, Chanel gains direct control over a production capability that proved its value on Blazy's runway. Blazy's tenure has generated visible commercial results. His autumn/winter 2026 show at the Grand Palais in March drew reports of editors and buyers queueing for hours at Chanel's Paris boutiques to secure pieces from his early collections. Positive performance in ready-to-wear and the reception of the Chanel 25 handbag campaign contributed to the house's 2025 growth.

article_title: Debenhams Group sees demand in ‘football fashion’ surge as World Cup fever strikes
sub_title: Debenhams Group’s Boohoo has seen football-related product sales increase by 1,827% from May to June, while searches are up 600% as World Cup fever takes hold.
article_content: Debenhams Group’s Boohoo has seen football-related product sales increase by 1,827% from May to June, while searches are up 600% as World Cup fever takes hold. As the nation gets behind England, who progressed to the last 16 of the tournament by beating DR Congo on Wednesday night, fans have been busy updating their matchday wardrobes. Debenhams itself has reported a 481% increase in official football shirt sales over the same period. Views of Boohoo’s men’s football shirts increased by 9,000%, while views of its women’s football collection also jumped 1,800%. A Debenhams Group spokesperson said: “Major sporting moments like the World Cup always create a real buzz, and that excitement naturally spills over into shopping habits. “As England heads into the knockout stages, fans are turning to fashion to show their support – from official team shirts to football-inspired fashion. “As the stakes get higher, we expect demand to continue to build. Every game gives supporters another reason to back the Three Lions, and we’re seeing that reflected in the products customers are choosing to wear.” Customers are also putting their own spin on matchday dressing, with football-led fashion emerging as one of the tournament’s biggest style trends. The England Football T-shirt has become the best-selling football-inspired product since the start of the tournament, while the England Football Strappy Vest became the Boohoo brand’s top-performing item following England’s opening 4–2 victory over Croatia. Debenhams has also seen a 260% increase in sales of retro football shirts, particularly vintage England shirt styles, with sales volumes rising 233%.

article_title: Former ASOS ESG boss to lead brand sales and marketing at NEXT
sub_title: Jodie Leek, the former Head of ESG at ASOS has been appointed to lead Brand Sales and Marketing at retailer NEXT.
article_content: Jodie Leek, the former Head of ESG at ASOS, has been appointed to lead brand sales and marketing at retailer NEXT. Leek brings over 25 years of experience in global sourcing, supply chain management, and environmental, social and governance (ESG), to her new role. In her last role at ASOS, she also oversaw brand engagement and was responsible for developing and delivering a programme spanning human rights due diligence, environmental performance, chemical compliance and animal welfare. Prior to her time at ASOS, where she spent seven years, she spent just over seven months at UK Denim Clothes Manufacturer Moseley Road. She was also previously Buying Manager for Menswear, Womenswear & Kids at Tesco. Next had previously announced it had increased the estimated cost from the impact of the Middle East conflict to £47 million from the £15 million guidance given in March, as it now expects disruption for the remainder of its financial year to next January. It said it would look to hike prices in international countries from the month of May, but said efforts to make cost savings would mean it does not need to push through extra price increases in the UK and Europe.

article_title: In Review, June 2026: Headline highlights from Alo Yoga, Hermès, Cubitts and more...
sub_title: Over the month of June we have seen early signs of a retail recovery, with brands upgrading and expanding their retail portfolio, while others are
article_content: Over the month of June we have seen early signs of a retail recovery, with brands upgrading and expanding their retail portfolio, while others are plotting entries into new markets. As brands are continuing to invest into enhancing their physical retail spaces, the warm weather has seen both an uplift in demand for seasonal products, as well as a "welcome boost" to retail sales. Yet consumer confidence, especially for young people, remains subdued amid fears for their personal finances and the wider economy. We also look back on some incredible interviews and features this month that look behind the curtains of the industry. From an interview with the CEO of Derek Rose, which just celebrated its 100 year anniversary, to show reports from Pitti, to Scoop and Source Fashion. We also looked at how brands and retailers are capitalising on football's biggest tournament, and how Frasers Group built up its stake in Hugo Boss over the last six years, ahead of its take-over offer earlier this month. Spanish womenswear brand Byan is gearing up to open its first London flagship store on Chelsea’s King’s Road in October. Footasylum has reopened its upgraded 17,178 sq ft store at the Trafford Centre in Manchester. The brand announced today that it was further expanding its UK footprint with the opening of a tenth "sanctuary" in Edinburgh in November this year. This marks the first time that Alo is coming to Scotland, offering its range of "studio-to-street design" to the local community. Performance footwear brand HOKA has opened its first-ever UK outlet pop-up store at Gunwharf Quays in Portsmouth. FatFace is continuing its expansion into the Republic of Ireland with the opening of a new store in Galway, taking its total store count in the region to seven. Photo: Valérie Sadoun for Hermès French luxury fashion house Hermès has opened a new flagship at 166 New Bond Street in London , its largest store in Europe. Bondi Active is entering the UK through a phased launch of its Forma collection, starting with a localised e-commerce offer and a King’s Road pop-up. Read the full piece here for the brand’s rollout plans into UK retail stores in August. Superdry has opened its first Superdry & Co outlet at Caledonia Park in Scotland, using the 4,500 sq ft unit to present its updated concept and product mix. The new outlet opening gives an early read on how the repositioned brand is being shown to shoppers. Cubitts has opened The Yard in King’s Cross , bringing frame making, lens production, repair, consultation and training into one central London site. The 13,000 sq ft manufactory also gives the eyewear brand a visible production base. Salomon will open a 3,500 sq ft store at Liverpool ONE this summer, marking its first full-price UK store outside London. Italian sportswear brand Macron is gearing to open a 2,200 sq ft store adjacent to Jack Wills and AllSaints at Gloucester Quays outlet shopping centre, ahead of the destination’s ‘Summer of Sport’ activation. Heritage outdoor lifestyle brand Dubarry of Ireland is gearing to open a 1,362 sq ft flagship store at 6 Conduit Street in London’s Mayfair this summer, following the signing of a six-year lease with London landlord The Crown Estate. Footasylum has opened a 4,000 sq ft store at Cyfarthfa Shopping Park in Merthyr Tydfil, Wales , creating 25 new jobs in the prominent high footfall retail destination. Manchester-based womenswear brand 4th & Reckless has launched its first-ever shop-in-shop concept in the Selfridges store at the Trafford Centre in its home city, in collaboration with Jolie interiors. Luxury fashion resale platform and retailer Designer Exchange is opening its latest store at 141 Grainger Street in Newcastle on 11 June. Vintage clothing retailer Rokit has opened its first dedicated footwear and accessories store at 107 Brick Lane in East London. Menswear brand Bound will be opening its debut flagship store at 34-36 Thomas Street in the heart of Manchester’s Northern Quarter on Saturday 13 June. British outdoor clothing and equipment brand Berghaus, which celebrates its 60th anniversary this year , will be opening a new 2,750 sq ft store at Manchester Arndale “later this year”, marking the brand’s first standalone store in the North West. ZARA has re-opened its flagship store at 333 Oxford Street , just opposite Bond Street station, featuring a renovated interior and exterior as well as new omnichannel and automation features. F rasers Group has opened a 30,000 sq ft store at Citycenter Mall in Helsinki, Finland , marking its first opening in the Nordic region following the acquisition of Norwegian retailer XXL in the summer of 2025. JD Sports-owned sneaker and streetwear retailer Size? is opening its second store in Spain in the heart of Barcelona on Friday, 5 June, adding to its existing flagship store in Madrid, which opened in 2016. British fashion label Victoria Beckham has opened its first US store at Bal Harbour Shops in Miami, making it the first location outside London to house both its fashion and beauty businesses under one roof. Value fashion retailer Primark opened its fifth store in Romania in June, as it continues to expand in the market with three further locations planned by the end of this year. June's retail data painted a mixed picture for the UK high street, with warm weather providing a welcome boost to sales of seasonal categories such as fashion, footwear and outdoor goods, while inflation remained stable thanks to widespread clothing discounts. However, consumer confidence weakened sharply among younger adults and footfall continued to decline year-on-year, even as social media emerged as a major driver of high street visits, highlighting the increasingly complex forces shaping retail performance. Shop price inflation remained unchanged in June despite warnings of looming price hikes as a result of the Middle East crisis. Social media is driving an estimated 1.7 billion visits to UK high streets annually - an average of more than 30 million visits a week - analysis suggests. Warm May weather provided a "welcome boost" to retail sales , with total volume of sales, which measures the quantity bought, rising by 1.2% last month, according to new figures by the Office for National Statistics (ONS). GfK’s long-running Consumer Confidence Index showed that among traditionally optimistic younger adults confidence has plummeted by 11 points, amid fears for their personal finances and the wider economy. May’s heatwave drove a surge in spending on products ranging from barbecue food to sandals and sunglasses in a boost to retailers, figures show. Covering the four weeks from 3-30 May, total UK footfall decreased by 2.6% year-on-year , up from -10.7% in April, according to the latest data from BRC-Sensormatic, with record temperatures in the last week of May cited as impacting activity.

article_title: Pandora launches new creative platform with celebrity stylist Harry Lambert
sub_title: Pandora has launched a new creative platform under the title of 'Pandora Wonders', “designed to bring fresh cultural relevance to the brand”.
article_content: Jewellery brand Pandora has launched a new creative platform under the title of 'Pandora Wonders', “designed to bring fresh cultural relevance to the brand” and create new reasons for customers to engage. Described as ‘Act I’, a new limited-edition freshwater pearl collection has been co-created for the platform with British celebrity stylist Harry Lambert, perhaps best known for his work with Harry Styles, which explores the beauty of freshwater pearls from a modern perspective. The collection features limited-edition dangle charms crafted from one-of-a-kind freshwater baroque pearls. To preserve the individuality of every pearl, Pandora’s highly skilled craftspeople use a precise micro-piercing technique before hand-setting each piece and finishing it with 14K gold plating. The plan is, each year Pandora will collaborate with a creative talent to reinterpret a signature material through the lens of contemporary culture, creating distinctive collections and “experiences that inspire”. Philippa Newman, Chief Product Officer at Pandora, said: “Great design starts with great materials. With Pandora Wonders, we’re exploring the beauty and character of iconic jewellery materials through the eyes of leading creative voices. “It’s about reimagining timeless materials in a way that feels fresh, expressive and unmistakably Pandora.” Harry Lambert added: “I'm such a fan of pearls, so I'm so thrilled to bring a renewed sense of childlike delight and nostalgia to Pandora's unique world of charms, signatures which already have such a place in so many people's hearts.” Pandora Wonders will debut during Paris Haute Couture Week on 7 July 2026. The collection will be available in limited quantities from 8 July at selected Pandora stores and on Pandora.net, with exclusive early access at Dover Street Market London from 7 July and a dedicated Café Nuances pop-up in Le Marais, Paris, from 8-11 July.

Bondi Active to debut in UK with localised website and London pop-up
sub_title: Australian activewear brand Bondi Active is making its UK debut with the 'Forma collection', as it looks to open an online store and  London pop-up, with planned entry into UK retail stores in August.
article_content: Australian activewear brand Bondi Active is making its UK debut with the launch of its 'Forma collection', supported by an upgraded online presence, a London pop-up, and a planned expansion into UK retail stores in August. Re-launched in 2021, the brand said it is now Australia's fastest-growing wearable wellness label, with the UK roll-out marking the beginning of the brand's international expansion plans. Bondi Active will introduce itself to UK customers with its Forma collection, spanning both mens and womenswear, on 8 July. The range will be available on the brand's website, which has been updated to offer UK and European customers faster delivery and a localised shopping experience. A retail pop-up activation at on Kensington High Street in London will then run from 11-21 July, which the brand said will be the first opportunity for UK customers to experience its products in person. It is also looking to enter UK retail stores from August, although specific partners have not yet been announced. The Forma collection sits within the ballet-core trend, which Bondi Active describes as having a "contemporary Bondi twistl". The range includes track sets, oversized T-shirts and performance-driven activewear designed to move between studio and street. The pieces are made from a nylon-spandex fabric that the brand said is lightweight, moisture-wicking and durable. Colour palettes span soft pastel pink alongside electric blue and red. Bondi Active calls it the brand's "most refined collection to date". The pop-up will be located at Gymbody, 96 Kensington High Street, W8 4SG, London, running from 11-21 July.

Frasers Group offloads Sports Direct Malaysia in $150m deal
sub_title: Frasers Group has agreed to sell 100% of its interest in Sports Direct Malaysia to its strategic partner MAP Active for about $150 million (£113.4 million).
article_content: Frasers Group has agreed to sell 100% of its interest in Sports Direct Malaysia to its strategic partner MAP Active (PT MAP Aktif Adiperkasa Tbk) for approximately $150 million (£113.4 million). Under the terms announced on 1 July, Frasers will enter a long-term agreement through which MAP Active will grow and develop the Sports Direct brand in Malaysia, with a continuing income stream payable to the British retail group. The deal is still subject to final completion adjustments. The transaction brings Malaysia into a partnership structure already in place across Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam and Cambodia. For Frasers, the effect is a shift toward capital-light international expansion: the group realises cash from the sale, hands day-to-day execution to a local retail specialist, and retains financial participation in the market's future growth. Six markets, one operator MAP Active's existing infrastructure and portfolio of distributed brands across Southeast Asia will now underpin Sports Direct operations in six markets. The two companies have set a long-term ambition to open over 350 stores across the region, targeting a consumer base of more than 600 million people. Michael Murray, CEO of Frasers Group, said: "MAP Active is a valued strategic partner, and this transaction further deepens our relationship as we accelerate Sports Direct's growth across Southeast Asia. Together, we are creating a strong platform to deliver our ambitious growth plans." V.P. Sharma, Group CEO of MAP Active, added: "Leveraging our local expertise and regional retail network, we look forward to offering more of Sports Direct's world-class offerings to our customers across the region and unlocking new opportunities that create long-term value for both companies." The Malaysia disposal comes during a period of deal activity for the group. In late June, Frasers Group said its €38-per-share takeover offer for Hugo Boss is final, putting an approximate value of €1.93 billion on the shares it has yet to buy. That bid followed six years of stake-building in the German fashion house, over which Frasers accumulated 26.58% of Hugo Boss shares. Separately, Frasers launched a takeover bid for Australia's Accent Group at A$0.65 per share , which Accent's independent board committee unanimously rejected as "materially inadequate" on 29 June. The group also picked up a 5.77% position in Puma in March, lifted its financial exposure to ASOS to 29.26% , and has continued to expand its UK property portfolio through outlet and shopping centre acquisitions . By contrast, the Malaysia sale converts a directly operated international business into a partner-led model while freeing up capital. The transaction remains subject to final completion adjustments.
