Balenciaga appoints former Nike and Vans exec as CMO
sub_title: Luxury fashion house Balenciaga has appointed Drieke Leenknegt as Chief Marketing Officer, effective immediately.
article_content: Luxury fashion house Balenciaga has appointed Drieke Leenknegt as Chief Marketing Officer, effective immediately. Leenknegt will report to CEO Gianfranco Gianangeli and join the company's executive committee, according to WWD. The position has been vacant since September 2025, following the departure of Ludivine Pont, who left to become CEO of Officina Profumo-Farmaceutica di Santa Maria Novella. Leenknegt brings more than two decades of international marketing and leadership experience. During her 20-year tenure at Nike, she held a range of roles across Europe, the United States and China, including General Manager of Nike Women in Greater China and Global Vice President of Influencer Marketing & Collaborations at the company's Portland headquarters. She later served as Chief Marketing Officer at Timberland before taking on the same role at Vans from 2023 to 2025. Both brands are part of VF Corporation. Most recently, Leenknegt worked as an independent adviser, with clients including Chinese sportswear company Anta. Her appointment comes as Balenciaga expands promotional activity around its TechWear line, featured in Creative Director Pierpaolo Piccioli's pre-fall 2026 collection, "Body & Being". The initiative includes pop-up experiences in Paris, Beijing, Shanghai and Bangkok, as well as takeovers at Barry's fitness studios in cities including Los Angeles, New York, London, Milan, Dubai and Sydney through 4 July.

article_title: Uniqlo reimagines returned clothing in scalable upcycling initiative
sub_title: UNIQLO is launching a new upcycled collection called EVERYDAY RE.IMAGINED, created from returned items in collaboration with graduates from the BA Fashion course at Central Saint Martins.
article_content: Uniqlo is launching a scalable upcycled collection called Everyday Re.Imagined, created from returned items designed in collaboration with graduates from the BA Fashion course at Central Saint Martins. The 10-piece upcycled collection will be available from tomorrow, 25 June, exclusively in-store across 15 Re.Uniqlo Studios in the UK and Europe. Each piece in the collection is made from returned Uniqlo garments that may have been damaged or imperfect. The pieces are upcycled, repaired and creatively reconstructed by seamstresses working for Re.Uniqlo Studios, using template designs created by graduates of the Central Saint Martins (CSM) BA Fashion course. The very first Re.Uniqlo Studio opened in the Regent Street store in 2022, offering in-store repair, remake and personalisation services. Today, the studio is available in more than 70 stores across 23 markets. In the new collection, classic pieces such as AIRism T-shirts are reshaped, while trousers and cotton fabrics are reworked, with careful attention to ensuring that each piece retains the character of the original garment while breathing new life into the design. The upcycled collection builds on Uniqlo's longstanding partnership with CSM, which the retailer said provides valuable insights into new approaches to circular design. That means that while no two designs will be exactly alike, the garments all follow the same blueprint construction. Each piece is designed to be crafted in under an hour in order to keep it affordable while also ensuring that the collection is scalable, with prices ranging from £29.90 to £89.90. At an event on Tuesday, Uniqlo Europe Head of Sustainability Maria Samoto le Dous noted that the upcycled collection is not a trial project, but forms part of Uniqlo's long-term sustainability strategy. She added that the collection had been designed with scalability in mind and could potentially be expanded into additional markets in the future, with designs possibly evolving seasonally. "Collaborating with Central Saint Martins and its incredibly talented emerging designers has been both inspiring and energising," noted le Dous. "This project shows that innovation in fashion doesn't always begin with something new, but with a new way of seeing what already exists. "By combining their creative perspective with our LifeWear philosophy, we demonstrate how everyday clothing can be continuously reimagined, extending not only its lifecycle but also its meaning." Sarah Gresty, Course Leader, BA Fashion Design at Central Saint Martins, University of the Arts London, added: "The most exciting ideas in fashion often begin by looking at something familiar in a completely different way. "Through this collaboration, our graduates have transformed everyday garments into pieces that are inventive, thoughtful and full of possibility. It shows how creativity and experimentation can breathe new life into existing materials, challenging us to rethink the value and potential of the clothes we wear every day." In the UK, the upcycled collection will be available in London at Uniqlo's 311 Oxford Street, Regent Street, Covent Garden and Coal Drops Yard stores. In Edinburgh, it will be available at the Princes Street store.

article_title: Versace CEO Emmanuel Gintzburger exits
sub_title: Emmanuel Gintzburger is leaving his role as Chief Executive of Versace, having led the Italian luxury house since September 2022.
article_content: Emmanuel Gintzburger is leaving his role as Chief Executive of Versace , having led the Italian luxury house since September 2022. Gintzburger joined then-owner Capri Holdings after six years as CEO of Alexander McQueen. His tenure at Versace spanned a period of ownership upheaval and repeated creative leadership changes, culminating in Prada Group's €1.25 billion acquisition , which closed in December 2025. Before joining Versace, Gintzburger spent more than a decade in senior roles across major luxury groups. He served as Worldwide Retail & Wholesale Director at Saint Laurent from 2011 to 2016, held a retail director position at Lanvin, and earlier spent six years at Louis Vuitton in the Asia-Pacific region. When Capri announced his appointment in 2022, Donatella Versace called him the "perfect partner" to take the house "to even greater heights". Gintzburger's exit follows a period of creative turnover. Donatella Versace stepped down from her design role in March 2025 after nearly three decades, moving into the position of chief brand ambassador. "It has been the greatest honour of my life to carry on my brother Gianni's legacy," she said at the time. Dario Vitale, formerly in charge of design and image at Miu Miu, was named Chief Creative Officer effective April 2025. However, by December 2025, Vitale had also departed in what was described as a mutual decision. Pieter Mulier was subsequently appointed Chief Creative Officer , becoming Versace's third creative leader in less than a year.

article_title: Jigsaw's search for new Design Director and CFO underway
sub_title: Jigsaw has confirmed that its CFO, Steve Thew, and Design Director, Julia Reimann, will be stepping down from their respective roles to pursue new opportunities, with a search for their replacements now underway.
article_content: Jigsaw has confirmed that its CFO, Steve Thew, and Design Director, Julia Reimann, will be stepping down from their respective roles to pursue new opportunities, with a search for their replacements now underway. Both Thew and Reimann will remain with Jigsaw during the recruitment process to ensure a smooth transition of responsibilities, a spokesperson for the brand has confirmed. An exact date of their departures has not been announced and is likely dependent on individual arrangements such as notice periods and the timing of new appointments. Thew has been with Jigsaw for over five years, joining in 2021 from Ballyclare International, a European designer and manufacturer of workwear and protective clothing. Prior to this, he was Chief Commercial Officer at Antler and held senior leadership positions at Boden. He has not yet announced where his next opportunity will take him. Reimann has been in the role of Design Director for over four years, joining Jigsaw from Stine Goya, the Copenhagen-based womenswear brand known for its colourful, bold prints. Prior to this, she held senior leadership roles at Peter Pilotto and Isa Arfen, and worked as a fashion consultant. "We would like to thank Steve and Julia for all they have done whilst at Jigsaw, with both having major roles in helping the business move on from a challenging period," a spokesperson for Jigsaw told TheIndustry.fashion. "We are all very grateful for their hard work and contribution to developing and delivering the turnaround plan that has enabled the business to commit to opening 10 new stores across the UK." Jigsaw has recently strengthened its leadership team with the appointment of Chris Browne as Retail Director , who will oversee the next phase of its bricks-and-mortar expansion. The brand is looking to expand its retail footprint by almost a quarter as it sets its sights on an ambitious 2026, following a strong Christmas trading period and the completion of a strategic turnaround that has returned the British brand to growth. The retailer had first announced its ambitions in February. It currently has 45 standalone stores across the UK, as well as a number of concession stores. With the announced store expansion, it will add another 10 stores to its portfolio this year. This follows Jigsaw's 2025/26 festive trading period, which saw sales increase by 26% year-on-year, reflecting renewed customer engagement across all channels. In-store sales increased by 14%, online sales rose by 34% and concession sales climbed by 46%, signalling broad-based momentum for the heritage retailer. The performance follows a strategic reset initiated in the second quarter of 2025, including a capital injection from Jigsaw’s majority shareholder and the appointment of Tikki Godley as Managing Director. In an exclusive interview with TheIndustry.fashion , Godley outlined the brand's evolving retail strategy, which would focus on digital innovation without compromising the brand’s hallmark quality or the intimacy of its stores. "Digital development has become key for all businesses and is constantly evolving, so it will most definitely be a core focus," she noted. "However, this cannot be to the detriment of our stores, which need to retain their individuality, customer service and loyal customer base. If and when the right opportunities arise, we will always look to expand our store estate." The time for this retail expansion has now come. While the focus right now is on perfecting the brand's UK operations, Godley also noted in her interview that she has her eyes on the global horizon. “North America and the Middle East are huge markets where British brands tend to resonate strongly. With marketplace models making it easier than ever to test and learn, multiple regions can launch within a relatively short time frame,” she added. Tikki Godley will be speaking at TheIndustry.fashion's Fashion Summit, taking place on 15 October 2026.

article_title: Julien Dossena departs Rabanne after 13 years as Creative Director
sub_title: Rabanne, the Puig-owned fashion and fragrance house, has confirmed that Julien Dossena is leaving after 13 years as creative director. The brand said that a successor “will be announced in due course”.
article_content: Rabanne, the Puig-owned fashion and fragrance house, has confirmed that Julien Dossena is leaving after 13 years as Creative Director. The brand said that a successor “will be announced in due course”. Dossena joined Paco Rabanne in early 2013, having trained at La Cambre in Brussels and spent four years as a senior designer at Balenciaga alongside Nicolas Ghesquière. He paused his own label, Atto, to focus on the house. Rabanne said Dossena had “played a defining role in shaping a new era for Rabanne”, adding that under his direction the house had “experienced significant growth and renewed global visibility". "I'm equally grateful to my teams, ateliers and collaborators, whose craft and commitment made the work possible," Dossena added. "This defining creative chapter at the helm of Rabanne will always have a significant resonance to me, both professionally and personally." WWD reported that Rabanne had already been sounding out possible successors, including Olivier Rousteing, who left Balmain in late 2025 after 14 years. The vacancy comes amid ongoing Creative Director turnover across European fashion, with more than a dozen major houses appointing new design leads over the past few years. Puig shortened the name from Paco Rabanne to Rabanne in 2023 as part of a wider push to bring its fashion and fragrance businesses under one banner. It reported €5.042 billion in net revenue for 2025, with 7.8% like-for-like growth and counts Rabanne among its top-10 global fragrance brands. The next creative appointment is expected to play a key role in defining how the house balances its fast-growing fragrance division with its fashion identity going forward.

article_title: Autumn Fair unveils first speakers for new Counter Talks Stage ahead of September show
sub_title: The UK retail marketplace has named experts in visual merchandising, social media, retail crime and licensing as the first confirmed speakers for a practical content programme shaped by research into the pressures facing independent retailers.
article_content: Autumn Fair has announced the first speakers for its new Counter Talks Stage, a free-to-attend talks and workshops programme for independent retailers. The programme was informed by the Voices of Retail 2026 report, produced by Spring & Autumn Fair and wholesale platform Faire, which surveyed 650 independent retailers and more than 2,000 UK consumers. The report highlighted rising retail crime, pressure on margins, shifting consumer behaviour, and the growing need for digital engagement and in-store experience as key challenges for operators. Among the consumer findings, 96% of those surveyed said they want more independent shops on their high street, while 90% said AI has made them more likely to want to view products in person and speak to a real expert. The confirmed line-up covers five areas directly linked to these research findings. John Abbate, Economic Growth Lead for High Streets at Westminster City Council and online visual merchandising tutor at the SDEA, will lead sessions on store design and customer engagement. Abbate brings more than two decades of experience shaping retail environments for brands including Ralph Lauren, Levi’s and Alfred Dunhill. Alison Battisby, founder of Avocado Social, will focus on turning social media into footfall and sales. Battisby has spent more than 15 years working with brands including John Lewis, Tesco and Estée Lauder on digital growth. Andrew Goodacre, CEO of the British Independent Retailers Association (BIRA), and Superintendent Lisa Maslen of the National Business Crime Centre at the City of London Police will appear together in a session on retail crime. The pair will discuss shoplifting, abuse against retail staff and practical steps to protect stores and profitability. Steve Manners, UK Managing Director of Licensing International, will explain how licensing works as a growth tool for retailers of all sizes. Elyse McAvoy, Industry and Trends Expert at Faire, will present consumer insights, buying behaviours,and product trends drawn from the Voices of Retail report and Faire’s wholesale platform data. Matthew Mein, Event Director at Autumn Fair & Glee, said: "What we wanted to create with the Counter Talks Stage was something genuinely practical and commercially useful, a space where retailers can hear directly from experts tackling the challenges they're facing every day and leave with ideas they can immediately apply to their business." Autumn Fair runs 6-9 September 2026 at the NEC Birmingham.

article_title: Quiz Clothing creditors face £16.7m deficit following administration
sub_title: Creditors of Orion Retail Limited are set to be left with an estimated £16.7 million deficit after the fashion retailer went into administration in February 2026.
article_content: Creditors of Orion Retail Limited, part of the Quiz Clothing entity, are set to be left with an estimated £16.7 million deficit after the fashion retailer went into administration in February 2026. The figure, which emerged through statement-of-affairs filings lodged at Companies House in June, gives creditors, including suppliers, landlords and other counterparties, a clearer measure of the losses from the collapse of the Scotland-founded chain. Orion Retail Limited was one of three entities, alongside Tarak International Limited and Zandra Systems Limited, that traded together as Quiz. Interpath had been appointed as the joint administrators for all three entities on 5 February 2026. The company’s statement of affairs, shows that total estimated assets available for creditors are set at £2 million against liabilities exceeding £18.7 million. The filings explained that payments of £306,552 to employees and £731,213 owed to HMRC, were treated as preferential claims and have been settled, leaving limited funds for other creditors. The estimated shortfall for creditors is £16.7 million, while shareholders are not expected to receive any return. Of these, £1.9m are owed to unsecured employee creditors, while £9.8 million are owed to unsecured trade creditors. Secured creditors are also expected to face significant deficits with property and equipment assets realising an estimated value of £20,000, instead of a book value of £2.2 million. Fixed charge holders, meanwhile, are owed an estimated £6 million. When administration began, Quiz had 40 UK stores and seven concessions in the Republic of Ireland, with around 565 staff employed across the business. As of the 20 June, all Quiz stores had closed. The online store ceased trading on the 5 February, with the website stating that "all remaining stock must be cleared" and all sales were final. The administration resulted in 109 redundancies across head office and warehouse roles, with further job losses following as stores have shut. It marked Quiz's second administration in just over a year, after the company collapsed in February 2025 and was subsequently acquired in a pre-pack deal by a subsidiary of its founding Ramzan family. Quiz Clothing concessions operating within New Look and Matalan stores in the UK are not part of the administration process and continue to trade as normal, according to earlier administrator updates. Geoff Jacobs, Managing Director at Interpath and joint administrator, said in May: "We'd once again like to say a huge thank you to Quiz staff who have shown such dedication and professionalism under difficult circumstances."

article_title: In Pictures: H&M partners with WARDROBE.NYC for latest designer collaboration
sub_title: H&M is partnering with the New York-based luxury essentials label, WARDROBE.NYC for its latest designer collaboration.
article_content: H&M is partnering with the New York-based luxury essentials label WARDROBE.NYC for its latest designer collaboration. WARDROBE.NYC was founded by editor and stylist Christine Centenera and designer Josh Goot, with the new collaboration translating the duo's minimalist vision into a "definitive wardrobe - directional and effortlessly wearable in equal measure". The label was founded in 2017 and focuses on "practical urban minimalism", with pieces designed to be timeless yet wearable and created using high-quality materials. Prices at WARDROBE.NYC range from £255 for a classic T-shirt to £2,500 for a Crepe Safari Jacket. The new collaborative collection with H&M draws on the label's archives to present a "tight edit of archetypal urban style". Defined by its sharp tailoring and timeless colour palette, the collection is anchored by core pieces including wool coats, blazers and tailored skirts, complemented by more casual pieces including washed denim, padded bombers and hoodies. Described as a capsule wardrobe, the collection also includes a number of versatile layers that allow for greater wearability. "We wanted to create a capsule for H&M that was true to the wardrobe concept: a timeless and honest statement that was both essential and of the moment," said Goot. "This approach comes from our personal philosophy of dress - this approach has always been a vital part of WARDROBE.NYC, and you can feel it in the H&M collaboration." "What we wanted, above all, was for all these pieces to become staples," Centenera added. She explained that it was about "building the base of a wardrobe and mixing it back in", highlighting that the key goal for the collaboration was always versatility. The collection will launch across the UK in selected stores and online on 6 August 2026.

article_title: Lacoste brings its tennis clubhouse to Selfridges
sub_title: Lacoste is bringing its contemporary tennis clubhouse 'Club Lacoste' to Selfridges London, after it has toured New York, Melbourne, Miami and Roland-Garros.
article_content: Lacoste has unveiled Club Lacoste at Selfridges London, extending the global tour of its contemporary tennis clubhouse after activations in New York, Melbourne, Miami and Roland-Garros. Bringing together heritage, hospitality and contemporary design, the pop-up is meant to offer visitors a "fresh perspective on London’s vibrant tennis season", while showcasing the brand's blend of sport, elegance, and the French art de vivre. The activation is inspired by the brand's founder and tennis champion, René Lacoste, inviting both tennis enthusiasts and "style-conscious" visitors to discover the brand's tennis heritage. Club Lacoste is also meant as a nod to Lacoste's passion for entertaining, with bespoke cocktails, including the “Croc Classic” and “Match Martini”, inspired by the brand's history and heritage and paying tribute to the game of tennis. Some of René Lacoste's sporting achievements and inventions are also on display behind the bar, alongside archival references to the cultural influence that continues to shape the brand today. René Lacoste's tennis journey began at the age of 15 during a trip to England. He then made his Grand Slam debut at the 1922 Wimbledon Championships before securing victory in the Wimbledon finals in both 1925 and 1928, Lacoste's Tennis Heritage Collection is also on display nearby, featuring the brand's classic court codes with a "contemporary edge". Club Lacoste is located upstairs on the Selfridges Menswear floor. It is open to the public from 22 June to 12 July 2026.
